### 230.4 Three things that bound the result, led with

**(1) INJECT is a partial collapse in LEVEL, and a full one in STEP SIZE.** INJECT sits 18.19 pp (+32.08 SE) above `k01` and keeps 0.3442 of the HEAD − `k01` gap; the registered branch counts it as a collapse because `P_INJECT` ≥ 10, and the `INJECT-PARTIAL` stamp is exactly the scorer saying it did not reach `k01`. What the records show (descriptive, from the runs' own `probe.jsonl` and `.out`; `analysis/cvt1_attack_indep.py` [6], [9]):

| arm | shared / complement `beta[0]` pinned from epoch | isolated `beta[1]` (idx 50) pinned from | arm-mean TEST at epoch 9 / 19 / 29 / 39 / 49 / 99 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `k01` | 36.4 / 36.6 / 36.2 | — | 2.1 / 10.8 / 11.9 / 11.8 / 11.9 / 11.9 |
| HEAD | **99.8 / 99.8 / 99.8** (`cpl2` 98.2 / 98.8 / never) | 21.0 / 21.6 / 23.6 | 2.1 / 20.3 / 45.1 / 57.8 / 64.2 / 64.8 |
| MUTE | 40.4 / 40.6 / 40.2 | — | 2.1 / 9.2 / 11.0 / 11.0 / 10.9 / 11.0 |
| DOSE | never continuously (at the clamp on 0.194 / 0.194 / 0.122 of records; last −14.958 / −14.997 / −14.980) | — | 2.1 / 10.2 / 11.9 / 12.0 / 12.0 / 11.9 |
| INJECT | **37.6 / 37.6 / 37.6** | 20.8 / 21.6 / 23.6 (= HEAD's) | 2.1 / **19.9** / **30.0** / 30.0 / 30.1 / 30.1 |

INJECT tracks HEAD to epoch 19 (19.9 vs 20.3) and its level is frozen at 30.0 from epoch 29, as its complement's `beta` falls (arm mean −11.23 at epoch 30 against HEAD's −6.89) and pins at 37.6. That timing is what 227.3's record-level prior said: on HEAD's records the ×691 twin first outvotes the complement's UP votes from about epoch 18. **So the partial level is consistent with a full step-size collapse that simply starts ~18 epochs in, rather than with a weaker vote — but that reading is not a registered statistic and is UNSURE:** a vote that acts from epoch 0 was not run, and nothing here separates "late" from "weaker because it is not 50's". The sentence "a carrier-sized vote from another tensor re-collapses the complement as fully as 50's own" is **not** licensed.

**(2) Removing 50's vote does not rescue, and on MUTE's records the vote does not go away — it moves.** On MUTE's records from epoch 36 every record votes the shared `beta` DOWN, and the largest DOWN voters are other BN scales: `layer4.1.bn1.weight` (47, the twin) 0.20–0.29 of the mean |L| mass, then 44, 41, 38 (every one DOWN on 1.00 of records), with `linear.weight` (UP) at 0.07–0.12 (`k01`: 50 0.61, `linear.weight` 0.12–0.13 UP). The scorer's own descriptive readout agrees: adding 50's term back would flip the sign on only 0.022–0.027 of MUTE's post-epoch-17 records. In HEAD's complement the same BN scales vote DOWN too (47 0.20, 44 0.11) but `linear.weight` holds 0.28 UP and the complement stays free to epoch 99.8. **So "vote removal does not suffice" means: with 50 on the shared step size, the collapse is re-carried by other terms. It does NOT license "50's vote is irrelevant", nor a mechanism for why its own step size matters (UNSURE).** MUTE sits 0.96 pp below `k01` (−1.70 SE, inside the 2.0 NULL bar) and pins ~4 epochs later; both are locations (`FLOOR-READINGS-ARE-BOUNDS`).

**(3) DOSE cannot separate a threshold account from a graded one here.** 227.3 registered DOSE ×0.1 as a threshold test *given* that MUTE rescues. MUTE did not, so every account consistent with MUTE at `k01` predicts DOSE at `k01`, and DOSE landed there (−0.0007 pp). The dose-response question is untested, not answered. (DOSE's shared `beta` never pins continuously and descends more slowly than MUTE's — arm mean −10.49 at epoch 40, −14.48 at 60 — while its TEST is at `k01`'s level from epoch 29; descriptive.)

### 230.5 The attack — an independent parser

`analysis/cvt1_attack_indep.py ../runs_cluster_b analysis/cVT1_voteweight_score.py <score log>` (NEW; imports nothing from the scorer or any repo module, no regex; the 53 tensor names come from the batch's own manifest, not from the scorer's `r18_tensors()`; bars and branch order re-typed from 227.6). **Exit 0, 0 violations.** Run on the Mac against `../runs_cluster_b` and on cluster_b against the ORIGINAL `~/metaopt/runs` with the stage scorer: **the two outputs are byte-identical** (`10930226…`, `cluster_b:~/l230_logs/attack_cvt1.log`).

* **[1]** 15/15 runs: one `.out` each, epochs 0–99 with no duplicate, `RUN_DONE`, 0 tracebacks; the ARGS line carries all 14 fixed HF flags plus the arm's spec, seed and run-name, with no repeated flag; ENV == `cpl2`'s; `PROBE_TENSOR` of the arm's type; `VOTE_W` == the arm's witness. PROVENANCE `SCORER_SHA256` == the scorer file's sha256.
* **[2]–[3]** Every per-run plateau5 and TRAIN5, every arm mean / sd / range, σ in-batch 0.595875, SE 0.567010 and all seven contrasts with TRAIN: **equal to the scorer's printed values digit for digit** (230.3's table is the parser's output). **The CSV `plateau5` of all 15 ingested rows equals the scorer's per-run plateau5** (15 checked, 0 mismatches at 5e−4) — three readers agree.
* **[4]** Branch `STEP-SIZE-NEEDED-VOTE-SUFFICES` and all six re-derived conditional stamps (`DOSE-AT-K01`, `INJECT-PARTIAL`, `MUTE-BELOW-HEAD`, `FLOOR-READINGS-ARE-BOUNDS`, `TRAIN-AGREES`, `SIGMA-PRIOR-FROZEN`) appear in the scorer's FINAL; every bar margin printed (230.3).
* **[5] THE WEIGHTS BIT — the probe-level check, re-derived, and one step further than `G-BITE`.** (a) Per record, per group, with `math.fsum`: `z_agg` == Σ wᵢ `z_tensor`ᵢ and `mom_pre` == Σ wᵢ `m_tensor`ᵢ, worst relative error 1.5e−06 (z) / 9.5e−06 (m) over all 7,500 records; `probe_tensor.json`'s 53 numels equal the manifest's and `block_sizes.json` equals each arm's grouping. (b) **THE APPLIED STEP**, which `G-BITE` does not read: on every record where a group's `beta_pre` is off the clamp and `beta` moved, the step is `−ms·sign(b2·mom_pre + (1−b2)·z_agg)` — the WEIGHTED Lion direction — on **all** of them (181–464 per run). On the records where the weighted and the UNWEIGHTED direction disagree in sign — MUTE 9 / 11 / 10, DOSE 84 / 103 / 113, INJECT 95 / 99 / 96 — **the applied step follows the weighted direction on all and the unweighted on none**; on `k01` and HEAD there are 0 such records. So the weights did not merely appear in a logged sum; they steered the step size.
* **[6]** Beta trajectories and pin epochs per arm, per seed, per group (230.4(1)'s table), plus arm-mean `beta` at epochs 10–100. The pin epochs agree with the scorer's descriptive readout to 0.1 epoch (the parser's clamp test is `≤ −14.999`, the scorer's `≤ −14.9999`).
* **[7]–[8]** The vote in the group that shares the step size, by phase, and its top five voters from epoch 36 (230.4(2)). INJECT's twin holds 0.87–0.89 of its complement's weighted mass from epoch 36, and 0.81–0.83 in epochs 17–36; `k01`'s 50 holds 0.61–0.62. The in-batch ×691 check: on `k01`'s pinned records mean |L₅₀| / mean |L₄₇| is 657.2 / 559.0 / 686.3 (scorer readout), against `cpl2`'s pooled 690.71.
* **[9]** Arm-mean TEST (TRAIN) at epochs 9–99 from the raw `.out` (230.4(1)).

**Deviations, disclosed.** The parser was extended twice after its first full pass, and each time the earlier sections were diffed and printed identically: [8] (top voters) was added after [0]–[7], and [9] (the TEST trajectory) after [0]–[8]. No gated number, branch or stamp changed in any pass.

### 230.6 What this licenses about identity vs magnitude, and what it does not

**Licensed (227.6's registered text for this branch).** On `PlainNet18_c100` at `cpl2`'s cell, over 100 epochs, with K = 691 and one dose: silencing `layer4.1.bn2.weight`'s term while it keeps the shared step size does NOT rescue the scalar collapse, yet a carrier-sized vote cast by a DIFFERENT tensor (its bn1 twin) into HEAD's rescued complement DOES collapse it (by the registered bar). A loud vote is sufficient to collapse; removing the loud vote is not sufficient to rescue while 50 shares the step size. **Magnitude and step-size sharing both act; neither alone is the mechanism.** In the identity-vs-magnitude terms 227.1 posed: **(a)** the rescue is not the removal of 50's vote — it needs 50 on its own step size; **(b)** a vote's collapsing effect does not require the vote to be 50's: a non-carrier's term at the carrier's magnitude collapses the complement's step size. This is the first result in the campaign in which magnitude was varied with identity held fixed, and it is the first in which MAGNITUDE-NOT-SEPARATED is not the whole story.

**Not licensed.**
* **That magnitude ALONE carries the collapse, or that identity is irrelevant.** INJECT keeps 0.3442 of the gap; whether that residue is timing (the ×691 vote turns DOWN only from ~epoch 18) or identity is not separated (230.4(1), UNSURE).
* **That 50's vote is irrelevant,** or why its own step size is needed (230.4(2)).
* **That ×691 is minimal, or record-matched.** One fixed K.
* **Any dose-response or threshold statement.** One dose, and uninformative given MUTE (230.4(3)).
* **Any other network** (ResNet with BN or GN, VGG), **any other cell**, or **anything past 100 epochs** (HEAD's own complement pins at 99.8).
* **Point agreement for MUTE or DOSE** with `k01` (locations; `FLOOR-READINGS-ARE-BOUNDS`), including "MUTE is below `k01`".
* **Any between-batch contrast.** `cpl2`'s levels are orientation only.
* **RULE 11** (one cell).

### 230.8 Marking the 9 intervention rows — `results/CORPUS-EXCLUSIONS.tsv`

**The choice, and why it is the least invasive.** Three routes were weighed. (i) A new CSV column: forbidden (schema). (ii) Populating an existing column (e.g. `hier`, or `provenance`) for these rows: every such column already has a meaning that pre-existing readers filter on (`hier` enters the 15-key cell tuple, so a non-empty value would move these rows into a NEW cell by accident of an unrelated column's semantics), and `aggregate.py` — unedited, registered — would overwrite it on the next re-aggregation, so the mark would silently vanish; making it persist would require editing `aggregate.py`. (iii) **A separate, machine-readable exclusion list keyed on `(run, job_id)`**, versioned beside the corpus: no schema change, no registered file edited, survives every re-aggregation, and can be checked against the raw witness lines. (iii) was implemented.

* **`results/CORPUS-EXCLUSIONS.tsv`** (NEW, sha `31105e32…`): a `#`-commented header stating the rule, then one TSV row per excluded run — `run, job_id, batch, arm, looks_like, intervention, witness, registered_at, reason` — for `cvt1-{MUTE,DOSE,INJECT}-s{78,79,80}` (job ids 5019106/7/8, 5019111/2/3, 5019116/7/8). `looks_like` names the plain arm whose cell key the row carries; `witness` is the run's own `VOTE_W:` line verbatim. `cvt1-k01-*` and `cvt1-HEAD-*` print `VOTE_W: off`, are ordinary measurements of their cells, and are **not** listed.
* **`analysis/corpus_exclusions.py`** (NEW, sha `5d7694ad…`, stdlib only): `load()`, `keys()`, `is_excluded(row)`, `filter_rows(rows)` for any reader, and `--check [--runs <dirs>]`, which verifies (a) every listed key is in the CSV exactly once and no key is listed twice, (b) each listed run's raw `.out` carries exactly its listed witness, and (c) **every unlisted `.out` of a listed batch prints `VOTE_W: off`, so the list is complete for that batch.** Run on the Mac (`../runs ../runs_cluster_b`) and on cluster_b (`~/metaopt/runs`, Python 3.10.4): **`VERDICT: PASS`, exit 0** — 9 listed runs carry their line, 6 unlisted `cvt1` runs print `off`.
* **How a future noise-floor derivation excludes them.** Drop every `(run, job_id)` in the list before grouping by cell: `rows = filter_rows(csv.DictReader(open("results/all_runs.csv")))`. `--check` prints the demonstration, with 227.6's own definitions re-typed (15-key cells; complete, unsuperseded, std cell):

| reader | `SIGMA_PLAIN` (df, cells) | `SIGMA_R18ALL` (df) |
|---|---|---|
| as 227 registered it (every `cvt1-` row dropped) | **0.395457** (23, 7) = 227.6's 0.39545713… | **0.694443** (209) = 227.6's |
| **future reader: the 9 listed rows dropped, `cvt1` k01/HEAD kept** | 0.462816 (29, 7) | 0.694443 (209) |
| naive: nothing dropped (the trap) | **7.895507** (38, 7) | 0.694443 (209) |

  The naive PlainNet floor is ×20 the registered one — INJECT's 30 pp rows pool into HEAD's 64 pp cell — which is the size of the error the list prevents. The rise to 0.4628 under the correct reader is `cvt1`'s legitimate `k01` and HEAD replicates joining `cpl1`/`cpl2`'s cells.
* **The rule, stated where registrations will read it.** The TSV's own header carries the rule and names the helper; any future batch whose design the ARGS line cannot carry appends its rows in the same commit as its ingest. **Owed, not done here:** no registered checklist file exists in the repo to point at the list (the pre-submission checklist lives in CORRECTIONS 125); the next registration that derives a corpus floor should call `filter_rows` and say so in its registration entry.
* **Nothing else moves.** `c73_mastertable_check.py` exit 0 (230.9); `args_repair.py` dry run afterwards "untouched rows: 2971"; `c98b_reproduce.py` exit 0 with 226.8's verdict line; the registered `cVT1` scorer's output is unchanged by the ingest.

### 231.6 Is the GroupNorm rescue a regime or a delayed collapse — and what it does not license

**Licensed (228.6's registered text for this branch, with the pin stamp that decides which sentence).** On `ResNet18_gn_c100` at `cgn2`'s cell, isolating {50, 53, 59} from the shared step size keeps a rescue of **+48.5 pp over the scalar arm at 430 epochs, 1.22 × its in-run 100-epoch size**, and the rescued level **survives the complement's freeze**: the complement's step size pins at ~225 and the level is flat for the following ~190 epochs. **It is a regime, not a delayed collapse** — the third network on which the isolation rescue outlives its complement's pin (`cvh1` VGG, RHO 1.0001; `ciso2` ResNet BN, RHO 0.9977, a number measured but whose verdict its superseded exact-clamp gate voided; here RHO 1.2235, larger because GN's arms were still rising at 100 epochs). The registered worry of 228.2 — a GN complement that never pins in 430 epochs — did not happen; the tail-linear extrapolation from `cgn2`'s records, the EARLY end of 228.2's model range (286.4–335.5), was itself later than every measured pin here (215.2–238.4) — by 48 to 120 epochs across the two ranges (different seeds, descriptive). And 50 alone ends at 0.81 of the gap: on GN, ONE's "partial" rescue at 100 epochs was mostly slowness.

**Not licensed.**
* **That the pin froze the level.** TEST stopped moving at ~162, 53–76 epochs before the pin, while TRAIN climbed (231.4(1)); the mechanism of that plateau is UNSURE.
* **That isolation recovers the layerwise ceiling on GN.** At 430 ISO is 3.02 pp below `kL` and ONE 9.77 pp below (231.4(2)); 225's "ISO sits above `kL`" was a 100-epoch transient.
* **Persistence past 430 epochs,** or the absence of a decay slower than `READ_BAR` (1.56 pp) over ~190 post-pin epochs.
* **Identity vs magnitude** (`MAGNITUDE-NOT-SEPARATED`): nothing here intervenes on the vote; `cvt1`'s PlainNet result does not transfer by assertion.
* **`DELTA_ID` at 430** (`NO-IN-BATCH-CTL`): the matched-set control was not re-run, so "the carriers, not any three tensors" is a 100-epoch statement (`cgn2`).
* **Any other normaliser** (GN(32) also changes per-channel invariance; LayerNorm, GN(C), none untested), **network or cell**; **any between-batch contrast** (`cgn2`'s levels are orientation only); **RULE 11**.

## 232. TRACK A — **`cvt3` REGISTERED AND DRY-RUN: DOES SILENCING THE WHOLE DOWN COALITION RESCUE WITHOUT AN OWN STEP SIZE?  230.4(2) LEFT THIS OPEN: cvt1's MUTE FAILED, BUT ON ITS RECORDS THE DOWN VOTE MOVED TO OTHER BN SCALES.  ON `PlainNet18_c100` AT cvt1's CELL, FROM cvt1's UNCHANGED TREE, NO NEW HARNESS CODE: 5 ARMS × SEEDS {84, 85, 86} = 15 JOBS, 100 EPOCHS — k01; HEAD (byte-identical, positive control); MUTE50 (cvt1's MUTE, replicated); MUTEDOWN (50 + THE DOWN COALITION, 21 WEIGHTS AT 0, ONE SHARED STEP SIZE); MUTECTL (50 + A COUNT- AND CLASS-MATCHED NON-DOWN SET, 21 WEIGHTS AT 0).  BOTH SETS ARE FIXED BY RULES WRITTEN HERE AND COMPUTED MECHANICALLY FROM cvt1 MUTE's 960 POST-EPOCH-36 RECORDS: RULE C (DOWN ON ≥ 0.90 OF RECORDS, RANKED BY VOTE SHARE, CUMULATIVE CUT 1.00) → 20 TENSORS (15 BN SCALES + 5 CONVS, 0.8280 OF THE MASS); RULE K (DOWN ON ≤ 0.50, SAME MODULE CLASS, NEAREST NUMEL) → 20 TENSORS (15 BN BIASES OF THE SAME MODULES + 5 SMALLER CONVS, 0.0276 OF THE MASS — MATCHED ON COUNT AND CLASS, NOT ON MASS; A MASS-MATCHED NON-DOWN SET DOES NOT EXIST ON THIS NET).  PRIMARY `P_COAL` = MUTEDOWN − MUTECTL, UNBOUNDED.  FIVE ACCOUNTS WITH EVERY ARM's PREDICTED LEVEL — COALITION, COALITION-PARTIAL, OWN-STEP-NECESSARY, NONSPECIFIC — PLUS THE NEW FAILURE MODE `UP-RUNAWAY` (NO DOWN VOTE LEFT → beta RUNS TO THE CLAMP CEILING OR BLOWS UP; NOT A RESCUE AT ANY LEVEL), DETECTED FROM EACH RUN's OWN beta TRAJECTORY BY `G-RUNAWAY` AND STAMPED BEFORE ANY BRANCH IS READ; THE BROKEN-PATCH NULL IS SEPARATED BY `G-BITE` AND A NEW SET-LEVEL HALF `G-BITE-SET`.  EVERY BRANCH STATES WHAT IT DOES TO 230's HEADLINE.  THE NOISE FLOOR IS READ THROUGH `corpus_exclusions.filter_rows` (OPERATIONS 36): SIGMA_PLAIN 0.4628 FILTERED vs 7.8955 NAIVE; THE PRIOR IS 0.694443.  THE EXACT VOTE_W STRINGS ARE PROVED INERT (WEIGHT 1, BITWISE) AND BITING (WEIGHT 0, INCLUDING THE SET LEVEL) ON A REAL 300-STEP GPU RUN: 38 PASS / 0 FAIL.  SCORER SELFTEST 141 / 0 / 0 ON THE MAC AND ON cluster_b; DRY RUN EXIT 0, 0 GUARD FAILURES, 15 LINES READ.  ≈10.4 GPU-h EXPECTED, HARD BOUND 30.**  Every bar is a frozen literal (O2).  **`cluster_a` NOT CONTACTED.**  THIS ENTRY TOOK NUMBER **232** (pre-assigned); `cvt2` holds 233, bookkeeping 234.

### 232.1 Question

cvt1 (230) returned `STEP-SIZE-NEEDED-VOTE-SUFFICES`. Its half (a) reads: **the rescue needs `layer4.1.bn2.weight` (idx 50) on its own step size** — silencing 50's term while it shares the step size (MUTE) left the arm at `k01` (10.99 vs 11.95).

230.4(2) bounded that: on MUTE's own records the DOWN vote did not disappear, it **moved**. From epoch 36 every record votes the shared beta DOWN, carried by 47 (0.20–0.29 of the mass), 44, 41, 38 — every one DOWN on 1.00 of records. So MUTE may have failed only because the rest of the DOWN coalition re-carried the collapse. If so, "the own step size is needed" is an artefact of silencing one voter.

`cvt3` silences the whole coalition, and a matched control, while every tensor keeps the ONE shared step size.

### 232.2 Design

* **Cell.** cvt1's exactly: CIFAR-100, `PlainNet18_c100` (53 tensors, 11,046,308 params), SGDm (0.99, wd 0.1) + Lion meta (0.99, b2 0.9, wd 0), ms 1e-3, alpha0 1e-6, 100 ep, batch 100, `AUGMENT=1`, `BETA_CLIP=-15:-2.3026`, `PROBE=100`, `PROBE_TENSOR=1`. The exports are cvt1's byte for byte, plus each arm's `VOTE_W`.
* **No new harness code.** The tree is `$WS/harness_cvt1/cifar10` (HF.py `3f2b98e1…`, build_network `e65e6773…`), the runner `$WS/jobs/run_cifar_cvt1.sh` (`d389e8a5…`), both unchanged; `bin/cVT1_stage_harness.sh` (verify mode, unedited) re-verifies them at every launcher pass. `PATCH_VOTEWEIGHT` already parses multi-item `name:w/name:w`; only the strings are new.
* **ONE submission, 15 jobs = 5 arms × seeds {84, 85, 86}** (pre-assigned; zero corpus rows and zero `.out` ARGS lines carry them; 0 `cvt3-` jobs in `sacct`).

| arm | `--stepsize-groups` | `VOTE_W` | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| k01 | `scalar` | unset | the floor anchor |
| HEAD | `sets:1-49,51-53/layer4.1.bn2.weight` | unset | positive control, byte-identical to cvt1's and cpl2's HEAD (selftest B reads both scorers) |
| **MUTE50** | `scalar` | `layer4.1.bn2.weight:0` | cvt1's MUTE, replicated (string and witness byte-identical) |
| **MUTEDOWN** | `scalar` | {50} ∪ C, 21 names `:0` | silences 50 AND the DOWN coalition; every tensor shares one step size |
| **MUTECTL** | `scalar` | {50} ∪ K, 21 names `:0` | silences 50 AND a count/class-matched NON-DOWN set |

* **PRIMARY** `P_COAL` = MUTEDOWN − MUTECTL (in batch; plateau5 from each run's own `.out`; TRAIN beside it). **KEY** `D_DOWN` = MUTEDOWN − k01, `D_CTL` = MUTECTL − k01, `D_HEAD` = HEAD − k01, `D_MUTE50` = MUTE50 − k01, `G_DOWN` = HEAD − MUTEDOWN.
* **Arm names carry no hyphen** (`MUTE50`, `MUTEDOWN`, `MUTECTL`), so every `-`-splitting reader (RULE 20 script, ENV audit, `corpus_exclusions --check`, the landing parser) parses them.

### 232.3 The two sets — rules written here, computed mechanically (`analysis/cvt3_registration_derivations.py`, NEW)

**The rules** (also in the derivation's docstring and printed by it; the scorer carries the output as literals and its selftest re-runs the rules on the host's cvt1 records and requires equality):

* **Records.** cvt1 MUTE (`VOTE_W=layer4.1.bn2.weight:0`), seeds 78/79/80, every probe record with epoch ≥ 36.0 (after `k01`'s pin at 36.2–36.6 and MUTE's own at 40.2–40.6): 320 per seed, **960 pooled**.
* **Vote.** L_i = w_i (b2·m_i + (1−b2)·z_i), with MUTE's weights (w_50 = 0). Lion moves beta by −ms·sign(Σ L_i), so a tensor votes **DOWN** on a record iff L_i > 0. share_i = |L_i| / Σ_j |L_j| per record.
* **RULE C (the DOWN coalition).** Eligible iff i ≠ 50 and DOWN on ≥ **0.90** of the 960 pooled records. Ranked by pooled mean share, descending (ties: lower index). **Cumulative mass cut 1.00: every eligible tensor is kept.** Why not 0.90 or 0.95: MUTE failed because the voters that were LEFT re-carried the vote; a cut would rebuild that trap by design. (A 0.90 cut would keep 12 of 20, a 0.95 cut 15 — printed, descriptive.)
* **RULE K (the NON-DOWN control).** Pool: i ≠ 50, not in C, DOWN on ≤ **0.50** of records. For each member c of C in rank order, the unused pool tensor of the **same module class** (manifest column 4) minimising |ln(numel_c / numel_i)|; ties → smallest |i − c|, then the lower index. If any member finds no candidate, the rule fails loudly.
* **VOTE_W strings** list items in ascending index, `<name>:0` joined by `/`; the patch prints its witness items in the same order.

**The result** (output sha on cluster_b `72f15ed1…`; on the Mac one line differs, see 232.9):

| rank | C (DOWN share, DOWN frac) | ↔ | K (share, DOWN frac) | numel C / K |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 47 `layer4.1.bn1.weight` (0.2467, 1.000) | | 48 `layer4.1.bn1.bias` (0.0003, 0.000) | 512 / 512 |
| 2 | 44 `layer4.0.bn2.weight` (0.1154, 1.000) | | 45 `layer4.0.bn2.bias` (0.0001, 0.000) | 512 / 512 |

| 13 | 40 `layer4.0.conv1.weight` (0.0153, 1.000) | | 19 `layer2.0.conv2.weight` (0.0056, 0.419) | ×8 |

* **COALITION C** (rank order) = 47 44 41 38 35 32 29 26 23 20 17 14 40 46 43 11 37 8 5 49: 15 BatchNorm2d + 5 Conv2d, **0.827994** of the mean |L| mass. **CONTROL K** (pair order) = 48 45 42 39 36 33 30 27 24 21 18 15 19 13 10 12 7 9 6 4: 15 BatchNorm2d + 5 Conv2d, **0.027615** of the mass.
* **Near the eligibility bar, NOT eligible:** 2 `bn1.weight` 0.8417, 34 `layer3.1.conv1.weight` 0.8396. Neither C nor pool (0.50 < DOWN < 0.90): 2, 16, 22, 25, 28, 31, 34 — these stay in every arm's sum.
* **What K is and is not (disclosed, not hidden).** Every BN pair is (scale, bias) of ONE module, numel-equal (15/15). The conv pairs are ×8–×64 smaller (C's convs 8,847,360 params vs K's 294,912): every conv with ≥ 294,912 params votes DOWN on ≥ 0.70 of records, so none is in the pool. **K holds 1/30 of C's mass, and every non-C tensor together holds only 0.172: a mass-matched NON-DOWN control does not exist on this net.** K controls for "silencing 20 more tensors of these classes (with 50)", not for "removing the same amount of vote".
* **The same rule on MUTE's decline records (epochs 17–36) instead**, descriptive: 14 tensors, all inside C (C adds 5, 14, 40, 43, 46, 49). No tensor the decline rule picks is missing from C.

**Record-level prior (S5; descriptive, NON-GATING; a counterfactual on cvt1's trajectories, NOT a prediction of cvt3's).** Fraction of group-0 records that would vote UP (Σ L < 0) with {50} ∪ C, and with {50} ∪ K, silenced:

| cvt1 records | epochs 0–17 (as run: UP on all) | 17–36 | 36–100 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `k01` s78/79/80 | UP-if-C 0.96–1.00; UP-if-K 1.00 | UP-if-C 1.000; UP-if-K 1.000 | UP-if-C 1.000; UP-if-K 1.000 |
| MUTE s78/79/80 | UP-if-C 0.96–1.00 | UP-if-C 0.853 / 0.253 / 0.832; UP-if-K 0.17 / 0.14 / 0.17 | UP-if-C **1.000 / 0.163 / 1.000**; UP-if-K 0.000 |
| HEAD (complement) | UP-if-C 0.96–1.00 | UP-if-C 0.54–0.58; UP-if-K 0.84–0.90 | UP-if-C **1.000**; UP-if-K 0.09–0.12 |

* Two readings, both UNSURE. (i) On `k01`'s and HEAD's trajectories, silencing C leaves an UP-voting sum on every post-17 record, with nothing left to brake it: **UP-RUNAWAY is a live outcome, not a formality.** (ii) On MUTE s79 the mixed convs (28, 31, 34, 16, 22, 25 — DOWN on 1.00 of that seed's records, not eligible pooled) keep the sum DOWN on 0.84 of post-36 records: the coalition as ruled may be re-carried on some seeds. On every cvt1 arm the silence of K alone changes the post-36 sign of MUTE's sum on 0 records.
* **No time gate.** Every weight is 0 from step 0; the sets were chosen on post-epoch-36 records. Dose and onset stay confounded exactly as in cvt1 (230.4(1)). In epochs 0–17 silencing C leaves the as-run UP vote UP on 0.96–1.00 of records, so the early rise is not predicted to change sign; nothing more is claimed.

### 232.5 Gates, branches, and what each does to 230's headline — `decide()`, first match wins; frozen bars

**Harness gates (→ `HARNESS-UNSOUND`, rc 1).** `G-ARGS` (every run's own single ARGS line: its spec, net, cell, 15 fixed HF flags, seed, run-name); `G-ENV` (one distinct ENV line == cvt1's/cpl2's; one `PROBE_TENSOR: on every=100 type=<arm's> tensors=53`); **`G-VOTEW`** (exactly one `VOTE_W` line == the arm's witness; MUTEDOWN's is 1,086 characters, MUTECTL's 1,054); `G-STRUCT` (manifest byte-identical to the scorer's, 6,626 bytes, with `COALITION_RANKED` / `CONTROL_PAIRED` lines); `G-PROV` (MODE submit; build_network `e65e6773…`; HF `3f2b98e1…`; **RUNNER `d389e8a5…`**; SCORER == the file); `G-FLOOR`/`G-CEIL` (max arm mean in 15–90).

**`G-BITE` + `G-BITE-SET` (→ `PATCH-NOT-VERIFIED`, rc 1; before any level).** From `runs/cvt3/probe_cvt3-<arm>-s<seed>/probe.jsonl`: 500 parseable records; on every FINITE record z_agg == Σ w_i z_tensor_i and mom_pre == Σ w_i m_tensor_i (rel 1e-4 of Σ|term|); intervened runs ≥ 50 records where weighted and unweighted sums differ by > 1e-2, the unweighted matching none. **NEW, `G-BITE-SET`** (MUTEDOWN, MUTECTL): ≥ 50 records where the registered set and the **50-only** set differ by > 1e-2, the 50-only sum matching none; and the OTHER arm's set matches no record. A patch that bit only on its first item, a swapped set, or a weight on a control arm cannot reach a level. On cvt1's own records the set difference exceeds 1e-2 on 373–499 of 500 records per run for C and K alike, so the half is informative. Individual BN-bias items (≤ 1e-4 of Σ|z| each) are below float32 resolution one by one: the bite is proved at the SET level, and the witness proves every item was parsed. **Non-finite records are counted, not failed** — a blow-up is `G-RUNAWAY`'s evidence, not a patch failure.

**`G-RUNAWAY` (stamped BEFORE any branch; feeds `decide()` as per-arm seed counts).** From each run's own probe `beta[0]`: a record is at the ceiling iff beta[0] ≥ −2.3026 − 0.01 (the clamp's upper end; `HF.step` clamps after every meta update); **a seed runs away iff ≥ 0.10 of its epoch-≥-17 records are at the ceiling, or any record carries a non-finite beta[0]** (only a large step size can blow up the net); **an arm runs away iff ≥ 2 of 3 seeds do.** `DRIFT` (stamp only): beta[0] ≥ −4.0 on ≥ 0.10 of those records on ≥ 2 seeds. Premise, re-checked by the selftest on the host's cvt1 records: **all 15 cvt1 runs: 0 runaway, 0 drift, maximum beta[0] −4.342** (MUTE s79).

**Branches** (after `INCOMPLETE` / `HARNESS-UNSOUND` / `PATCH-NOT-VERIFIED`):

| order | condition | branch | what it does to 230's half (a), "the rescue needs 50 on its own step size" |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | MUTEDOWN runs away on ≥ 2 seeds | **`UP-RUNAWAY`** | **Neither strengthened nor rescinded; it stands, untested by this design.** Silencing every consistent DOWN voter removes the brake: the coalition is what holds the shared step size down, but the intervention replaced the collapse by a different failure, so it cannot say whether the silence rescues. MUTEDOWN's level is printed, never quoted as a rescue. |
| 2 | exactly 1 seed | `UNRESOLVED-RUNAWAY-SPLIT` | none (bimodal, reported not averaged) |
| 3 | any OTHER arm runs away on ≥ 1 seed | `CONTROL-RUNAWAY` | none (unregistered; stop) |
| 4–6 | seed range > 5 / k01 > 20 / D_HEAD < 20 | `UNRESOLVED-DIVERGED` / `SCALAR-NOT-COLLAPSED` / `POSITIVE-CONTROL-FAILED` | none |
| 7 | D_MUTE50 ≥ 10 | `MUTE50-RESCUES` | **put IN QUESTION** by a between-batch disagreement (cvt1's MUTE did not replicate), not rescinded; stop |
| 8 | D_DOWN < −2 without a runaway | `MUTEDOWN-BELOW-K01` | none (unregistered; stop) |
| 9 | D_CTL ≥ 10 and P_COAL ≥ 10 | `COALITION-OVER-NONSPECIFIC` | **rescinded as worded**; a coalition-specific part sits on a nonspecific one |
| 10 | D_CTL ≥ 10 otherwise | **`NONSPECIFIC`** | **rescinded as worded** (a vote intervention with no own step size rescued), but NOT attributable to the coalition; mechanism UNSURE |
| 11 | 2 < D_CTL < 10 | `CONTROL-WEAK` | neither |
| 12 | D_CTL ≤ 2, D_DOWN ≥ 10, HEAD − MUTEDOWN ≤ 5 | **`COALITION`** | **RESCOPED**: the own step size is NOT needed once the whole DOWN coalition is silent; 230(a) holds only against a vote removal that leaves other DOWN voters in the sum |
| 13 | D_CTL ≤ 2, D_DOWN ≥ 10, HEAD − MUTEDOWN > 5 | **`COALITION-PARTIAL`** | **WEAKENED**: vote removal carries part of the rescue |
| 14 | D_CTL ≤ 2, D_DOWN ≤ 2 | **`OWN-STEP-NECESSARY`** | **STRENGTHENED**: survives 230.4(2)'s re-carriage objection at the coalition level. Not licensed: that no other silenced set rescues (~0.17 of the mass still votes) or why |
| 15 | D_CTL ≤ 2, 2 < D_DOWN < 10 | `DOWN-WEAK` | neither |

* **Frozen bars (O2).** GAP_MIN 20.0, K01_MAX 20.0, RESCUE 10.0 (17.64 SE), NULL 2.0 (3.53 SE), MATCH 5.0 (8.82 SE), DIVERGED 5.0, FLOOR_MIN 15.0, CEIL_MAX 90.0; G-BITE: BITE_TOL 1e-4, INFORM 1e-2, MIN_INFORMATIVE 50, N_RECORDS 500; G-RUNAWAY: ceiling −2.3026, tolerance 0.01, from epoch 17, fraction 0.10, ≥ 2 seeds; DRIFT −4.0.
* **Stamps.** Always: `HARNESS-CLEAN`, `PATCH-BITES`, `SETS-FROM-CVT1-MUTE`, `CTL-COUNT-CLASS-NOT-MASS`, `NO-TIME-GATE`, `ONE-NETWORK-PLAINNET`, `HORIZON-100-ONLY`, `SIGMA-PRIOR-FROZEN`/`-INBATCH`. Conditional: `RUNAWAY-<arm>-<n>of3`, `NONFINITE-<arm>`, `DRIFT-MUTEDOWN`, `POSITIVE-CONTROL-REPRODUCES`, `MUTE50-AT-K01`/`-WEAK`, `DOWN-ABOVE-HEAD`, `CTL-BELOW-K01`, `FLOOR-READINGS-ARE-BOUNDS`, `TRAIN-AGREES`/`-DISAGREES`.
* **After FINAL, descriptive and unable to move it:** per-arm beta trajectories and pin epochs; on MUTE50 / MUTEDOWN / MUTECTL records from epoch 36, the sum's DOWN fraction and the top six UNSILENCED voters (who re-carries, if anyone).

### 232.9 Deviations and limits, disclosed

* **One printed digit differs between hosts.** The derivation prints `SIGMA_PLAIN` via `repr`: 0.46281639069317043 on the Mac (Python 3.14) and 0.4628163906931704 on cluster_b (3.10.4) — `sum()` of floats became compensated in 3.12, so the last ulp differs. Every other line is identical. The scorer's check is to 1e-12, and the prior (`SIGMA_R18ALL`) is identical on both.
* **The stage holds more than this registration.** `~/stage_cvt3` was rsync'd from the shared working copy, which also held Track B's untracked `cvt2` files (not staged by this track into any guard, not committed here). The launcher and scorer read none of them; at launch the 13 files guard 1b names are compared with `git show HEAD:<path>`.
* **K is not mass-matched** and **the silence has no time gate** (232.3). **One eligibility bar (0.90), one cut (1.00), one record window (epoch ≥ 36)** — which coalition members are necessary is not tested.
* **The live shared harness is untouched.** `~/l232_hashes.sh` (read-only) wrote `~/l232_logs/live_hashes_before.txt` (47 lines, `de9a8f04…`: the live cifar10 tree, cvt1's and cpl1's trees, `run_cifar.sh`, `run_cifar_cvt1.sh`, `run_cifar_cpl1.sh`, cvt1's STAGE-MANIFEST); it is re-taken after launch.

### 233.1 Question (from 227 + 230)

### 233.3 The ladder, derived from `cvt1`'s records (`analysis/cvt2_registration_derivations.py`, NEW; output `1405f3a7…`, **byte-identical on the Mac and on cluster_b**)

`L_i = b2·m_i + (1−b2)·z_i` per tensor; DOWN = the group's Lion direction sum > 0.

* **E1, the brief's currency (the twin's share of the complement's |L| mass).** On INJECT's records, epochs 17–36, pooled: share at 691 = 0.81–0.83 (as 230.5[7]); inverted exactly, **K(share 0.50) = 116.8, K(0.63) = 212.5** (per seed 110–129 / 201–234). The brief's 152 / 258 were a closed-form estimate of the same quantities. On HEAD's own (unintervened) records the same inversion gives 15.2 / 33.6. E2: idx 50 holds 0.614–0.623 of `k01`'s mass from epoch 17 (the 0.5–0.63 reference).
* **But Lion moves beta by the SIGN of the sum, not by shares.** Two record-level counterfactuals bracket the knee:
  * **E3, initiation (HEAD's trajectory).** The fraction of HEAD's epoch-18–36 complement records the twin at K turns DOWN: K 1: 0.57 / 0.67 / 0.71 (HEAD itself); K 2: 0.88–0.94; K 5: 0.96 / 0.99 / 0.98; K ≥ 10: 0.99–1.00. **`K_INIT` = 5** (smallest probe K ≥ 0.95 on every seed).
  * **E5, sustain (INJECT's own collapsed trajectory).** From epoch 20, on **every** INJECT record the other 51 terms' net vote is UP and the twin's DOWN; the record stays DOWN only if K > −rest/L₄₇. Median over epoch ≥ 38 records **85.28 / 99.78 / 84.41**, max over every record from epoch 20 **117.78**. At K ≤ 50 every such record would flip back UP; at K = 152 none does.
* **E6, the rungs.** 13 and 33 = `K_INIT`·(84.41/5)^(1/3), ^(2/3) = 12.83, 32.90 (the initiate-but-not-sustain interval split in three equal log parts). **152 is retained** (1.29 × the largest K_SUSTAIN: it holds on every collapsed record). **691** replicates `cvt1`. **2000** is the brief's top dose. **258 is DROPPED**: at 2.19 × the largest K_SUSTAIN it is, like 152 and 691, above the sustain knee on every record, so it carries no shape information 152 lacks, and its GPU-h went to the two sub-knee rungs. The brief's share-based rungs (117, 213) are above the knee too; this is the deviation from the brief, taken by derivation and stated here.
* **Onset is nearly fixed; dose and onset are confounded — disclosed.** On HEAD's records no epoch-0–14 record has an UP-voting complement and a DOWN-voting twin (0/70 per seed; 1–2 of 10 in 14–16), so no K can turn the complement DOWN before ~epoch 15. The epoch from which the twin DOMINATES HEAD's complement (|K·L₄₇| > |net of the rest| with the total's sign, on ≥ 0.8 of the next 25 records) moves only 19.4 (K 10) → 17.6 (50) → 16.8 (152) → 16.6 (691) → **16.4 (2000)** → 15.4 (30,000). The same definition on `cvt1`'s own records: INJECT 16.8 / 16.6 / 16.8; `k01`'s idx 50 16.0 ×3. **So the ladder varies dose, cannot move onset by more than ~3 epochs, and — with no time gate — cannot separate "late" from "not 50's".** Every run's DOM epoch is printed after FINAL beside its K (descriptive).
* **What the derivation predicts, as a prior (not a statistic):** K152 = K691 = K2000 by sign saturation; K13, K33 start the collapse but cannot hold it. That is the `SIGN-SAT-*` accounts below; the others are registered against it.

### 233.6 Gates, branches and what each licenses — `decide()`, first match wins; frozen bars

* **Harness gates (→ `HARNESS-UNSOUND`, rc 1):** `G-ARGS`, `G-ENV` (one ENV line == `cvt1`'s == `cpl2`'s; one PROBE_TENSOR line of the arm's type), **`G-VOTEW`** (one `VOTE_W` line == the arm's witness), `G-STRUCT`, `G-PROV` (MODE submit, POST_SHA, HF_POST_SHA, SCORER_SHA256), `G-FLOOR`/`G-CEIL` (15 / 90).
* **`G-BITE` (→ `PATCH-NOT-VERIFIED`, rc 1, before any branch):** 500 parseable records per run; per group z_agg == Σ wᵢ z_tensorᵢ and mom_pre == Σ wᵢ m_tensorᵢ (rel 1e−4 of Σ|wᵢ·termᵢ|); every ladder run ≥ 50 informative records and on none does the unweighted sum match. A run carrying the WRONG K (K2000 at ×691) fails here (selftest E).
* **Branches:** `UNRESOLVED-DIVERGED` (a seed range > 5) → `SCALAR-NOT-COLLAPSED` (k01 > 20) → `POSITIVE-CONTROL-FAILED` (HEAD − k01 < 20) → **`REPLICATE-FAILED`** (HEAD − K691 < SHAPE_GAP 15) → `LADDER-ABOVE-HEAD` (a rung > HEAD + 5; unregistered, stop) → **`NON-MONOTONE`** (along HEAD, 13, 33, 152, 691, 2000 a level rises > 5; unregistered, stop). Then **SHAPE** from K13 / K33 / K152: AT-HEAD (HEAD − L ≤ 5), AT-PLATEAU (|L − K691| ≤ 5), else BETWEEN — any BETWEEN → **`GRADED`**; all AT-PLATEAU → **`KNEE-BELOW-LADDER`**; otherwise **`THRESHOLD`** with `KNEE-IN-(a,b]`. And **TOP** = K691 − K2000: |TOP| ≤ 5 → **`TOP-FLAT`**; ≥ 10 → **`TOP-DROPS`**; between → `TOP-ATTENUATED`. `FINAL: <SHAPE> | <TOP> | stamps`.
* **Licences (registered text in the scorer).** `THRESHOLD`: a single switch between the bracketing rungs; not its location finer than the rungs, nor a mechanism. `GRADED`: that dose re-collapses partially; no functional form. `KNEE-BELOW-LADDER`: shape unresolved. **`TOP-FLAT` licenses "the 0.34 residue is not removed by dose above 691" — NOT "it belongs to HEAD's isolated tensor" as distinct from the twin's own-sign onset (both are dose-independent; no time gate).** `TOP-DROPS`: part of the residue is dose-sensitive above 691, with any onset shift bought by the larger K inside "dose" (the DOM readout reports it).
* **Frozen bars (O2).** GAP_MIN 20.0, K01_MAX 20.0, **SHAPE_GAP 15.0** (26.45 SE; `cvt1` 34.65), MATCH 5.0 (8.82 SE), COLLAPSE 10.0 (17.64 SE), NULL 2.0, DIVERGED 5.0, FLOOR_MIN 15.0, CEIL_MAX 90.0; G-BITE: BITE_TOL 1e−4, INFORM 1e−2, MIN_INFORMATIVE 50, N_RECORDS 500; DOM (descriptive) 25 records at 0.8.
* **Noise floor — read THROUGH `corpus_exclusions.filter_rows` (OPERATIONS §36).** On the 2,983-row corpus (`1aa245d6…`) with `CORPUS-EXCLUSIONS.tsv` (`31105e32…`) dropping `cvt1`'s 9 listed rows: `SIGMA_R18ALL` **0.694442846939599** (df 209); `SIGMA_PLAIN` **0.46281639069317043** (df 29, 7 cells: `cpl1` + `cpl2` + `cvt1` k01/HEAD). **Unfiltered, SIGMA_PLAIN would read 7.895507 (df 38)** — the trap; selftest C re-derives both frozen literals through `filter_rows` and shows the unfiltered value is not the literal. `SIGMA_PRIOR` = max = 0.694443 (unchanged by the filter); `SE_PRIOR` 0.567010. The scorer's only corpus reader, `read_corpus()`, calls `filter_rows`; `corpus_exclusions.py --check` exits 0 on cluster_b (dry-run guard 1d).
* **Stamps.** Always: `HARNESS-CLEAN`, `PATCH-BITES`, `ONE-NETWORK-PLAINNET`, `HORIZON-100-ONLY`, **`DOSE-ONSET-CONFOUNDED`**, `SIGMA-PRIOR-FROZEN`/`-INBATCH`. Conditional: `POSITIVE-CONTROL-REPRODUCES`; `K13-/K33-/K152-AT-HEAD/-BETWEEN/-AT-PLATEAU`; `KNEE-IN-(a,b]`; `TOP-AT-K01`; `FLOOR-READINGS-ARE-BOUNDS`; `TRAIN-AGREES`/`-DISAGREES`.

### 235.4 Three things that bound the result, led with

**(1) The DOWN vote was re-carried again, by the tier the eligibility bar left in.** From the runs' own probe records (`analysis/cvt3_attack_indep.py` [7], [8]; descriptive):

| arm | sum DOWN, epochs 17–36 | sum DOWN, 36–100 | silenced share of the RAW mass, 17–36 / 36–100 | records whose sign the silence flipped, 17–36 | DOWN mass OUTSIDE {50} ∪ C, 36–100 | shared beta first ≤ −14 (after the peak) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `k01` | 1.000 ×3 | 1.000 ×3 | — | — | 0.001 | 34.4 ×3 |
| MUTE50 | 0.884 / 0.895 / 0.884 | 1.000 ×3 | 0.69 / 0.73 / 0.60 ; 0.65 / 0.72 / 0.54 | 0.105–0.116 | 0.007–0.071 | 38.2–38.6 |
| **MUTEDOWN** | **0.842 / 0.800 / 0.779** | **0.988 / 0.963 / 0.909** | 0.90 / 0.88 / 0.89 ; 0.94 ×3 | 0.147–0.211 | **0.596 / 0.563 / 0.549** | **40.4 / 42.0 / 43.0** |
| MUTECTL | 0.863 / 0.874 / 0.863 | 1.000 ×3 | 0.47 / 0.53 / 0.48 ; 0.36 / 0.44 / 0.37 | 0.126–0.137 | 0.072–0.076 | 39.2–39.4 |
| HEAD (complement) | 0.642 / 0.653 / 0.632 | 0.844 / 0.809 / 0.816 | — | — | 0.015–0.021 | 61.4–64.6 |

On MUTEDOWN's post-epoch-36 records the top UNSILENCED voters are `linear.weight` (0.22–0.29, UP), `layer4.1.bn2.bias` (0.10–0.11, UP), then `layer3.0.conv1.weight` (0.08–0.09), `layer2.0.conv1.weight` (0.07–0.08), `layer2.1.conv2.weight` (0.05–0.06) and `bn1.weight` (0.06–0.07), **each DOWN on 1.00 of records** — four of the seven tensors 232.3 named as "neither C nor pool" (DOWN on 0.50–0.90 of `cvt1` MUTE's pooled records). The silence of 94 % of the raw mass delayed the shared step size's fall by ~2–4 epochs against MUTE50 and left the network's level where MUTE50's is. **So: removing the coalition as ruled does not rescue; it does NOT show that no silenced set could (a larger set was not run), and the objection "re-carriage" is answered only at the level of the registered coalition.** Continuous pins read late for MUTEDOWN (90.6 / 99.6 / 99.6) because its beta touches −15 intermittently; from epoch 40 it sits at or below −14 on 0.99 / 0.97 / 0.95 of records.

**(2) `P_COAL` is not a coalition effect.** MUTEDOWN sits on MUTE50 (+0.03 pp); the primary is positive because MUTECTL is 3.75 pp (−6.61 SE) BELOW `k01`, on every seed (−4.90 / −2.98 / −3.38 paired). MUTECTL's shared beta peaks highest and latest (−4.11 at epoch 19.4–19.6), its TEST peaks at 8.79 at epoch 20 and then FALLS to 7.8 by epoch 29, TRAIN with it (8.4 → 7.8). Why silencing 15 BN biases and 5 small convs (0.028 of the mass) costs 3.75 pp is **UNSURE**; nothing registered speaks to it. `CTL-BELOW-K01` is stamped; its reading is a location (`FLOOR-READINGS-ARE-BOUNDS`).

**(3) The scalar arms do not fail for want of shared step size (descriptive, UNSURE, not a registered statistic).** Mean step-size multiplier r = exp(beta[0] + 15) over epochs 15–30 (the window in which every arm's TEST level is set), with the arm's level (`cvt3_attack_indep.py` [11], [9]):

| arm | r, epochs 15–30 (arm mean) | r, epochs 30–40 | TEST settles (within 0.5 pp of plateau5, for good) | level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `k01` | 3,440 | 5.0 | epoch 21 | 11.57 |
| HEAD (complement) | 8,672 | 2,280 | epoch 52 | 64.60 |
| MUTE50 | 10,749 | 36.8 | epoch 23 | 11.29 |
| MUTEDOWN | 11,364 | 130.3 | epoch 23 | 11.33 |
| MUTECTL | 13,845 | 58.8 | epoch 25 | 7.82 |

Every intervened scalar arm had MORE shared step size in epochs 15–30 than HEAD's complement, and its TEST stopped rising by epoch 21–25 while r was still in the thousands; across the scalar arms more shared step size in that window does not raise the level (MUTECTL has the most and the lowest). What differs between MUTE50 and HEAD is **only** whether idx 50 moves with the shared beta or on its own (in both, 50's term is absent from the sum the others' step size reads; HEAD's isolated beta[1] pins at 21.0–23.6). **So the record is consistent with 50's OWN large step size (not a shortage of the others' step size, and not 50's vote) being what stalls the scalar arm — but that is a reading, UNSURE; no arm varied 50's step size with the rest held.**

### 235.5 The attack — an independent parser

`analysis/cvt3_attack_indep.py <runs> analysis/cVT3_downcoalition_score.py <score log>` (NEW, `51c45a4e…`; imports nothing from the scorer or any repo module, no regex; the 53 names, numels and classes come from the batch's own manifest; C and K re-typed from 232.3 and checked equal to the manifest's `COALITION_RANKED` / `CONTROL_PAIRED`; the three witness lines BUILT from the names; bars and branch order re-typed from 232.5). **Exit 0, 0 violations.** Run on the Mac against `../runs_cluster_b` and on cluster_b against the ORIGINAL `~/metaopt/runs` with the stage scorer: **byte-identical output** (`413094fc…`; also identical under `PYTHONHASHSEED` 1 and 2 on cluster_b).

* **[0]–[1]** manifest 53 tensors / 11,046,308 params; C and K 15 BN + 5 conv each, pairwise class-equal, disjoint, 50 in neither; PROVENANCE SCORER == the file; 15/15 runs: one `.out`, epochs 0–99, `RUN_DONE`, 0 tracebacks, ARGS (14 fixed flags + spec, seed, run-name, no repeat), ENV, `PROBE_TENSOR`, `VOTE_W` == the built witness (11 / 78 / 1,086 / 1,054 chars).
* **[2]–[3]** every plateau5 / TRAIN5, arm mean, sd, range, σ 0.430913, SE 0.567010 and every contrast (235.3's table is the parser's output): **equal to the scorer's printed values digit for digit**; the CSV `plateau5` of all 15 ingested rows equals the raw `.out`'s (236.8) — three readers agree.
* **[4]** G-RUNAWAY re-derived (235.2's table), branch `OWN-STEP-NECESSARY`, and all 6 re-derived conditional stamps appear in the scorer's FINAL; every bar margin printed.
* **[5] The weights bit, one step further than `G-BITE`.** (a) fsum decomposition, worst 1.8e-07 (z) / 9.3e-07 (m); set-level and swap counts equal to the scorer's. (b) **THE APPLIED STEP**: on every interior record where beta moved (182–465 per run) the step follows `−ms·sign(b2·mom_pre + (1−b2)·z_agg)`; on the records where the weighted and UNWEIGHTED directions disagree — MUTE50 11 / 10 / 10, MUTEDOWN 16 / 21 / 34, MUTECTL 13 / 12 / 13 — it follows the weighted one on all and the unweighted on none; on `k01` and HEAD there are 0 such records.
* **[6]** beta trajectories: peak, first ≤ −10 / −14 after the peak, pinned-from, clamp fraction, arm-mean beta at 10…100 (235.4). **[7]–[8]** the vote by phase and the unsilenced voters (235.4(1)). **[9]** arm-mean TEST (TRAIN) at epochs 9–99 and settle epochs. **[10]** the registration's runaway counterfactual on THIS batch (`k01` UP-if-C 1.000 ×3; MUTE50 0.957 / 0.964 / 0.029; MUTEDOWN's own trajectory 0.046 / 0.075 / 0.120). **[11]** the step-size windows (235.4(3)).

No level, contrast, gate, branch or stamp changed in any pass.

### 235.6 What this licenses, and what it does not

**Licensed (232.5's registered text for `OWN-STEP-NECESSARY`).** On `PlainNet18_c100` at `cvt1`'s cell, over 100 epochs: even with 50 and every tensor that voted DOWN on ≥ 90 % of `cvt1` MUTE's post-pin records silenced, sharing one step size leaves the scalar arm at `k01`, and the matched control does too. **Effect on 230's half (a), "the rescue needs 50 on its own step size": STRENGTHENED — it survives 230.4(2)'s re-carriage objection at the coalition level.** The BROKEN-PATCH null predicts these levels and is excluded only because G-BITE and G-BITE-SET passed.

**Not licensed.**
* That no OTHER silenced set rescues — the next tier re-carried the vote (235.4(1)); ~0.17 of the registration's mass and 0.55–0.60 of MUTEDOWN's own weighted mass still voted DOWN.
* WHY the own step size is needed (235.4(3) is a descriptive reading, UNSURE).
* That the coalition's silence has any effect on level (MUTEDOWN − MUTE50 +0.03 pp), or that `P_COAL` measures one (235.4(2)).
* A mass-matched control (K holds 1/30 of C's mass); any time-gated silence (weights act from step 0; sets chosen on post-epoch-36 records).
* Point agreement of MUTE50 / MUTEDOWN / MUTECTL with `k01` (locations), including "MUTECTL is below `k01`" as more than a stamp.
* ResNet18_c100 (BN or GN), VGG11_bn_c100; anything past 100 epochs; RULE 11.

### 236.4 Three things that bound the result, led with

**(1) Both verdict words sit on near bars, and the one rung that carries `GRADED` robustly is still moving.** K33 is `BETWEEN` only because K33 − K691 = 5.316 exceeds the 5.0 MATCH bar by 0.316 pp (+0.44 SE); `TOP-ATTENUATED` exceeds the TOP-FLAT edge by 0.259 pp (+0.36 SE). Remove either margin and the words change (K33 → AT-PLATEAU leaves K13 carrying `GRADED`; TOP → `TOP-FLAT`). K13 is clear of both bars (7.07 and 17.07 pp) — **but K13's TEST is still rising at epoch 99 (+0.015 to +0.028 pp per epoch, settle epoch 81), and its complement never pins: its beta is −12.16 (arm mean) at epoch 100 and still falling ~0.4 per 10 epochs** (`cvt2_attack_indep.py` [6], [9]). K13's 52.35 is a 100-epoch level of a still-moving arm; whether it holds (a K-dependent equilibrium) or keeps falling toward K33's (a delay) is untested. `HORIZON-100-ONLY` is stamped.

**(2) The registered sign-saturation prior failed at K33, and the record says why (descriptive).** 233.3 derived from `cvt1` INJECT's collapsed records that the rest's net UP vote would flip the complement back UP below K_SUSTAIN = 84–118. On each arm's OWN records from epoch 20 (records where the other 51 terms net UP and the twin votes DOWN; K needed = −rest / L₄₇; [8]):

| arm | K needed: median (p90, max) per seed | fraction of such records the arm's own K holds |
|---|---|---|
| HEAD (K 1) | 0.92 / 0.89 / 0.91 (≤ 1.15, max 12.3) | 0.74 / 0.77 / 0.73 |
| K13 | 12.96 / 12.87 / 12.86 (p90 ≤ 13.8, max 16.5) | **0.52 / 0.57 / 0.59** |
| K33 | 26.36 / 28.64 / 30.49 (max 35.5) | **1.00 / 0.99 / 0.92** |
| K152 | 31.69 / 41.30 / 32.37 (max 47.3) | 1.00 ×3 |
| K691 | 96.13 / 83.64 / 78.05 (max 108.9) | 1.00 ×3 |
| K2000 | 197.32 / 220.50 / 279.00 (max 329.5) | 1.00 ×3 |

The K691 row reproduces 233.3's 84–118 on `cvt1`'s INJECT records. **But the threshold is not a property of the network: along each arm's own trajectory the rest's UP vote, in units of the twin's term, scales with K** — so K33 held its collapse and K13 hovered at its own threshold (held on ~0.55 of records; complement DOWN on 0.47–0.58 of epoch-40–100 records, twin's weighted share 0.49). That is exactly the K13 behaviour SIGN-SAT-GRADED described; K33 behaved like the plateau rungs (pins at 36.4–37.8 by beta ≤ −14, as K152's).

**(3) Above K33 the rungs differ by ONSET — dose and onset confounded, as registered (descriptive, UNSURE).** Complement beta ([6]; arm per seed):

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HEAD | −4.83…−4.89 (18.0) | 41.0–41.6 | 50.0–51.8 | 56.0–58.2 | 61.6–64.6 | 99.6–99.8 | 44.2–49.8 | 0.32–0.36 |

From K33 up, beta falls 2.0 units every 4.0 epochs on every arm — Lion's maximum rate (ms 1e-3 × 500 steps = 0.5 per epoch) — so the descents are parallel lines and the rungs differ by where they start: K152 → K691 → K2000 move the peak 0.2–0.4 and 0.4 epochs earlier and the whole descent 0.6–0.8 epochs earlier each, while the level drops 4.06 and 5.26 pp. TEST settles at epoch 26–28 on every such arm, in the middle of that descent. And the level ranks with the complement's mean step-size multiplier over epochs 15–30 across all 18 blockwise runs (HEAD 8,679 / K13 7,028 / K33 6,233 / K152 5,992 / K691 5,029 / K2000 4,034 × the floor, arm means; **Spearman 0.9649**; [10]). **So the dose effect above 152 is consistent with onset bought by dose; the design cannot separate them (no time gate, `DOSE-ONSET-CONFOUNDED`), and the registered licence allows only "partly dose-sensitive above 691".**

### 236.6 What this licenses, and what it does not

**Licensed (233.6's registered text).** `GRADED`: on `PlainNet18_c100` at `cvt1`'s cell, over 100 epochs, at least one rung (K13, robustly; K33, by 0.32 pp) sits more than 5 pp from both HEAD and K691's plateau — the twin's injected vote re-collapses HEAD's complement partially, by degree. `TOP-ATTENUATED`: K2000 sits 5–10 pp below K691 — the top dose lowers `cvt1`'s residue partially; "partly dose-sensitive above 691" and nothing more about what the 0.344 was.

**Not licensed.**
* A functional form, a knee, or its location (three shape rungs; K33 ≈ K152 in trajectory and level).
* That the grading is a vote EQUILIBRIUM (K13 is still moving at 100 epochs; 236.4(1)).
* Separating dose from onset (236.4(3) is descriptive; no time gate).
* That the residue "belongs to HEAD's isolated tensor" — it falls with K; nor that any K removes it (K2000 still 13.54 pp above `k01`).
* Any caster but `layer4.1.bn1.weight`, any complement but HEAD's; ResNet (BN or GN), VGG; anything past 100 epochs; RULE 11.

### 236.7 What the two batches together say about the mechanism now (descriptive where marked)

* **Registered, both batches:** on PlainNet the isolation rescue of `layer4.1.bn2.weight` is not a vote-removal effect in a shared step size — removing its vote (`cvt1` MUTE, `cvt3` MUTE50) or its vote AND the 20-tensor DOWN coalition (`cvt3` MUTEDOWN) leaves the scalar arm at `k01` — **and** a DOWN vote injected into the rescued complement collapses that complement by degree in its weight (`cvt2`, `GRADED`), with no fixed residue (`TOP-ATTENUATED`).
* **Descriptive, UNSURE, across both:** the TEST level of every arm is set in epochs ~15–30. Inside HEAD's grouping, the level follows how much step size the COMPLEMENT keeps in that window (Spearman 0.965 over 18 runs); a stronger DOWN vote shortens the window by starting the maximum-rate descent earlier. In the scalar arms, the shared step size in that window was LARGER than HEAD's complement's on every intervened arm (10,749–13,845 vs 8,672) and the level still stalled at or below `k01` by epoch 21–25. The one factor that separates MUTE50 from HEAD is whether idx 50 rides the shared step size or its own (which pins at ~21–25 in HEAD). **So the records point to 50's OWN large step size — not the complement's vote and not a shortage of step size elsewhere — as what stalls the scalar arm, while the vote governs how long the others' step size stays large. This is a reading of descriptive readouts, not a registered result; no arm has varied 50's step size with everything else held.**
* **What stays open:** a direct manipulation of 50's own step size (236.11 R1); whether K13 and HEAD on PlainNet survive past 100 epochs (R2); dose vs onset (R3); every other network; RULE 11.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | `cvt4` — hold 50's step size | With HEAD's grouping (50's vote already out of the complement), does the rescue follow the MAGNITUDE of 50's own step size? ## 237. TRACK A — **`cvt4` REGISTERED AND DRY-RUN: IS TENSOR 50's OWN LARGE STEP SIZE THE LEVER?  236.7 READ THE RECORDS (DESCRIPTIVE, UNSURE) AS POINTING AT `layer4.1.bn2.weight`'s OWN LARGE STEP SIZE; NOTHING HAD VARIED IT WITH EVERYTHING ELSE HELD.  A NEW ADDITIVE, OPT-IN, ENVIRONMENT-CONTROLLED PATCH (`PATCH_BETAHOLD`, `BETA_HOLD=<name>:floor|shared|tri:<P>`) OVERWRITES ONE GROUP's beta AFTER EVERY META UPDATE AND ITS CLAMP, AND AT INIT, WHILE EVERY OTHER PART OF THE META-UPDATE RUNS UNCHANGED.  ON `PlainNet18_c100` AT `cvt1`'s CELL, IN AN ISOLATED TREE (`harness_cvt4` = `cvt1`'s TREE + THE PATCH): 6 ARMS × SEEDS {90, 91, 92} = 18 JOBS, 100 EPOCHS — `k01`; HEAD (byte-identical); HOLDLOW (50's beta at the −15 floor from init); HOLDSHARED (50's beta := the complement's LIVE beta, its vote still OUT of the complement's sum); HOLDHIGH (an EXOGENOUS REPLAY of MUTE's shared trajectory); HOLDHEAD (an exogenous replay of HEAD's OWN 50-trajectory: the hold's positive control).  TWO THINGS THE DERIVATION FOUND CHANGE THE BRIEF (237.3): (1) EVERY LANDED k01 / MUTE SHARED beta AND HEAD's ISOLATED beta IS A MAX-RATE TRIANGLE (≤ 0.114 log units over 24 runs), SO ONE INTEGER REPLAYS A MEASURED TRAJECTORY — HOLDHIGH REPLAYS MUTE's (P = 9428), NOT A FIXED VALUE AND NOT k01's; (2) HOLDSHARED IS THE `cvt1` MUTE ARM IN EXACT ARITHMETIC, SO IT IS NOT THE DECISIVE ARM (MUTE ALREADY SAT AT k01 TWICE) — THE DECISIVE CONTRASTS ARE HOLDHIGH vs HEAD (MAGNITUDE, VOTE OUT, COMPLEMENT FREE) AND HOLDHIGH vs HOLDSHARED (COUPLING AT MATCHED MAGNITUDE).  LION MOMENTUM: THE HELD GROUP's MOMENTUM KEEPS ITS OWN UNPATCHED RECURSION AND IS DEAD STATE (NEVER READ INTO AN APPLIED beta; NO RELEASE) — PROVED BITWISE.  SIX ACCOUNTS WITH EVERY ARM's PREDICTED LEVEL; THE BROKEN-PATCH NULL PREDICTS VOTE-REMOVAL's LEVELS EXACTLY AND IS SEPARATED BY `G-BITE`, WHICH READS THE HOLD, THE UNTOUCHED COMPLEMENT AND THE PATCH's OWN AUDITED RECORD OFF EVERY PROBE RECORD, AND WHOSE NON-VACUITY IS SHOWN ON THE 9 LANDED HEAD RUNS (36/36 REAL-RECORD NULLS FAIL).  INERTNESS PROVED BEFORE LAUNCH (CPU AND STRUCTURE 67 / 0; A REAL 300-STEP GPU RUN 51 / 0 — OFF IS BITWISE THE UNPATCHED TREE ON k01 AND HEAD, EACH EXACT STRING HOLDS 50's beta AT EVERY STEP WITH THE COMPLEMENT ON LION, AND HOLDSHARED REPRODUCES cvt1's MUTE BITWISE (beta, EVERY LOSS, EVERY FINAL WEIGHT)).  THE NOISE FLOOR IS READ THROUGH `corpus_exclusions.filter_rows`: SIGMA_PLAIN 0.4583 FILTERED vs 10.2845 NAIVE; THE PRIOR IS 0.694443. The live shared harness and `cvt1`'s tree are unchanged (hashes before and after).  **`cluster_a` NOT CONTACTED.**  THIS ENTRY TOOK NUMBER **237** (pre-assigned); `cvt5` holds 238.

### 237.1 Question

`cvt1` (230), `cvt3` (235) and `cvt2` (236) established on `PlainNet18_c100`: isolating `layer4.1.bn2.weight` (idx 50) rescues (HEAD ≈ 64.4–64.8 vs `k01` ≈ 11.5–11.9); silencing its vote while it SHARES the step size does not (MUTE 10.99, MUTE50 11.29), nor does silencing the whole DOWN coalition with it (MUTEDOWN 11.33); injecting its twin's vote into HEAD's complement collapses that complement graded in K.

Isolation does two things at once: it takes 50's vote OUT of the others' sum, and it takes 50 OFF the others' step size. 236.7 read the records (descriptive, UNSURE): in the scalar arms the shared step size over epochs 15–30 was LARGER than HEAD's complement's, yet TEST stalled at `k01` — pointing at 50's OWN large step size. **`cvt4` holds 50's step size directly, with its vote kept out of the complement's sum (HEAD's grouping), and asks whether the magnitude of 50's own step size is the lever.**

### 237.2 Design

* **Cell.** `cvt1`'s exactly (227.2): CIFAR-100, `PlainNet18_c100` (53 tensors, 11,046,308 params), SGDm (0.99, wd 0.1) + Lion meta (0.99, b2 0.9, wd 0), ms 1e-3, alpha0 1e-6, 100 ep, batch 100, `AUGMENT=1`, `BETA_CLIP=-15:-2.3026`, `PROBE=100`, `PROBE_TENSOR=1`. The ENV line is `cvt1`'s / `cpl2`'s byte for byte.
* **Isolated tree.** `$WS/harness_cvt4/cifar10`, built by `bin/cVT4_stage_harness.sh --stage` (NEW): every file of `cvt1`'s tree byte-identical (8 files, `data` a symlink to the same live target) except `Optimizers/HF.py` = `cvt1`'s HF.py (`3f2b98e1…`, kept as `HF.py.pre_betahold`) + `PATCH_BETAHOLD` = **`84b345ad…3d96`**. Runner `$WS/jobs/run_cifar_cvt4.sh` (`c801fc85…`) differs from `run_cifar.sh` in exactly its `cd` line (V-d). `cvt1`'s tree is not written (verified before and after; `cvt5` runs from it).
* **ONE submission, 18 jobs = 6 arms × seeds {90, 91, 92}** (pre-assigned; zero corpus rows, zero `.out` ARGS lines, zero `sacct` jobs carry them).

| arm | `--stepsize-groups` | `BETA_HOLD` | what 50's beta does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `k01` | `scalar` | unset | the floor anchor (shares the one beta; its vote in the sum) |
| HEAD | `sets:1-49,51-53/layer4.1.bn2.weight` | unset | its own Lion beta (rises to ≈ −8.8 at epoch ≈ 10, pins at 21–25); positive control, byte-identical to `cvt1`/`cvt2`/`cvt3`/`cpl2` |
| **HOLDLOW** | HEAD's | `layer4.1.bn2.weight:floor` | −15 (the clamp floor, 3.06e-7) from init: 50 essentially frozen |
| **HOLDSHARED** | HEAD's | `layer4.1.bn2.weight:shared` | := the complement's live beta after every update (vote out, step size shared) |
| **HOLDHIGH** | HEAD's | `layer4.1.bn2.weight:tri:9428` | exogenous replay of MUTE's shared trajectory: max-rate rise to −4.3875 (epoch 18.86), max-rate fall, clamp at epoch 40.08 |
| **HOLDHEAD** | HEAD's | `layer4.1.bn2.weight:tri:5041` | exogenous replay of HEAD's own 50-trajectory: peak −8.7745 (epoch 10.08), clamp at epoch 22.54 |

* **CO-PRIMARY** (in batch; plateau5 from each run's own `.out`; TRAIN beside TEST; each bounded in neither direction): `P_HIGH` = HEAD − HOLDHIGH (does MUTE's step size on 50 stall, with the vote out and the complement free?); `P_COUP` = HOLDHIGH − HOLDSHARED (coupling at matched magnitude); `P_LOW` = HOLDLOW − HEAD (does freezing 50 cost anything?). **KEY:** `D_HEAD` = HEAD − `k01`; `P_CTL` = HEAD − HOLDHEAD; `D_<arm>` = arm − `k01`.
* **Arm names carry no hyphen**, so every `-`-splitting reader parses them. **Six arms, not the brief's five**: HOLDHEAD is added as the hold's positive control (237.3(4)); cost 237.8.

### 237.3 Four decisions, taken from landed records (`analysis/cvt4_registration_derivations.py`, NEW; output ``4738f801…` on cluster_b`)

**(1) The shape fact: every relevant trajectory is a max-rate triangle.** From b0 = float32(log 1e-6) = −13.815510749816895, Lion moves beta by exactly ±ms per update. On every landed record set the derivation reads (S1), beta rises at the maximum rate to a peak, falls at the maximum rate to the −15 clamp, and stays:

| source | runs | peak value (range) | peak epoch | pinned from | max \|record − own triangle\| | r = e^(β+15), epochs 15–30 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `k01` shared beta | 9 (cvt1/2/3) | −5.412 … −5.332 | 17.0 ×9 | 36.2–36.6 | 0.040–0.098 | 3,339–3,617 |
| MUTE / MUTE50 shared beta | 6 (cvt1, cvt3) | −4.444 … −4.306 | 18.8–19.2 | 40.2–40.6 | 0.050–0.114 | 10,152–11,521 |
| HEAD's isolated beta[1] | 9 (cvt1/2/3) | −9.257 … −8.232 | 9.2–11.2 | 21.0–25.0 | 0.044–0.094 | 3.0–19.3 |

Worst deviation over all 24 trajectories 0.1143 log units (×1.12 in step size). So one integer — the number of up-moves P — replays a measured trajectory to that fidelity. The patch's `tri:<P>` schedule is u(n) = min(n−1, P) − max(0, n−1−P), beta = min(hi, max(lo, b0 + ms·u(n))) after update n (update 1 is Lion's no-op: h = 0 ⇒ z = 0 ⇒ sign 0; a probe record with `step` s follows update s+2).

**(2) HOLDHIGH replays a MEASURED trajectory — MUTE's, not `k01`'s — and not a fixed value.** RULE P (written in the derivation's docstring before any `cvt4` run): P = round((median over the source runs of the peak record value − b0) / ms).
* **Why a replay, not a fixed value.** Every landed trajectory starts at 1e-6 and is back at the floor by epoch 21–41. A constant large beta from step 0 would be large from the first update and for all 100 epochs — magnitude confounded with onset and duration, in a state no failing arm ever had. A replay changes ONE thing relative to HEAD: how large 50's step size is, on the schedule a failing arm actually gave it.
* **Why MUTE's, not `k01`'s.** HOLDSHARED is, in exact arithmetic, the MUTE arm (point (3)), so MUTE's measured shared trajectory is the step size HOLDSHARED is predicted to hand 50. HOLDHIGH hands 50 the same magnitude EXOGENOUSLY, so HOLDHIGH vs HOLDSHARED isolates coupling at matched magnitude, and HOLDHIGH vs HEAD isolates magnitude with the vote out and the complement free. `k01`'s trajectory (peak epoch 17.0, ⅓ of MUTE's r over epochs 15–30) is what 50 got WITH its vote in the sum — a state no vote-out arm reaches. P_K01 = 8437 is printed; a `k01`-matched dose rung was considered and deferred (237.9).
* **Result.** MUTE's six peaks (−4.410, −4.342, −4.430, −4.364, −4.444, −4.306), median −4.387422 → **P_HIGH = 9428**: peak −4.387511 after update 9429 (epoch 18.86), clamp after update 20042 (epoch 40.08); schedule r(15–30) 10,064 vs the runs' 10,152–11,521; max |record − schedule| over the six runs 0.030–0.254. HEAD's nine beta[1] peaks, median −8.774473 → **P_HEAD = 5041**: peak −8.774511 at epoch 10.08, clamp at epoch 22.54; r(15–30) 6.4 vs 3.0–19.3; max |record − schedule| 0.064–1.152 (the per-seed peaks spread over 1.02 log units; the median replay sits inside that spread).
* The step size the replay hands 50 is > 100 × the floor from epoch ≈ 6.8 to ≈ 30.9.

**(3) HOLDSHARED is the MUTE arm in exact arithmetic — declared, and it demotes HOLDSHARED from "decisive".** MUTE (scalar, `VOTE_W=layer4.1.bn2.weight:0`): one beta b; z = Σ_{i≠50} z_i + 0·z_50 (an exact +0.0); b ← clamp(b − ms·sign(b2·m + (1−b2)·z)); every tensor, 50 included, steps with e^b. HOLDSHARED: group 0 is the 52 others, so z_0 = Σ_{i≠50} z_i with the same Lion recursion; beta[1] := beta[0] at init and after every update, so 50 also steps with e^b. **The same equations from the same state**; only float paths differ (53- vs 52-term python sums with an exact +0.0; `np.exp` on a 0-d value vs a 2-vector; beta on GPU vs CPU) — measured on a real run (237.4, RR4). Consequences, stated before any run: **(a)** the operator's "decisive arm" separation of "its vote leaves the shared sum" from "it stops receiving the shared step size" was already made by `cvt1` MUTE and `cvt3` MUTE50 (vote out, shared step size ⇒ `k01`); **(b)** VOTE-REMOVAL ("HOLDSHARED rescues like HEAD") contradicts two landed batches under an arithmetic identity — its prior is ≈ 0, and a HOLDSHARED rescue would first mean the two float paths diverge over 100 epochs; **(c)** what HOLDSHARED adds is the in-batch, in-grouping anchor HOLDHIGH is compared to. The decisive contrasts are `P_HIGH` and `P_COUP`.

**(4) HOLDHEAD, the hold's positive control.** Every held arm replaces 50's responsive Lion beta by a schedule. If replacing it breaks the rescue by itself, no held arm speaks to magnitude. HOLDHEAD replays HEAD's own median 50-trajectory; it is predicted at HEAD under every account but ANY-HOLD-BREAKS, and the branch map reads it FIRST.

**The meta-optimiser's state for the held group (Lion momentum), stated exactly.** `Lion_meta_update` runs unchanged on the whole beta vector (elementwise sign, then momentum ← 0.99·momentum + 0.01·z, then PATCH_CLIP's clamp); only after that is beta[0][1] overwritten. So (i) the complement's beta and momentum are bitwise what they would be given the same z; (ii) group 1's momentum is NOT reset, frozen or copied — it keeps the unpatched recursion on 50's own raw z; (iii) it is DEAD STATE: the only reader is group 1's own Lion step, whose output is overwritten on the same update, from init to the last update with no release. `tests/test_betahold.py` B4 proves (i)–(ii) BITWISE over 3,000 updates of synthetic z for all four holds and a `tri:100` (the whole momentum vector equals the unpatched object's at every update). A hold released mid-run would inherit a stale momentum; this patch has no release.

### 237.4 The patch, its inertness and its bite (proved BEFORE launch)

**`patches/patch_betahold.py`** (NEW, `1c6dfadb…`) applies on top of `cvt1`'s HF.py and makes FOUR insertions, editing no existing line:
1. a guarded `self._bh_apply()` in `step()`, after PATCH_CLIP's clamp and before `self._probe(...)`;
2. one `self._bh_init(net_param_names_and_size)` call right after `init_meta`'s `_vw_init` call;
3. a guarded `self._bh_attach(rec)` in `_probe`, right before `_pt_attach`;
4. six new `_bh_` methods before `check_required_attributes`.

How it behaves:
* **OFF.** `BETA_HOLD` unset or empty → prints `BETA_HOLD: off`, `_bh_on` False; no tensor touched, no probe key added.
* **ON.** Parses `<name>:floor | <name>:shared | <name>:tri:<P>`; the named tensor must sit ALONE in a group of a blockwise grouping; applies hold(0) at init; after every update records the value Lion + clamp wrote (`bh_nat`), overwrites it, and counts the updates where they differed (`bh_active`). Each probe record of a held run gains `bh_n`, `bh_active`, `bh_nat`, `bh_held`.
* **Loud.** A malformed value, an unknown name, a name not alone in its group, a non-blockwise spec, `shared` without exactly 2 groups, a meta algorithm other than Lion, BETA_CLIP unset, HIER other than ''/`none`, a `tn:` spec, or VOTE_W on at the same time → ValueError.
* **Witness line on every run** (the runner's ENV line cannot carry BETA_HOLD): `BETA_HOLD: off`, or e.g. `BETA_HOLD: on type=blockwise group=1 groupsize=1 name=layer4.1.bn2.weight mode=tri P=9428 b0=-13.815510749816895 ms=0.001 lo=-15.0 hi=-2.3026 peak=-4.387510749816894`. The tree also prints `VOTE_W: off` on every run.

| proof | where | result |
|---|---|---|
| **Structure** (`tests/test_betahold.py` B0): the four regions appear as registered; **deleting them reproduces `HF.py.pre_betahold` (= `cvt1`'s HF.py) BYTE FOR BYTE**; exactly six new `_bh_` methods; every pre-existing method present in order | stage V-f; launcher guard 4b2; in the log | 10 / 0 |
| **CPU, live PlainNet** (B1–B5): each registered string prints exactly the scorer's witness and inits beta [b0, b0] / [b0, −15]; unset and EMPTY print `BETA_HOLD: off` and leave beta and every attribute EQUAL to the unpatched object's; 18 malformed forms raise; the patch's schedule == the scorer's at every n in 0..50,001 (both P, floor); **B4: through the harness's own `Lion_meta_update` + clamp for 3,000 updates of synthetic z, the complement's beta and the WHOLE momentum vector are BITWISE the unpatched object's for every hold, beta[1] is the hold after every update, `bh_nat` is what Lion wrote, `bh_active` counts exactly the differing updates (1,470–2,199 > 0)** | `$WS/runs/cvt4/inertness_betahold.log` | **67 / 0**, `TEST_BETAHOLD_RC 0` |
| **GPU, REAL run** (`tests/test_betahold_realrun.py`, job `cvt4inert` **5021680**, [HOST_3c1b003035] RTX 2080 Ti, 7 min 50 s, imports `cvt1`'s registered `tests/test_voteweight_realrun.py` UNEDITED — train.py's own parse_args, build_network, build_optimizer, load_data, CIFAR-100, AUGMENT=1, seed 90, 300 steps, PROBE every 10, PROBE_TENSOR=1, cudnn deterministic, one process per variant; the unpatched tree is `cvt1`'s, read-only). **RR0** unpatched vs itself bitwise. **RR1 OFF** (unset and empty, on `k01` AND HEAD) == unpatched: beta every step, loss every step, probe.jsonl bytes, every final parameter and buffer, BITWISE; each printed `BETA_HOLD: off` and `VOTE_W: off`. **RR2** each of the four exact strings (and a test-only `tri:100`): one witness line == the scorer's; beta[1] after EVERY step == the hold; at every record the complement == Lion recomputed, beta/beta_pre[1] == the hold, and the `bh_*` record audits. **RR3** HOLDLOW's beta[1] differs from HEAD's at every step and its final weights differ; `tri:100` departs from the natural rise after its peak with `bh_active` > 0; HOLDSHARED / HOLDHIGH / HOLDHEAD differ from HEAD's beta on ≥ 1 step with `bh_active` > 0. **RR4** HOLDSHARED vs MUTE (scalar, VOTE_W 50:0, same tree): beta identical at every step (gating); **loss identical at every step and every final parameter and buffer BITWISE IDENTICAL** (reported, non-gating) — the arithmetic identity of 237.3(3) holds to the bit on this path | same log | **51 / 0, ALL PASS, `REALRUN_RC 0`**; log `5529e33a…` |

* **Every hold bites within 300 real steps, in beta.** Against the unpatched HEAD: HOLDLOW's beta[1] differs at every step and its final weights differ (`067ebdd1…` vs `dbaf26e4…`); HOLDSHARED's beta differs on 296 / 300 steps (`bh_active` 6: 50's own Lion step disagreed with the complement's 6 times), HOLDHIGH's and HOLDHEAD's on 298 / 300 (`bh_active` 123; the two schedules coincide below their peaks); `tri:100` tracks the natural rise to its peak (float32 accumulation only, 4.0e-05) and departs after it (≥ 0.100 from step 150, `bh_active` 233). **Limit, disclosed (as 227.4):** the final weights of HOLDSHARED, HOLDHIGH, HOLDHEAD and `tri:100` are bitwise HEAD's — a step-size difference of ~1e-7 per step on BatchNorm scales near 1.0 sits below float32 resolution in 300 steps — so for those four non-vacuity reaches beta and the probe record, not the parameters.
* **Two first attempts failed, both in the TESTS, and were fixed before any batch result existed.**
  1. On cluster_b's login node `tests/test_betahold.py` stopped at its first torch section: `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` returns None for a file named `HF.py.pre_betahold` (no `.py` suffix). `_load` now passes an explicit `SourceFileLoader`; B0 had passed; no assertion changed.

Anchors (between batch, non-gating): `k01` 11.95 / 11.57 / 11.48, HEAD 64.79 / 64.60 / 64.42 (`cvt1` / `cvt3` / `cvt2`), MUTE 10.99, MUTE50 11.29. Intervals: K01_PL 8–16, FREE_PL 56–72, PART_PL 20–50.

* **Asserted in selftest D.** The lowest level any account predicts for any arm is 8 pp (7.0 above chance; `cvt1`'s MUTE was 10.99). Every co-primary's predicted interval sits ≥ 25 pp inside ±99 under every account (bounded in neither direction). HEAD is predicted ≥ 40 pp off `k01` under every account. Every account's midpoint lands in its registered branch, and the six non-null accounts' midpoints land in six different branches.

### 237.6 Gates, branches and what each licenses — `decide()`, first match wins; frozen bars

**Harness gates (→ `HARNESS-UNSOUND`, rc 1).** `G-ARGS` (each run's own single ARGS line: spec, net, cell, 18 fixed flags, seed, run-name); `G-ENV` (one ENV line == `cvt1`'s / `cpl2`'s; one `PROBE_TENSOR: on every=100 type=<arm's> tensors=53`); **`G-VOTEW`** (exactly one `VOTE_W: off`); **`G-HOLDW`** (exactly one `BETA_HOLD` line == the arm's witness: `off` ×2 arms; floor 96 chars, shared 108, tri 165 ×2); `G-STRUCT` (manifest byte-identical to the scorer's, 4,508 bytes, with the `REPLAY B0 … P_HIGH 9428 P_HEAD 5041` and `BETAHOLD` / `WITNESS` tables); `G-PROV` (MODE submit; build_network `e65e6773…`; **HF `84b345ad…`**; **RUNNER `c801fc85…`**; SCORER == the file); `G-FLOOR`/`G-CEIL` (max arm mean in 15–90).

**`G-BITE` (→ `PATCH-NOT-VERIFIED`, rc 1; before any level)**, from `runs/cvt4/probe_cvt4-<arm>-s<seed>/probe.jsonl`, on every finite record (non-finite records are counted and stamped `NONFINITE-<arm>`, not failed):
* (a) 500 parseable records at steps 0, 100, …, 49,900 with beta, beta_pre, mom_pre and z_agg per group;
* (b) **every UNHELD group follows Lion**: recorded beta[g] == clamp(beta_pre[g] − ms·sign(b2·mom_pre[g] + (1−b2)·z_agg[g])) within 1e-5 (all groups of `k01` and HEAD; group 0 of every held arm — the hold touched nothing else); ties at rounding level (|L| ≤ 1e-12 of its parts) are counted, not judged;
* (c) **the schedule on the held group 1**: beta[1] == hold(step+2) AND beta_pre[1] == hold(step+1) (floor −15; tri v_P; shared: == beta[0] and == beta_pre[0]) — the beta_pre half catches a hold that acted only at probe steps;
* (d) **the patch's own record, audited**: `bh_n` == step+2; `bh_nat` == Lion recomputed from the record's group-1 `beta_pre` / `mom_pre` / `z_agg`; `bh_held` == beta[1]; `bh_active` non-decreasing, ≤ `bh_n`, ≥ the records where `bh_nat` ≠ `bh_held`;
* (e) `k01` and HEAD carry no `bh_*` key.
* **No minimum on `bh_active`**, by design: HOLDHEAD replays a trajectory close to what 50 would do, so few overrides differ from Lion's value (on HEAD's own records 0–6 of 500 would); a minimum would fail a working control. The separation from the null is (c), non-vacuous by 237.4.

**Branches.** `UNRESOLVED-DIVERGED` (a seed range > 5) → `SCALAR-NOT-COLLAPSED` (`k01` > 20) → `POSITIVE-CONTROL-FAILED` (HEAD − `k01` < 20). Then per held arm, state = **AT-HEAD** iff L ≥ HEAD − 5, **AT-K01** iff L ≤ `k01` + 2 (below included), else **BETWEEN**:

| order | condition | branch | what it does to 236.7's reading ("50's OWN large step size stalls the scalar arm") |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | HOLDHEAD AT-K01 | **`HOLD-CONTROL-FAILED`** | untested: an exogenous schedule on 50 breaks the rescue by itself; no magnitude sentence |
| 2 | HOLDHEAD BETWEEN | `HOLD-CONTROL-PARTIAL` | untested; stop |
| 3 | HOLDSHARED AT-HEAD | **`VOTE-REMOVAL`** | contradicted for HEAD's grouping; first read as the float paths diverging (237.3(3)); 230(a) and 235 put IN QUESTION, not rescinded |
| 4 | HOLDSHARED BETWEEN | `SHARED-PARTIAL` | neither; stop |
| 5 | HOLDLOW AT-K01 | **`LOW-STALLS`** | reframed: small is not sufficient, the trajectory matters (HOLDHIGH's state stamped) |
| 6 | HOLDLOW BETWEEN | `LOW-PARTIAL` | neither (HOLDHIGH's state stamped) |
| 7 | HOLDLOW AT-HEAD, HOLDHIGH AT-K01 | **`OWN-STEP-MAGNITUDE`** | **CONFIRMED BY INTERVENTION** at this cell: 50's own large step size is sufficient to stall, a small one sufficient to keep the rescue, vote out either way; 230(a) sharpens to "50 on a SMALL step size". Not licensed: which window matters, a dose curve, why, any other tensor / network / horizon |
| 8 | HOLDLOW AT-HEAD, HOLDHIGH BETWEEN | **`OWN-STEP-GRADED`** | partly confirmed: magnitude carries part, coupling the rest |
| 9 | HOLDLOW AT-HEAD, HOLDHIGH AT-HEAD | **`COUPLING`** | **REFUTED AS WORDED**: the same magnitude applied exogenously keeps the rescue; the stall needs 50's step size to move with the complement's |

* **Frozen bars (O2).** GAP_MIN 20.0 (35.27 SE), K01_MAX 20.0, MATCH 5.0 (8.82 SE), NULL 2.0 (3.53 SE), RESCUE 10.0 (TRAIN-agreement threshold only), DIVERGED 5.0, FLOOR_MIN 15.0, CEIL_MAX 90.0; G-BITE: BH_TOL 1e-5 (≤ 1/50 of one Lion step), TIE_REL 1e-12, N_RECORDS 500.
* **Stamps.** Always: `HARNESS-CLEAN`, `PATCH-BITES`, `HOLD-FROM-INIT`, `REPLAY-MAX-RATE-TRIANGLE`, `SHARED-IS-MUTE-ARITHMETIC`, `ONE-NETWORK-PLAINNET`, `HORIZON-100-ONLY`, `SIGMA-PRIOR-FROZEN`/`-INBATCH`. Conditional: `POSITIVE-CONTROL-REPRODUCES`; `<ARM>-AT-HEAD`/`-BETWEEN`/`-AT-K01` for the four held arms; `<ARM>-ABOVE-HEAD`; `<ARM>-BELOW-K01`; `NONFINITE-<ARM>`; `FLOOR-READINGS-ARE-BOUNDS`; `TRAIN-AGREES`/`-DISAGREES` (every co-primary with |TEST| ≥ 10 has TRAIN's sign).
* **After FINAL, descriptive and unable to move it:** per run the complement's and 50's beta peak, pin epoch and r(15–30), and `bh_active`; arm-mean TEST (TRAIN) at epochs 9 / 19 / 29 / 39 / 49 / 99.

The landing track needs an additive, opt-in extension of the helper (or a separate check of the BETA_HOLD lines) — not done here, UNSURE which.

### 237.9 Deviations from the brief and limits, disclosed

* **Six arms, not five.** HOLDHEAD (the hold's positive control) is added; without it a stall of HOLDHIGH could be "any exogenous schedule on 50 breaks the rescue". Cost +3 runs (≈ +2.1 GPU-h).
* **HOLDSHARED is not decisive** (237.3(3)): it is MUTE in exact arithmetic, and MUTE already answered "vote out, shared step size". The decisive contrasts are `P_HIGH` and `P_COUP`. VOTE-REMOVAL is registered as the brief asked, with a prior of ≈ 0 stated.
* **HOLDHIGH replays MUTE's trajectory, not `k01`'s** (237.3(2)); a `k01`-matched rung (P_K01 8437, ⅓ of MUTE's step size over epochs 15–30) and a fixed-value arm were considered and not run. **No time gate**: every hold acts from init to the end; which window of 50's large step size matters is not tested.
* **One replay per trajectory.** HOLDHEAD replays the MEDIAN HEAD trajectory; the nine per-seed peaks spread over 1.02 log units (max |record − schedule| up to 1.15), so HOLDHEAD is not each seed's own trajectory.
* **The float32 schedule is exact; Lion's accumulation is not.** The patch computes b0 + ms·u(n) in double and stores it in float32; Lion accumulates ms in float32 and drifts by ~2e-4 per 500 updates from the exact line. So a replay is not bit-identical to a natural max-rate rise (the drift is ≤ ~1 % in step size and is inside 237.3(1)'s fidelity).
* **The `corpus_exclusions --check` gap at landing** (237.7) is owed, not solved.
* **The stage holds more than this registration.** `~/stage_cvt4` was rsync'd from the shared working copy (which also holds `cvt5`'s committed files); the launcher and scorer read none of them; at launch the files guard 1b names are compared with `git show HEAD:<path>`.
