### 238.6 Gates, branches and what each licenses — first match wins

* **Harness gates (→ `HARNESS-UNSOUND`, rc 1):** `G-ARGS` (all 19 flags incl. `--num-epochs 300` and `--max-time 999:00:00`), `G-ENV` (one ENV line == `cvt1`'s == `cvt2`'s; one `PROBE_TENSOR … tensors=53` of the arm's type), `G-VOTEW`, `G-STRUCT` (manifest byte-identical, `EPOCHS 300`, `CTRL_EPOCHS 100`), `G-PROV` (MODE submit, build_network, HF, **RUNNER**, **TRAIN**, SCORER shas), `G-FLOOR` / `G-CEIL`. **`G-BITE`** (→ `PATCH-NOT-VERIFIED`, rc 1, before any level): 1,500 parseable records per run; per group z_agg == Σ wᵢ z_tensorᵢ and mom_pre == Σ wᵢ m_tensorᵢ; K13 / K33 ≥ 50 informative records, the unweighted sum matching none. A dropped run, or one with fewer than 300 epoch lines → `INCOMPLETE` (rc 2).
* **Global (void A, B, C):** `UNRESOLVED-DIVERGED` (a seed range @100 > 5) → `SCALAR-NOT-COLLAPSED` (`k01`@100 > 20) → `POSITIVE-CONTROL-FAILED` (D_HEAD@100 < 20).
* **(a), `decide_a()`:** `K13-PREMISE-NOT-REPLICATED` (HEAD@100 − K33@100 < 15, or K13@100 within 5 of HEAD or of K33) → `UNRESOLVED-K33-DIVERGED` (K33's range @300 > 5) → `UNRESOLVED-K13-SPLIT` (K13's range @300 > 5; per-seed tokens stamped, not averaged) → `K13-BELOW-K33` (G13 < −5; unregistered, stop) → **`GRADED-WAS-A-DELAY`** (G13 ≤ 5) → `K13-ABOVE-HEAD` (unregistered, stop) → **`K13-RECOVERS-TO-HEAD`** (DROP13 ≥ +5 and HEAD@300 − K13@300 ≤ 5) → **`K-DEPENDENT-EQUILIBRIUM`** (DROP13 ≥ −5) → **`GRADED-PARTLY-A-DELAY`**.
* **(b), `decide_b()` (`cgn3`'s map):** `UNRESOLVED-HEAD-DIVERGED` (HEAD's or `k01`'s range @300 > 5) → **`RESCUE-COLLAPSES`** (D_HEAD@300 ≤ 5) → **`RESCUE-SURVIVES`** (RHO ≥ 0.80 and D_HEAD@300 ≥ 15) → **`RESCUE-ATTENUATES`** (+ `ATTENUATE-MILD` / `-SEVERE`).
* **(c), `decide_c()` (a registered token that cannot move A or B):** `K33-SPLIT-AT-300` → **`K33-REOPENS`** (any seed's max r after epoch 100 ≥ 10, or K33@300 − K33@100 ≥ +5) → **`K33-HOLDS-PINNED`** (K33 complement PINNED on ≥ 2 seeds, every seed's max r after epoch 100 ≤ 2, and |K33@300 − K33@100| < 5) → `K33-UNRESOLVED`.
* **The pin gate, AFTER all three, as stamps** (cvh1's magnitude form, never the exact-clamp dwell): `K13-COMPLEMENT-PINNED/-NEITHER/-FREE`; if PINNED `K13-PIN-EPOCH:x`, `K13-POST-PIN-WINDOW:x`, `K13-WINDOW-MEETS-W100`/`-SHORT`, `K13-PIN-INSIDE-BOUND`/`-AFTER-BOUND` (vs 223.5), `K13-FROZEN-AT-PIN`/`-DECAYS-AFTER-PIN`/`-IMPROVES-AFTER-PIN` (level 5–10 epochs after the latest pin vs @300, READ_BAR); otherwise **`UNRESOLVED-NOT-PINNED` (INFORMATIVE: a K13 complement that never collapses in 300 epochs is the stronger equilibrium reading)** and `K13-POST-PIN-UNMEASURED`. The same set for HEAD; `K33-COMPLEMENT-*`, `K33-MAXR-POST100:x`, `K33-EXACT-CLAMP-CONTINUOUS`/`-EXCURSIONS`; `K01-<class>`; `FLOOR-HOLDS`/`-DRIFTS`. Also `RHO:x`, `TRAIN-AGREES-A`/`-B` (the same maps on TRAIN), `K13-`/`HEAD-`/`K33-LEVEL-FALLS/-HOLDS/-RISES`, and always `HARNESS-CLEAN`, `PATCH-BITES`, `ONE-NETWORK-PLAINNET`, `HORIZON-300`, `NO-TIME-GATE`, `ONE-CELL-ONLY`, `SIGMA-PRIOR-FROZEN`/`-INBATCH`. **FINAL: `<A> | <B> | <C> | stamps`.**
* **Licences (registered text in the scorer), in short.** `GRADED-WAS-A-DELAY`: at long horizon the ladder collapses at every K ≥ 13 and 236's GRADED is a 100-epoch statement; read with the pin stamp. `K-DEPENDENT-EQUILIBRIUM` is an equilibrium **of the level**: with `K13-COMPLEMENT-PINNED` + `K13-FROZEN-AT-PIN` the level held through its complement's own collapse (so it was set before the pin, as on GN, and is NOT a step-size equilibrium); with `UNRESOLVED-NOT-PINNED` the step size never collapsed either. `RESCUE-SURVIVES` with HEAD pinned and frozen: the rescue's level survives ≥ 234 post-pin epochs — `cvh1`'s / `cgn3`'s sentence on the fourth network. `K33-HOLDS-PINNED`: the stricter reading's exact-clamp departures are excursions inside r ≤ 2, not a re-opening. **Not licensed under any branch:** any network but PlainNet; any K but 13 and 33 at long horizon; anything past 300 epochs; dose vs onset; the layerwise ceiling (no `kL`); any between-batch contrast; point agreement for floor-band readings; RULE 11.
* **After FINAL, descriptive and unable to move it:** arm-mean TEST (TRAIN) at epochs 29–299, arm-mean group-0 beta at 50–299 and group-1 pinned-from, and K13's complement DOWN fraction by 50-epoch window.

### 239.1 The gap

`--check` compared a listed run's `VOTE_W` lines with its listed witness and required every unlisted run of a listed batch to print `VOTE_W: off`. `cvt4`'s 12 held runs print `VOTE_W: off` plus a `BETA_HOLD: on ...` line and must be listed with that `BETA_HOLD` line as witness (237.7), so the check would FAIL a correct landing. It also could not see an ON run missing from the list: it read only batches that already had a listed row, and only their `VOTE_W` lines.

### 239.2 What changed (`analysis/corpus_exclusions.py`, `5d7694ad…` → `9ede7453…`; only the `--check` path and its docstring)

* **A `KINDS` table** — `("VOTE_W", "VOTE_W: off")`, `("BETA_HOLD", "BETA_HOLD: off")`. A row's kind is the entry its `witness` starts with (`<prefix>:`); a witness naming no kind FAILS. A future kind is one line.
* **Witness check, generalised.** A listed run's lines of its kind must equal `[witness]`; an unlisted run of a listed batch must print exactly the `off` line of every kind that batch's rows use. Line extraction is the old `startswith(prefix)` (the same rule `cVT4_betahold_score.py` uses, lines 511–512). The per-run messages and the summary line are unchanged for a VOTE_W-only list.
* **Completeness, new.** With `--runs`, every `.out` found is scanned. A run that is a row of `all_runs.csv` (by `(run, job_id)` from `<run>-<job_id>.out`) and prints an ON line (any line of a kind other than its `off` line) must be listed, with a witness of that kind. ON runs **not yet in the CSV are counted, not required**: listing them would fail the existing present-exactly-once check, and a running batch or an inertness job must not block another batch's landing. One new stdout line reports the counts.
* **Unavailable logs: unchanged.** Without `--runs` no log is read. With `--runs`, only logs under those dirs are seen (a listed `.out` that is absent still FAILs `found N of M`). The `cvt4` / `cvt5` `.out` files are on cluster_b only today, so at landing they must be synced to `../runs_cluster_b` before running the check on the Mac.

### 239.3 Tests (`tests/test_corpus_exclusions_check.py`, NEW, `40feb903…`, stdlib; synthetic TSV, CSV and `.out` in a temp copy of the repo layout, the real module run as a subprocess)

C1 BETA_HOLD row passes; C2 mismatched BETA_HOLD witness fails and quotes the log's line; C3 VOTE_W row passes with the old summary line byte for byte, and a VOTE_W mismatch fails with the old message; C4 an ON corpus run missing from the TSV fails (a: BETA_HOLD batch with no listed row; b: one held run left out of a listed batch; c: VOTE_W run of an unlisted batch); C5 `off` / witness-less runs not required; C6 ON runs not in the CSV not required, and counted; C7 a listed run printing an ON line of another kind fails; C8 an unregistered kind fails; C9 no `--runs` reads no log. **Before the edit: 9 FAIL / 6 PASS, exit 1** (the 6 passes are the regression guards C3 ×3 and C9, plus C2's exit code and C7, which the old code also failed for the wrong reason). **After: 15 PASS / 0 FAIL, exit 0.**

### 240.4 Three things that bound the result, led with

**No registered bar is near any reading; the three bounds are about what the design can separate.**

**(1) "Complement free" is not "complement like HEAD's": in HOLDHIGH the complement collapsed too.** 237.2 described HOLDHIGH as "vote out, complement free". The complement's step size was not forced, but it did not behave like HEAD's. From the runs' own records (`cvt4_attack_indep.py` [6], [D1], [D3], [D4]):
* HOLDHIGH's complement followed MUTE's measured shared path — peak −4.448 / −4.354 / −4.494 at epoch 18.8–19.0, pinned at **40.4 on every seed**, within 0.064–0.160 of the `v_9428` replay at every record — while HEAD's complement pinned at **99.6 / 97.8 / 99.6**. At epoch 40 the arm-mean complement beta is −14.86 in HOLDHIGH against −7.81 in HEAD.
* **So the batch cannot say whether 50's large step size stalls the network directly, or by making the complement collapse early. `P_HIGH` changes both.**
* **Timing (DESCRIPTIVE, UNSURE; corrected at 240.6).** Tensor 50's beta leaves HEAD's at epoch 10 (HOLDHIGH − HEAD, arm means, +0.56 at epoch 10, +2.50 at 12). The arm-mean TEST gap HEAD − HOLDHIGH by `Epoch` line (line n = after n+1 epochs): +0.24 (14), +0.84 (15), **+2.05 (16)**, +3.15 (17), +7.16 (18), +12.49 (20), +34.07 (30); it stays above 2 pp from line 16 on. The complement beta difference HOLDHIGH − HEAD (arm means) is **−0.001 after 17 epochs** (end of line 16), **+0.077 after 18** (end of line 17) and **+0.927 after 19** (end of line 18; per seed 0.84 / 1.04 / 0.91); per seed it first exceeds 0.1 at epoch **18.2 / 18.2 / 18.0**. **So the TEST gap passes 2 pp while the two complements are still identical, and the stall begins before the complement's collapse** — a reading of descriptive records, not a registered statistic. HOLDSHARED shows the same order (gap +1.9 at line 16, +6.7 at line 18; complement difference +0.08 at 18.0).

**(2) No time gate, one shape per arm, no dose curve.** The replay holds 50's step size above 100 × the floor from epoch ≈ 6.8 to ≈ 30.9. The TEST split begins at epoch 16–17, while that step size is still rising. Which part of the trajectory does the damage is not tested, and there is one large trajectory (MUTE's), one small (HEAD's own) and the floor — no rung between. HOLDHEAD replays the MEDIAN HEAD trajectory (peak −8.815); in-batch HEAD's own 50-peaks were −8.853 / −9.169 / −9.501, and `P_CTL` is +0.07 pp.

**(3) Floor readings are locations, and `P_LOW` has a narrow window.** HOLDSHARED sits 0.30 pp and HOLDHIGH 0.57 pp (−1.00 SE) below `k01` — locations (`FLOOR-READINGS-ARE-BOUNDS`), not point agreement. [AMENDED at CORRECTIONS 244 (the `cvt4` verifier's fix 3): so `P_COUP` = HOLDHIGH − HOLDSHARED ≈ 0 (−0.27 pp) is a reading between two arms at the same floor location, not a measured absence of coupling; what the batch does say against COUPLING is that its predicted HOLDHIGH band 56–72 was missed, by 44.87 pp (240.3).] HOLDLOW sits +0.73 pp above HEAD (+1.28 SE; TRAIN +1.52), **per seed +0.92 / +1.14 / +0.12** — not a registered effect and no stamp is reached. And HOLDLOW differs from HEAD only while HEAD's own 50 is above the floor: HEAD's isolated beta pins at 20.2–22.8 and sits at −15 on 386–399 of its 500 records (read as HOLDLOW, HEAD fails on only 101–114 records). **`P_LOW` is a statement about roughly the first 22 epochs, nothing later.**

### 240.8 What this licenses, and what it does not

**Licensed (237.6's registered text for `OWN-STEP-MAGNITUDE`).** On `PlainNet18_c100` at `cvt1`'s cell, over 100 epochs, with 50's vote out of the complement's sum in every held arm: handing 50 the step size MUTE's shared beta had (an exogenous max-rate replay) stalls the arm at `k01`, as HOLDSHARED (= MUTE) does; freezing 50 at the floor keeps HEAD's level; the replay of HEAD's own 50-trajectory keeps HEAD's level. **Effect on 236.7's reading: CONFIRMED BY INTERVENTION — 50's own large step size is sufficient to stall, and 50 on a small step size is sufficient to keep the rescue, vote out either way. `cvt1`'s half (a) sharpens to "the rescue needs 50 on a SMALL step size". [AMENDED at CORRECTIONS 244 (the `cvt4` verifier's fix 2): the licence is SUFFICIENCY at this cell, as the sentence before says — one large trajectory sufficient to stall, the floor or HEAD's own trajectory sufficient to keep the rescue; no dose curve and no time window, so "needs a SMALL step size" says no more than that.]** The BROKEN-PATCH null predicts HOLDSHARED and HOLDHIGH at 56–72 and is excluded by level and by `G-BITE`.

**Not licensed.**
* That 50's large step size stalls the network DIRECTLY rather than through the complement's early collapse (240.4(1); the timing reading is descriptive, UNSURE).
* Which window of the trajectory matters; a dose curve; why a large step size on this BatchNorm scale stalls the network (240.4(2)).
* That HOLDSHARED and MUTE are the same RUN (the same equations on different float paths, 237.3(3)); point agreement for arms read at `k01`; `P_LOW` as an effect or beyond ~epoch 22 (240.4(3)).
* Any other tensor, network (ResNet with BN or GN, VGG), cell or horizon; RULE 11.

### 240.9 What `cvt1`–`cvt4` together say about the mechanism now (descriptive where marked)

* **Registered, four batches:** on PlainNet the isolation rescue of `layer4.1.bn2.weight` is not a vote-removal effect in a shared step size (`cvt1` MUTE, `cvt3` MUTE50 and MUTEDOWN at `k01`); a DOWN vote injected into the rescued complement collapses it by degree in its weight (`cvt2`); **and with the vote held out, the magnitude of 50's OWN step size decides the level — large stalls, small rescues (`cvt4`).**
* **Descriptive, UNSURE:** the level is set in epochs ~15–30; in the two arms where 50 rode a large step size with its vote out (HOLDSHARED, HOLDHIGH) the TEST gap to HEAD opened at epoch 16–17 while their complements were still identical to HEAD's, and the complements then collapsed on MUTE's schedule. The records are consistent with 50's large step size starting the stall and the complement's early collapse following from it — **not tested; 241.12 R1 is the experiment that tests it.**

### 241.4 Three things that bound the result, led with

**(1) No branch bar is near; the stamp-level readings are soft.** The smallest branch margins are DROP13 (4.58 pp under the +5 recovery edge, 5.42 pp over −5), the HEAD − K13@100 premise (6.55 pp over 5) and K33's rise (4.81 pp under +5); RHO is 0.20 over 0.80. But every `LEVEL-HOLDS` and both `FROZEN-AT-PIN` stamps are 0.96–1.34 pp inside READ_BAR 1.384 (1.4–1.9 SE): treat those as locations, not tight nulls.

**(2) K13's `PINNED` is a hover near the floor, not a clamp (DESCRIPTIVE, UNSURE; wording corrected at 241.7).** From epoch ~160 K13's complement stays within ×3 of the floor, and the gate's median r over the last quarter is 1.5146 / 1.6196 / 1.2239. But after its first r ≤ 2 it goes back above r 2 on **74 / 104 / 5** records; its largest later excursions are r 2.744 at epoch 282.6 (s93), r 2.644 at 283.2 (s94; the same float32 value recurs at 293.2 and 293.4 [SUPERSEDED at CORRECTIONS 244: 'recurs at 293.4' — the raw records carry beta −14.027607 at 283.2, 293.2 and 293.4, `results/c244_cvt5_k13_readouts.txt`]) and r 2.191 at 181.6 (s95); **its last records above r 2 are at 292.2 (s93, r 2.12), 299.8 (s94, r 2.59 — the run's final record) and 183.4 (s95, r 2.03)**. It sits at the exact clamp on only 3–6 % of post-pin records; the arm-mean beta rises from −14.95 at epoch 200 to −14.54 at 299 (r ≈ 1.05 → 1.58); s93 is above r 2 on 30 % of its epoch-250–300 records. The complement's DOWN fraction stays near 0.5 in every 50-epoch window from epoch 100 (0.47–0.56). So it is a balanced vote bouncing near the floor: **its step size is small but not frozen**, and "collapsed to the clamp" would be wrong. `UNRESOLVED-NOT-PINNED` was not reached, as registered. The same caution in smaller form: K33-s94 first reached r ≤ 2 at 69.4 (not ~37), never held the exact clamp and has 762 records off it after epoch 100 (max r 1.23), so `K33-EXACT-CLAMP-CONTINUOUS` rests on the ≥ 2-of-3-seeds rule; HEAD's complement sits at the exact clamp on only 0.71–0.79 of its post-pin records (max r 1.04–1.10 after epoch 100).

**(3) The level stopped moving before the pin, as on GroupNorm (231.4(1)).** K13's arm-mean TEST is within 0.5 pp of its @300 level from **epoch 105**; its complement first reaches r ≤ 2 at ~160, when r at epoch 100 was still 15–18 and at 150 still 2.6–3.8. TEST gained +0.31 pp from the 95–99 window to 145–149, then +0.11 to 295–299; per-seed slopes after epoch 150 are ≤ 0.0022 pp per epoch in size. TRAIN kept climbing to ~160 (settle 160; +1.58 pp from 100 to 300). **So `K13-FROZEN-AT-PIN` is true as registered, but "the pin froze the level" is not licensed**; and the scorer's own licence already reads K-DEPENDENT-EQUILIBRIUM with a pinned complement as an equilibrium of the LEVEL, set before the pin — not a settling of the step size [SUPERSEDED at CORRECTIONS 244: 'not a step-size equilibrium' — the phrase is retired, the `cvt5` verifier's fix 5].

### 241.8 What this licenses, and what it does not

**Licensed (238.6's registered text).**
* **(a) `K-DEPENDENT-EQUILIBRIUM` (of the LEVEL).** At 300 epochs K13 is still more than 5 pp above K33's plateau and has not fallen more than 5 pp from its in-run 100-epoch level: **`cvt2`'s `GRADED` is NOT a delay at this horizon; the partial level is K-dependent.** With `K13-COMPLEMENT-PINNED` + `K13-FROZEN-AT-PIN`, the level held through its complement's own collapse — it was set before the pin, as on GN — so it is not a settling of the step size [SUPERSEDED at CORRECTIONS 244: 'so it is not a step-size equilibrium' — the phrase is retired]. [AMENDED at CORRECTIONS 244 (the `cvt5` verifier's fix 5): `K-DEPENDENT-EQUILIBRIUM` is an equilibrium of the LEVEL only, with 231.4(1)'s qualifier — K13's arm-mean TEST settled (within 0.5 pp of its end) from ~epoch 105, and its complement first reached r ≤ 2 ~55 epochs later (159.2–161.4); it says nothing settled about the vote or the step size.] 236.4(1)'s bound ("K13's level may be a delay") is answered at 300 epochs.
* **(b) `RESCUE-SURVIVES`.** HEAD's PlainNet rescue persists to 300 epochs with the 100-epoch control read in the same runs; with `HEAD-COMPLEMENT-PINNED` + `HEAD-FROZEN-AT-PIN` it is `cvh1`'s / `cgn3`'s sentence on PlainNet: the rescue's level survives 236 epochs of its own complement's magnitude pin — a regime, not a delayed collapse. 230.6's "HEAD's own complement pins at 99.8, so nothing past 100 epochs" is answered.
* **(c) `K33-HOLDS-PINNED`.** Over epochs 100–300 K33's complement stays inside the magnitude pin and its level moves < 5 pp: `cvt2`'s exact-clamp departures were excursions within r ≤ 2, not a re-opening.

**Not licensed.** Anything past 300 epochs; a decay slower than 5 pp per 200 epochs (or than READ_BAR over the post-pin window); that the pin froze the level (241.4(3)); that K13's step size is frozen (241.4(2)); any K but 13 and 33 at long horizon; dose vs onset (no time gate); the ceiling (no `kL`); any between-batch contrast; point agreement for floor-band readings; ResNet (BN or GN) or VGG; RULE 11.

### 242.1 Question

`cvt4` (240) held `layer4.1.bn2.weight`'s (idx 50) step size in HEAD's grouping, with its vote out of the complement's sum, and found `OWN-STEP-MAGNITUDE`: on MUTE's large step size (HOLDHIGH) the arm stalls at `k01` (11.13 vs 11.69); at the floor (HOLDLOW) it keeps HEAD's level (65.46 vs 64.73). **240.4(1) bounds it:** in HOLDHIGH the complement's own FREE Lion beta collapsed too, on MUTE's path (pinned at 40.4 vs HEAD's 97.8–99.6), so `P_HIGH` changed 50's step size AND the complement's. Descriptively (UNSURE) the TEST gap passed 2 pp while the two complements still differed by 0.001, which points at the direct route — but nothing had held the complement.

**`cvt6` holds the complement's step size too, and crosses it with 50's: does 50's large step size stall the network by itself (with the complement kept on HEAD's rescuing path), and does the complement's early collapse stall it by itself (with 50 kept small)?**

### 242.2 Design

* **Cell.** `cvt1`'s / `cvt4`'s exactly: CIFAR-100, `PlainNet18_c100` (53 tensors, 11,046,308 params), SGDm (0.99, wd 0.1) + Lion meta (0.99, b2 0.9, wd 0), ms 1e-3, alpha0 1e-6, 100 ep, batch 100, `AUGMENT=1`, `BETA_CLIP=-15:-2.3026`, `PROBE=100`, `PROBE_TENSOR=1`. The ENV line is `cvt1`'s / `cvt4`'s byte for byte.
* **Isolated tree.** `$WS/harness_cvt6/cifar10`, built by `bin/cVT6_stage_harness.sh --stage` (NEW): every file of `cvt4`'s tree byte-identical (9 files, `data` a symlink to the same live target) except `Optimizers/HF.py` = `cvt4`'s HF.py (`84b345ad…`, kept as `HF.py.pre_comphold`) + `PATCH_COMPHOLD` = **`f1b9c8aa…2edd2e`**, plus `Optimizers/cvt6_headpath.json` (`74be71fa…`, the replay) and `Optimizers/cvt6_testdown.json` (`ae17432f…`, read ONLY by the tests; no launcher line carries it, guard 6). Runner `$WS/jobs/run_cifar_cvt6.sh` (`9aa2ed5c…`) differs from `run_cifar.sh` in exactly its `cd` line (V-d). `cvt4`'s and `cvt1`'s trees are not written (verified before and after; V-g runs `cvt4`'s `tests/test_betahold.py` B0 UNEDITED on the base).
* **ONE submission, 21 jobs = 7 arms × seeds {96, 97, 98}** (pre-assigned; zero corpus rows, zero `.out` ARGS lines, zero `sacct` jobs carry them — guards 1c4, 2c, 2d, 2e).

| arm | `--stepsize-groups` | `BETA_HOLD` (50, group 1) | `COMP_HOLD` (the 52-tensor complement, group 0) | cell |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `k01` | `scalar` | unset | unset | floor anchor |
| HEAD | `sets:1-49,51-53/layer4.1.bn2.weight` | unset | unset | positive control (byte-identical to `cvt1`–`cvt4`) |
| HOLDLOW | HEAD's | `layer4.1.bn2.weight:floor` | unset (Lion) | LOW × FREE — `cvt4` replicate |
| HOLDHIGH | HEAD's | `layer4.1.bn2.weight:tri:9428` | unset (Lion) | HIGH × FREE — `cvt4` replicate |
| **HIGHHEADPATH** | HEAD's | `layer4.1.bn2.weight:tri:9428` | `rec:cvt6_headpath` | HIGH × HEADPATH (decisive) |

| **LOWHEADPATH** | HEAD's | `layer4.1.bn2.weight:floor` | `rec:cvt6_headpath` | LOW × HEADPATH (COMP_HOLD positive control) |

* **CO-PRIMARY** (in batch; plateau5 from each run's own `.out`; TRAIN beside TEST; each bounded in neither direction): **`P_50` = LOWHEADPATH − HIGHHEADPATH** (50's magnitude, the complement's step size bitwise identical: the DIRECT route) and **`P_C` = LOWHEADPATH − LOWMUTEPATH** (the complement's path, 50 bitwise identical at the floor: the VIA-COMPLEMENT route). **KEY:** `D_HEAD` = HEAD − `k01`; `P_CTLC` = HEAD − LOWHEADPATH; `R_LOW` = HOLDLOW − HEAD and `R_HIGH` = HEAD − HOLDHIGH (`cvt4`'s, replicated); `D_<arm>`. **DESCRIPTIVE:** `P_INT` = `P_50` − (LOWMUTEPATH − HOLDHIGH), with HOLDHIGH standing in for HIGH × MUTEPATH (its complement free, 242.3(3)).
* **Arm names carry no hyphen.** Seven arms, not the brief's six: LOWHEADPATH is the complement hold's positive control (242.3(4)); cost 242.8.

### 242.3 Five decisions, taken from landed records (`analysis/cvt6_registration_derivations.py`, NEW, `ec412783…`; output `c17e4b82…` on cluster_b)

**(1) MUTEPATH is a closed form: `tri:9428`.** 237.3 showed every landed MUTE / MUTE50 shared beta is a max-rate triangle; RULE P re-run on this host gives **P_HIGH 9428** (P_HEAD 5041, P_K01 8437). Against `v_9428` the six MUTE runs miss by 0.030–0.254 (mean 0.007–0.054), and **`cvt4`'s three HOLDHIGH free complements by 0.064 / 0.160 / 0.080** (mean 0.015–0.034; peaks −4.448 / −4.354 / −4.494 at 18.8–19.0, clamp 40.4). So MUTEPATH needs no replay file; it is the same integer the 50-hold already uses, and HIGH × MUTEPATH forced would put the same schedule on both groups.

**(2) HEADPATH is an exact replay file, not a closed form.** HEAD's complement beta (12 landed 100-epoch HEAD runs, cvt1 s78–80, cvt2 s87–89, cvt3 s84–86, cvt4 s90–92 [CORRECTED at CORRECTIONS 246: 12 of the 15 landed 100-epoch HEAD runs at this cell with probe records — `cpl2` HEAD s75–77 were omitted, although the derivation's docstring says 'every landed 100-epoch HEAD run at this cell'; the 15-run median differs by at most 0.1601 log units, mean 0.0100 (246.9); the registration stays valid, because the replay file is what was registered and bitten]) rises at the maximum rate from b0 to a peak of −4.826 … −4.978 at epoch 17.8–18.0 (deviation from the pure rise ≤ 0.078), falls at the maximum rate to ≈ −5.8 by epoch 20, then drifts: −6.81 … −6.93 at 30, −7.68 … −7.98 at 40, −9.28 … −10.09 at 50, −12.17 … −13.48 at 60, −15.00 by 80; r ≤ 2 for good from epoch 62.2–66.0 (the exact clamp at 96.4–99.8). **The best max-rate triangle misses every run by 4.210–4.530 log units somewhere** (S1). A hand-built closed form would be a fit with free knots; the brief's alternative is taken.
* **RULE H (written in the derivation's docstring before any `cvt6` run).** For record index k = 0..499 (step 100k, written after meta update n = 100k + 2): v_k = the median over the 12 runs [CORRECTED at CORRECTIONS 246: the 12 named above, not every eligible run — see the bracket above and 246.9] of the record's complement beta (python double; the mean of the 6th and 7th values), n_k = 100k + 2. The file stores `{id, rule, source, n, v}` as sorted-key compact JSON (10,828 bytes, **sha `74be71fa524ad0122d1408e01dd2b633b004b2e27228393fe6e593f494358a5d`**). **cvt5's three HEAD runs are held OUT** (300-epoch runs) and serve as the out-of-sample check with `cvt4`'s HOLDLOW and HOLDHEAD complements.
* **The schedule the patch applies** (`_ch_value`, and the scorer's `rec_value`, the same arithmetic in the same order): hold_c(n) = b0 for n < n_0 = 2 (update 1 is Lion's no-op); v_k + (v_{k+1} − v_k)(n − n_k)/100 for n_k ≤ n < n_{k+1}; v_last = −15 for n ≥ 49,902; clamped and stored into float32.
* **The tolerance, stated and proved.** (a) At all 500 record steps the applied float32 value is within **4.77e-7** of the measured median (selftest A; the patch's float32 value equals the scorer's at every n in 0..50,001, test C3, 0 mismatches). (b) Between records the schedule is linear; every source trajectory moves by at most 100 ms = 0.1 log units between two records (measured 0.1000004, float32 accumulation), so the schedule is within 0.1 log units of the piecewise-exact median path at every update. (c) Against individual runs the spread is reported, not hidden: max |record − schedule| **0.160–1.019 in-sample** (mean 0.019–0.129) and **0.195–1.352 out-of-sample** (cvt5 HEAD 0.547 / 1.017 / 0.591; cvt4 HOLDLOW 0.703 / 1.352 / 0.374; cvt4 HOLDHEAD 0.525 / 0.195 / 0.424). Window means r = e^(β+15): schedule 8,632 (epochs 15–30) / 1,021 (30–60) / 1.52 (60–100); in-sample runs 8,412–8,782 / 967–1,106 / 1.14–1.98. The schedule reaches r ≤ 2 for good at epoch 64.8 (runs 62.2–66.0).
* **How far the two complement paths are apart** (the contrast the design makes; schedule values): equal to within 0.04 through epoch 18 (both max-rate rises); HEADPATH below MUTEPATH at epoch 20 (−5.81 vs −4.96, r ratio 0.43); above from ~22: +0.99 at 25, +3.08 at 30 (r ×22), **+7.10 at 40 (r ×1,210)**, +5.33 at 50, +2.30 at 60; equal (the floor) from ~66. They first differ by > 0.1 at epoch 18.2 [CORRECTED at CORRECTIONS 246: update 9,036 = epoch 18.07, read independently by the `cvt6` score stage (18.1) and its verifier]. r over epochs 30–60: 1,021 vs 11.4.

**(3) HIGH × MUTEPATH forced is not run.** It is predicted at `k01` under every account (DIRECT, VIA-COMPLEMENT, BOTH-NEEDED, EITHER-SUFFICES all stall with 50 HIGH and a collapsing complement; so does COMP-HOLD-BREAKS), so it separates no two accounts; its information is carried by HOLDHIGH, whose free complement already rides MUTEPATH within 0.16. Its only use would be a forced-forced interaction term; `P_INT` is printed as DESCRIPTIVE with HOLDHIGH in its place. Saving: 3 runs (≈2.0–2.5 GPU-h).

**(4) The complement hold's positive control: LOWHEADPATH, not the brief's HEAD × HEADPATH — justified and priced.** Every forced arm replaces the complement's responsive Lion beta by an exogenous replay. If that breaks the rescue by itself, neither decisive arm speaks to a route (the COMP-HOLD-BREAKS account). Both candidate controls are predicted at HEAD under every mechanism account and at `k01` only under COMP-HOLD-BREAKS, and both cost 3 runs (≈2.0–2.5 GPU-h). LOWHEADPATH is registered because (i) it shares 50's level (LOW, bitwise the floor) with LOWMUTEPATH and the complement's schedule (HEADPATH, bitwise) with HIGHHEADPATH, so each co-primary is a single-factor contrast between two fully exogenous arms; (ii) HEAD × HEADPATH would leave 50's Lion responding to a network whose complement is forced — a closed loop no decisive arm has — and shares no factor level with either decisive arm; (iii) `cvt4` already showed an exogenous 50 is harmless (HOLDLOW, HOLDHEAD at HEAD), so the untested piece is the complement hold, which LOWHEADPATH isolates. Running both was considered: +3 runs ≈ +2.1–2.5 GPU-h (21 → 24 jobs, ≈15.8–19.9 GPU-h expected), for a control that answers the same null; not run. PATCH_COMPHOLD requires BETA_HOLD on (floor or tri), so a 50-free complement hold would also need another patch mode (242.9).

**(5) The meta-optimiser's state (Lion momentum), stated exactly.** `Lion_meta_update` runs unchanged on the whole beta 2-vector (elementwise sign, momentum ← 0.99·momentum + 0.01·z), then PATCH_CLIP's clamp, then PATCH_BETAHOLD overwrites beta[0][1], and only then PATCH_COMPHOLD overwrites beta[0][0]. So (i) in HOLDLOW / HOLDHIGH nothing changes from `cvt4` (COMP_HOLD unset is bitwise `cvt4`'s tree, 242.4); (ii) in the three forced arms NO applied beta depends on z or on momentum: both momentum entries keep the unpatched recursion on their own raw z and are DEAD STATE (their only reader is their own Lion step, overwritten on the same update, from init to the last update, no release) — the step sizes the network receives are an open-loop function of the update count; (iii) the gradients, h and z still depend on the network, so the momentum VALUES differ from any free run's; they are never read. **`tests/test_comphold.py` C4 proves it BITWISE** over 3,000 updates of synthetic z for all three registered strings, a test `tri:100` and the test replay: the whole momentum vector equals the `cvt4`-tree object's (same BETA_HOLD, COMP_HOLD unset); 50's beta equals it too (COMP_HOLD writes nothing on group 1); the complement's beta equals the schedule after every update; `_ch_nat` equals what Lion wrote and `_ch_active` counts exactly the differing updates (1,560–2,125); and **a second patched object driven by a DIFFERENT z stream holds bitwise-identical beta at every update**. On the real path, RR4 checks that the applied beta vector at every record IS the pair of schedules.

### 242.4 The patch, its inertness and its bite (proved BEFORE launch)

**`patches/patch_comphold.py`** (NEW, `7a90b728…`) applies on top of `cvt4`'s HF.py and makes FOUR insertions, editing no existing line:
1. a guarded `self._ch_apply()` in `step()`, right after PATCH_BETAHOLD's guarded `_bh_apply` region and before `self._probe(...)`;
2. one `self._ch_init(net_param_names_and_size)` call right after `init_meta`'s `_bh_init` call;
3. a guarded `self._ch_attach(rec)` in `_probe`, right after PATCH_BETAHOLD's `_bh_attach` region and before `_pt_attach`;
4. five new `_ch_` methods, right after PATCH_BETAHOLD's method block and before `check_required_attributes`.

How it behaves:
* **OFF.** `COMP_HOLD` unset or empty → prints `COMP_HOLD: off`, `_ch_on` False; no tensor touched, no probe key added.
* **ON.** `tri:<P>` (PATCH_BETAHOLD's triangle on group 0) or `rec:<id>` (the JSON `<dir of HF.py>/<id>.json`, lists `n` strictly increasing ints ≥ 1 and `v` finite floats inside the clamp, `id` matching). Holds the OTHER group of BETA_HOLD's 2-group grouping; applies hold_c(0) at init; after every update records the value Lion + clamp wrote (`ch_nat`), overwrites it, counts the updates where they differed (`ch_active`). Each probe record of a forced run gains `ch_n`, `ch_active`, `ch_nat`, `ch_held` after the `bh_*` keys.
* **Loud.** A malformed value (22 forms tested, C2), a missing / non-JSON / decreasing / out-of-clamp / one-knot / float-n / NaN / wrong-id replay file, BETA_HOLD off, BETA_HOLD `shared`, or a grouping with other than 2 groups → ValueError. PATCH_BETAHOLD's own premises (blockwise, Lion, BETA_CLIP, no VOTE_W, no HIER, no tn:) hold because it must be on.
* **Witness line on every run**, prefix deliberately NOT starting with `BETA_HOLD` (so `corpus_exclusions.py`'s KINDS, which collect lines by prefix, see exactly `cvt4`'s BETA_HOLD lines): `COMP_HOLD: off`, or `COMP_HOLD: on type=blockwise group=0 groupsize=52 mode=tri P=9428 b0=-13.815510749816895 ms=0.001 lo=-15.0 hi=-2.3026 peak=-4.387510749816894` (141 chars), or `COMP_HOLD: on type=blockwise group=0 groupsize=52 mode=rec id=cvt6_headpath sha256=74be71fa524ad0122d1408e01dd2b633b004b2e27228393fe6e593f494358a5d knots=500 n0=2 n1=49902 b0=-13.815510749816895 lo=-15.0 hi=-2.3026 vmax=-4.852388381958008 vlast=-15.0` (250 chars) — **the replay file's sha256 rides the witness**, so `G-CHOLDW` pins the replayed numbers per run.

| proof | where | result |
|---|---|---|
| **Structure** (`tests/test_comphold.py` C0): the four regions appear as registered; **deleting them reproduces `HF.py.pre_comphold` (= `cvt4`'s HF.py) BYTE FOR BYTE**; exactly five new `_ch_` methods, directly after the six `_bh_`; every pre-existing method present in order. Also `cvt4`'s `tests/test_betahold.py` B0, UNEDITED, on `HF.py.pre_betahold` → `HF.py.pre_comphold` | stage V-f / V-g; launcher guards 4b1 / 4b2 | 11 / 0 and 10 / 0 |
| **CPU, live PlainNet** (C1–C5, on cluster_b's login node, CPU only, `~/l242_logs/test_comphold_login.log` `b925fa16…`, and again inside the GPU job): each arm prints exactly its BETA_HOLD witness (`cvt4`'s lines), its COMP_HOLD witness and `VOTE_W: off`, with the registered initial beta; COMP_HOLD unset and EMPTY leave every attribute and beta EQUAL to the `cvt4`-tree object's on k01, HEAD, HOLDLOW and HOLDHIGH; 22 malformed forms raise (bad files in a TEMP COPY of HF.py's directory — the tree is never written); the patch's schedules == the scorer's at every n in 0..50,001; C4 as 242.3(5) | `$WS/runs/cvt6/inertness_comphold.log` | **93 / 0**, `TEST_COMPHOLD_RC 0` |
| **GPU, REAL run** (`tests/test_comphold_realrun.py`, job `cvt6inert` **5022457**, [HOST_3c1b003035] RTX 2080 Ti, **10 min 53 s**, imports `cvt1`'s registered `tests/test_voteweight_realrun.py` UNEDITED — train.py's own parse_args, build_network, build_optimizer, load_data, CIFAR-100, AUGMENT=1, seed 96, 300 steps, PROBE every 10, PROBE_TENSOR=1, cudnn deterministic, one process per variant; the unpatched tree is `cvt4`'s, read-only). **RR0** unpatched vs itself bitwise. **RR1 OFF** (COMP_HOLD unset AND empty, on k01, HEAD, HOLDLOW and HOLDHIGH, each with its own BETA_HOLD) == `cvt4`'s tree: beta every step, loss every step, probe.jsonl bytes, every final parameter and buffer, BITWISE; each printed `COMP_HOLD: off`, its `cvt4` BETA_HOLD witness and `VOTE_W: off`. **RR2** each of the three exact strings and two test-only strings (LOW + `tri:100`; HIGH + `rec:cvt6_testdown`): one witness line of each kind == the scorer's; **beta[0] AND beta[1] after EVERY one of 300 steps == the registered schedules (0 bad)**; at every record both groups on schedule in beta and beta_pre and the `bh_*` / `ch_*` records audit (`ch_active` 100 / 124 / 100 / 234 / 237). **RR3** the test strings' complement departs from `cvt4`'s same-BETA_HOLD free complement by ≥ 0.090 (`tri:100`) and ≥ 0.354 (testdown) from step 150, `ch_active` > 0; the registered strings' complements differ from `cvt4`'s free ones on 298 / 300 steps by ≤ 6.6e-3–1.0e-2 (both rise at the maximum rate in 300 steps; float32 accumulation vs the double-precision schedule), reported non-gating. **RR4** at every real record of the three registered strings the applied beta vector IS the pair of schedules, bitwise | same log | **70 / 0, ALL PASS, `REALRUN_RC 0`**; whole log **163 / 0**, `217e6779…` |

* **Limit, disclosed (as 237.4).** In 300 steps both registered complement schedules coincide with the free complement's max-rate rise, so for the three registered strings non-vacuity on the real path reaches beta and the probe record to float32 rounding only (and HIGHHEADPATH's / LOWHEADPATH's final weights differ from `cvt4`'s HOLDHIGH / HOLDLOW, non-gating); the departure of the `rec:` and `tri:` modes from a free complement is shown by the two test strings. Over 100 epochs the departures are the several log units of 242.3(2), and `G-BITE`'s non-vacuity (242.6) is established on 100-epoch landed records.
* **One first attempt failed, in the TEST, and was fixed before the GPU job.** On the login node the CPU test stopped at C1 with `AttributeError: 'HF' object has no attribute 'param_groups_indices'` on the `scalar` spec (k01 has no groups). The comparison now reads the attribute with `getattr(…, None)` on both objects; no assertion changed. The same pass also moved C2's bad replay files from the tree's `Optimizers/` directory to a temp copy of HF.py, so no test ever writes the tree.
* **The live shared harness, `cvt1`'s and `cvt4`'s trees are unchanged.** `~/l242_hashes.sh` (`f717e02e…`, a copy of `l237_hashes.sh` that also covers `cvt4`'s tree, its runner and STAGE-MANIFEST) wrote `~/l242_logs/live_hashes_before.txt` (59 lines, `fe462d1d…`) before staging; re-taken after staging and after the tests (`cmp` identical both times) and after launch (242.13).

**`G-BITE` non-vacuity, shown on LANDED records (derivation S4; scorer selftest B re-runs it on the host).** Each forced arm's BROKEN-COMP_HOLD null is the landed FREE complement of its `cvt4` twin. Read against the schedule it must pass, **cvt4 HOLDHIGH's complement misses HEADPATH on 340 / 500 records (max 7.118–7.124); cvt4 HOLDLOW's misses MUTEPATH on 360–388 (max 7.122–7.242) and HEADPATH on 364–391 (max 0.374–1.352)**, beta_pre alike; even the 12 SOURCE runs of the median miss it by ≥ 0.160 somewhere. Minimum over the nulls: 0.3742, 37,420 × BH_TOL. Read as controls or as their own arms: **all 24 landed `k01` / HEAD runs (cvt1–cvt4) PASS the Lion half; the 6 landed `cvt4` HOLDLOW / HOLDHIGH runs PASS G-BITE as `cvt6`'s HOLDLOW / HOLDHIGH; the 9 free twins read as their forced arms pass 50's schedule and FAIL the complement's (9 / 9); every landed HEAD run read as each of the 5 held arms FAILS (60 / 60).** The free complement of every landed HOLDLOW / HOLDHIGH record is Lion recomputed from its own record (0 mismatches of 3,000).

### 242.5 Accounts and the floor table (164.6) — every arm, every account (UNSURE)

Anchors (between batch, non-gating): `cvt4` `k01` 11.69, HEAD 64.73, HOLDLOW 65.46, HOLDHIGH 11.13. Intervals K01_PL 8–16, FREE_PL 56–72, PART_PL 20–50. Every account predicts `k01` 8–16, HEAD 56–72, HOLDLOW 56–72, HOLDHIGH 8–16 (the replicates).

| account | HIGHHEADPATH | LOWMUTEPATH | LOWHEADPATH | `P_50` | `P_C` | branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **DIRECT** (50's large step size stalls by itself; the complement's collapse is a consequence) | **8–16** | 56–72 | 56–72 | +40…+64 | −16…+16 | `DIRECT` |
| **VIA-COMPLEMENT** (the stall runs through the complement's early collapse; 50 only triggers it) | 56–72 | **8–16** | 56–72 | −16…+16 | +40…+64 | `VIA-COMPLEMENT` |
| **BOTH-NEEDED** (only 50 HIGH with the complement collapsed stalls — HOLDHIGH) | 56–72 | 56–72 | 56–72 | −16…+16 | −16…+16 | `BOTH-NEEDED` |
| **EITHER-SUFFICES** (each route stalls alone) | **8–16** | **8–16** | 56–72 | +40…+64 | +40…+64 | `EITHER-SUFFICES` |
| **GRADED** (each route carries part) | 20–50 | 20–50 | 56–72 | +6…+52 | +6…+52 | `GRADED` |
| **COMP-HOLD-BREAKS** (forcing the complement onto any replay breaks the rescue) | 8–16 | 8–16 | **8–16** | −8…+8 | −8…+8 | `COMP-HOLD-CONTROL-FAILED` |
| **BROKEN-PATCH (null)** (COMP_HOLD never bites: each forced arm = its free twin) | 8–16 | 56–72 | 56–72 | = DIRECT on every arm | | reaches NO branch: `PATCH-NOT-VERIFIED` |

* **Asserted in selftest D.** The lowest level any account predicts for any arm is 8 pp (7.0 above chance). Every co-primary's interval sits ≥ 25 pp inside ±99 under every account. HEAD is predicted ≥ 40 pp off `k01` under every account. Every account's midpoint lands in its registered branch; the six non-null accounts' midpoints land in six different branches.
* **DIRECT and the BROKEN-PATCH null predict identically on every arm: declared.** A COMP_HOLD that never bit would leave HIGHHEADPATH = HOLDHIGH and LOWMUTEPATH = LOWHEADPATH = HOLDLOW — exactly DIRECT. Only `G-BITE` separates them; every other account differs from the null by level on at least one forced arm. **This is the account the descriptive reading of 240.4(1) leans to (UNSURE), which is why `G-BITE` reads the complement's schedule at every record, in beta and beta_pre, before any level.**
* **No numeric prior is registered.** 240.4(1)'s timing (the TEST gap passed 2 pp at epoch 16 with the complements 0.001 apart) leans DIRECT; nothing in the landed records bounds VIA-COMPLEMENT or EITHER-SUFFICES, and the two complement schedules are themselves within 0.04 until epoch 18 — so if the damage is done before epoch 18, `P_C` is predicted near 0 under every account but EITHER-SUFFICES / VIA-COMPLEMENT acting later. UNSURE.
* **Floor readings are bounds.** Arms predicted at `k01` sit on the clamp-frozen level (`FLOOR-READINGS-ARE-BOUNDS`); a reading at `k01` is a location.

### 242.6 Gates, branches and what each licenses — `decide()`, first match wins; frozen bars

**Harness gates (→ `HARNESS-UNSOUND`, rc 1).** `G-ARGS` (each run's own single ARGS line: spec, net, cell, 18 fixed flags, seed, run-name); `G-ENV` (one ENV line == `cvt1`'s / `cvt4`'s; one `PROBE_TENSOR: on every=100 type=<arm's> tensors=53`); `G-VOTEW` (exactly one `VOTE_W: off`); `G-HOLDW` (exactly one `BETA_HOLD` line == the arm's witness, `cvt4`'s strings: `off` ×2 arms, floor ×3, tri 9428 ×2); **`G-CHOLDW`** (exactly one `COMP_HOLD` line == the arm's witness: `off` ×4, rec ×2 (250 chars, carrying the replay sha), tri ×1 (141 chars)); `G-STRUCT` (manifest byte-identical to the scorer's, 5,922 bytes, `c519c253…`, with the `REPLAY … HEADPATH cvt6_headpath SHA256 74be71fa… KNOTS 500` line and the BETAHOLD / COMPHOLD / WITNESS / CWITNESS tables); `G-PROV` (MODE submit; build_network `e65e6773…`; **HF `f1b9c8aa…`**; **RUNNER `9aa2ed5c…`**; **REPLAY `74be71fa…`**; SCORER == the file); **`G-REPLAY`** (the replay file the scorer reads has the registered sha and 500 knots); `G-FLOOR`/`G-CEIL` (max arm mean in 15–90).

**`G-BITE` (→ `PATCH-NOT-VERIFIED`, rc 1; before any level)**, from `runs/cvt6/probe_cvt6-<arm>-s<seed>/probe.jsonl`, on every finite record:
* (a) 500 parseable records at steps 0, 100, …, 49,900 with beta, beta_pre, mom_pre and z_agg per group;
* (b) **every UNHELD group follows Lion** within 1e-5: all groups of `k01` and HEAD; group 0 of HOLDLOW and HOLDHIGH; ties at rounding level counted, not judged;
* (c) **the schedules**: group 1 of every held arm (beta[1] == hold(step+2) and beta_pre[1] == hold(step+1)), and **group 0 of every forced arm** (beta[0] == hold_c(step+2) and beta_pre[0] == hold_c(step+1)) — the beta_pre halves catch a hold that acted only at probe steps;
* (d) **the patches' own records, audited**: `bh_n` / `ch_n` == step+2; `bh_nat` / `ch_nat` == Lion recomputed from the record's own group-1 / group-0 `beta_pre` / `mom_pre` / `z_agg`; `bh_held` == beta[1], `ch_held` == beta[0]; the `_active` counters non-decreasing, ≤ the update count, ≥ the records where nat ≠ held;
* (e) `k01` and HEAD carry no `bh_*` or `ch_*` key; HOLDLOW and HOLDHIGH carry no `ch_*` key.
* No minimum on either `_active` counter (as 237.6): a replay close to what Lion would do overrides few updates; the separation from the null is (c), non-vacuous by 242.4.
* **Selftest E breaks, each confirmed to fail for its own reason** (a scratch reader printed the failing half): every forced complement unheld at DIRECT's levels (complement schedule 342–413 records, `ch` audit); unheld but carrying `ch_*` keys (schedule); 50 unheld on a forced arm (50's schedule, `bh` audit); HIGHHEADPATH carrying MUTEPATH and LOWMUTEPATH carrying HEADPATH (complement schedule 340–341); LOWHEADPATH carrying `tri:9428` on 50 (50's schedule 201); complement or 50 held only at probe steps (beta_pre 500); HOLDHIGH's free complement touched (Lion 500); `ch_nat` / `bh_nat` forged; `ch_n` off by one; HOLDLOW carrying `ch_*` keys; plus a control carrying `bh_*` keys, `k01`'s Lion broken, garbled / missing / short files.

**Branches.** `UNRESOLVED-DIVERGED` (a seed range > 5) → `SCALAR-NOT-COLLAPSED` (`k01` > 20) → `POSITIVE-CONTROL-FAILED` (HEAD − `k01` < 20). Then per held arm, state = **AT-HEAD** iff L ≥ HEAD − 5, **AT-K01** iff L ≤ `k01` + 2 (below included), else **BETWEEN**:

| order | condition | branch | what it does to 240's `OWN-STEP-MAGNITUDE` and its bound 240.4(1) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | LOWHEADPATH AT-K01 | **`COMP-HOLD-CONTROL-FAILED`** | untested: forcing the complement onto a replay breaks the rescue by itself; no route sentence |
| 2 | LOWHEADPATH BETWEEN | `COMP-HOLD-CONTROL-PARTIAL` | untested; stop |
| 3 | HOLDLOW not AT-HEAD, or HOLDHIGH not AT-K01 | **`REPLICATE-FAILED`** | `OWN-STEP-MAGNITUDE` PUT IN QUESTION by a failed replication at new seeds (not rescinded); no route sentence |
| 4 | HIGHHEADPATH AT-K01, LOWMUTEPATH AT-HEAD | **`DIRECT`** | **the bound CLOSES in the DIRECT direction**: 50's own large step size stalls PlainNet by itself; the complement's early collapse is a consequence, not a necessary route. Not licensed: why; which window; a dose curve; that no other complement path stalls; any other tensor / network / horizon |
| 5 | HIGHHEADPATH AT-HEAD, LOWMUTEPATH AT-K01 | **`VIA-COMPLEMENT`** | **the bound CLOSES in the VIA direction**: the stall runs through the complement's collapse; `OWN-STEP-MAGNITUDE` keeps its text with the rider "via the complement's step size". Not licensed: how 50 drives the collapse |
| 6 | HIGHHEADPATH AT-HEAD, LOWMUTEPATH AT-HEAD | **`BOTH-NEEDED`** | REFINED: an interaction — neither route stalls alone. Not licensed: that forcing both reproduces HOLDHIGH (not run) |
| 7 | HIGHHEADPATH AT-K01, LOWMUTEPATH AT-K01 | **`EITHER-SUFFICES`** | two sufficient routes; `OWN-STEP-MAGNITUDE` stands and the complement's collapse is also sufficient. Not licensed: which acts in HOLDHIGH |
| 8 | otherwise (a decisive arm BETWEEN) | **`GRADED`** | partly resolved; the two states are stamped; no single-route sentence |

* **Frozen bars (O2)** — `cvt4`'s, unchanged: GAP_MIN 20.0 (35.27 SE), K01_MAX 20.0, MATCH 5.0 (8.82 SE), NULL 2.0 (3.53 SE), RESCUE 10.0 (TRAIN agreement only), DIVERGED 5.0, FLOOR_MIN 15.0, CEIL_MAX 90.0; G-BITE: BH_TOL 1e-5, TIE_REL 1e-12, N_RECORDS 500.
* **Stamps.** Always: `HARNESS-CLEAN`, `PATCH-BITES`, `HOLD-FROM-INIT`, `MUTEPATH-MAX-RATE-TRIANGLE`, `HEADPATH-REPLAY-FILE`, `FORCED-ARMS-OPEN-LOOP`, `ONE-NETWORK-PLAINNET`, `HORIZON-100-ONLY`, `SIGMA-PRIOR-FROZEN`/`-INBATCH`. Conditional: `POSITIVE-CONTROL-REPRODUCES`; `<ARM>-AT-HEAD`/`-BETWEEN`/`-AT-K01` for the five held arms; `<ARM>-ABOVE-HEAD`; `<ARM>-BELOW-K01`; `NONFINITE-<ARM>`; `FLOOR-READINGS-ARE-BOUNDS`; `TRAIN-AGREES`/`-DISAGREES`.
* **After FINAL, descriptive and unable to move it:** per run the complement's and 50's beta peak, pin epoch, r(15–30) and r(30–60), `bh_active` and `ch_active`; arm-mean TEST (TRAIN) at epoch lines 9 / 14 / 15 / 16 / 17 / 18 / 19 / 24 / 29 / 39 / 49 / 99; the first epoch line from which LOWHEADPATH − HIGHHEADPATH, LOWHEADPATH − LOWMUTEPATH and HEAD − HOLDHIGH stay > 2 pp (the timing question of 240.4(1), now with the complement held).

### 242.9 Deviations from the brief and limits, disclosed

* **LOWHEADPATH instead of HEAD × HEADPATH as the complement-hold positive control** (242.3(4)), same price; PATCH_COMPHOLD cannot hold the complement with 50 free (it requires BETA_HOLD on in floor or tri mode), so HEAD × HEADPATH would need another mode. Running both: +2.1–2.5 GPU-h, not taken.
* **Seven arms; HIGH × MUTEPATH forced not run** (242.3(3)). The interaction term is descriptive.
* **The extension is a new ENV spelling and a new patch, not a change to PATCH_BETAHOLD.** `COMP_HOLD` (not `BETA_HOLD_C`) so no prefix reader of BETA_HOLD lines sees a new line; PATCH_BETAHOLD's regions and methods are byte-untouched (V-g).
* **HEADPATH is the MEDIAN of 12 runs** [CORRECTED at CORRECTIONS 246: 12 of the 15 eligible — `cpl2` HEAD s75–77 omitted; the 15-run median differs by ≤ 0.1601 log units, mean 0.0100 (246.9)], not any run's trajectory: individual runs miss it by 0.16–1.02 (in-sample) and 0.20–1.35 (out-of-sample), mostly in the steep 50–66-epoch descent where the per-run pin epochs spread over 3.8 epochs. The replay's r windows sit inside the runs' (242.3(2)).
* **Linear interpolation between records.** Between two records the schedule is a straight line, while a Lion trajectory moves by ±ms per update; the difference is ≤ 0.1 log units by construction, and the schedule is not Lion-realizable (it can move by less than ms per update).
* **Open loop.** In the forced arms neither step size responds to the network at all; this is a stronger intervention than `cvt4`'s single hold. A stall in HIGHHEADPATH could in principle also come from the loss of the complement's responsiveness together with 50's large step size; LOWHEADPATH controls responsiveness only at 50 LOW. UNSURE; stated.
* **No time gate, no dose curve**, on either factor (as 240.4(2)); 241.12 R3 remains the experiment for that.
* **The float32 schedule is exact; Lion's accumulation is not** (as 237.9): the complement's max-rate rise in a free run and the replay's differ by float rounding (≤ 1.0e-2 in 300 real steps, RR3).
* **The `corpus_exclusions --check` gap for the second witness** (242.7) is owed to landing, not solved.
* **The stage holds more than this registration.** `~/stage_cvt6` was rsync'd from the shared working copy (which also holds `cvt7`'s uncommitted files and the fix track's 244); the launcher and scorer read none of them; at launch the files guard 1b names are compared with `git show HEAD:<path>`.

### 243.1 Question

`cvt4` (240) on `PlainNet18_c100`: with idx 50's vote OUT of the complement's sum, 50 on a large step size (a replay of MUTE's collapsing shared trajectory) stalls at `k01`; at the floor, or on HEAD's own small trajectory, it keeps HEAD's rescue.  240's sentence: **the rescue needs the carrier on a SMALL step size**.  All of `cvt1`–`cvt5` are `ONE-NETWORK-PLAINNET`.  **`cvt7` asks whether that sentence holds on `ResNet18_c100`, the network the count-matched partition audit is about**, by holding the step size of ISO's carrier group directly, with the carriers' vote kept out of the complement's sum (ISO's grouping).

### 243.2 What ISO is, re-derived (not quoted)

* **Cell.** `ciso1`'s exactly: CIFAR-100, `ResNet18_c100` (62 tensors, 11,220,132 params), SGDm (0.99, wd 0.1) + Lion meta (0.99, b2 0.9, wd 0), ms 1e-3, alpha0 1e-6, 100 epochs, batch 100, `AUGMENT=1`, `BETA_CLIP=-15:-2.3026`, `PROBE=100`, `PROBE_TENSOR=1`; the ENV line is `ciso1`'s / `cdep1`'s byte for byte.

On cluster_b today: live HF.py `4732b74a…`, build_network.py `c7998883…`, train.py `3fea309e…`, build_optimizer.py `25a899b3…`, load_data.py `b52b58a3…`, run_cifar.sh `a0d0a1b9…`.
* **Levels at this cell (between batch, non-gating).** `k01` 23.2807 (`ciso1`), 23.3520 (`cdep1`); ISO 70.2113, 70.0440.  **`k01` does not sit near chance on ResNet** (PlainNet's `k01` ≈ 11.5): K01_MAX is 30 here, not 20 (243.6).

### 243.4 The patch, its inertness and its bite (proved BEFORE launch)

**`patches/patch_grouphold.py`** (NEW, `691d2f3f…`) applies on top of `cvt4`'s HF.py (`84b345ad…`) and makes FOUR insertions, editing no existing line: a guarded `_gh_apply()` right after PATCH_BETAHOLD's guarded apply (after the clamp, before `_probe`); one `_gh_init` call right after `_bh_init`; a guarded `_gh_attach(rec)` after PATCH_BETAHOLD's attach, before `_pt_attach`; five `_gh_` methods before `check_required_attributes`.
* **OFF.** `GROUP_HOLD` unset or empty → prints `GROUP_HOLD: off`; nothing touched; no probe key.
* **ON.** `<name>[+<name>...]:floor | …:tri:<P>`; the names must be in model order, each once, and together EXACTLY the membership of one group of a blockwise grouping; the same `tri` formula as PATCH_BETAHOLD; after every update it records what Lion + clamp wrote (`gh_nat`), overwrites it, counts differing updates (`gh_active`); records gain `gh_n`, `gh_active`, `gh_nat`, `gh_held`.  The held group's Lion momentum keeps its unpatched recursion and is dead state (the 237.3 statement, re-proved bitwise in G4).
* **Loud.** Malformed value, unknown / repeated / out-of-order name, a partial set, a superset, the complement's member, non-blockwise, `tn:`, VOTE_W on, BETA_HOLD on, non-Lion, BETA_CLIP unset, HIER → ValueError (25 cases in G2).
* **Name chosen so no registered reader misreads it.** `corpus_exclusions.py`'s `witness_lines` and cVT4's `parse_run` select witness lines with `startswith(<prefix>)`, so a `BETA_HOLD_SET:` line would have been read as a BETA_HOLD witness; `GROUP_HOLD` starts with neither `BETA_HOLD` nor `VOTE_W` (selftest A and G5 assert it).
* **Witness line on every run** (plus `BETA_HOLD: off`, `VOTE_W: off`), e.g. `GROUP_HOLD: on type=blockwise group=1 groupsize=3 names=layer4.0.bn2.weight+layer4.0.shortcut.1.weight+layer4.1.bn2.weight mode=tri P=8609 b0=-13.815510749816895 ms=0.001 lo=-15.0 hi=-2.3026 peak=-5.2065107498168945` (215 chars; floor 145; HOLDISO 214).

**The tree** (`bin/cVT7_stage_harness.sh`, NEW, `d741cf82…`; `$WS/harness_cvt7/cifar10`, STAGE-MANIFEST `888e97a6…`): every live `*.py` byte-identical (5 files, build_network.py the LIVE one — no PlainNet patch), `HF.py.pre_probe_tensor` the live backup, `data` a symlink to the live data; HF.py built live → +PATCH_VOTEWEIGHT (**== `cvt1`'s HF.py `3f2b98e1…`, checked**) → +PATCH_BETAHOLD (**== `cvt4`'s `84b345ad…`, checked**) → +PATCH_GROUPHOLD = **`2396f2be…`**, with the three intermediates kept as `.pre_voteweight` / `.pre_betahold` / `.pre_grouphold`.  Runner `$WS/jobs/run_cifar_cvt7.sh` `805267e4…` = run_cifar.sh with exactly the `cd` line changed.  Verify mode: V-a…V-f3, including the REGISTERED structural tests of both earlier patches UNEDITED on the intermediate pairs (`test_voteweight.py` V0 9 PASS, `test_betahold.py` B0 10 PASS) and `test_grouphold.py` G0 10 PASS.

### 243.6 Gates, branches and what each licenses — `decide()`, first match wins; frozen bars

**Harness gates (→ `HARNESS-UNSOUND`, rc 1).** `G-ARGS` (each run's own ARGS line: spec, net, cell, 18 fixed flags, seed, run-name); `G-ENV` (one ENV line == `ciso1`'s / `cdep1`'s; one `PROBE_TENSOR: on every=100 type=<arm's> tensors=62`); `G-VOTEW` (exactly one `VOTE_W: off`); **`G-BHOLD`** (exactly one `BETA_HOLD: off`); **`G-GHOLD`** (exactly one `GROUP_HOLD` line == the arm's witness); `G-STRUCT` (manifest byte-identical to the scorer's, 5,085 bytes, with the `CARRIERS`, `REPLAY B0 … P_HIGH 8609 P_ISO 5153`, `GROUPHOLD` and `WITNESS` lines); `G-PROV` (MODE submit; build_network == the LIVE `c7998883…`; **HF `2396f2be…`**; **RUNNER `805267e4…`**; SCORER == the file); `G-FLOOR`/`G-CEIL` (max arm mean in 15–90).

**`G-BITE` (→ `PATCH-NOT-VERIFIED`, rc 1; before any level)**, from `runs/cvt7/probe_cvt7-<arm>-s<seed>/probe.jsonl`: (a) 500 records at steps 0…49,900; (b) every UNHELD group follows Lion within 1e-5 (all groups of `k01` and ISO; group 0 of every held arm); (c) held group 1: beta[1] == hold(step+2) AND beta_pre[1] == hold(step+1); (d) `gh_n` == step+2, `gh_nat` == Lion recomputed for group 1, `gh_held` == beta[1], `gh_active` non-decreasing, ≤ `gh_n`, ≥ the records where `gh_nat` ≠ `gh_held`; (e) `k01` / ISO carry no `gh_*` key and NO run carries a `bh_*` key.  No minimum on `gh_active` (HOLDISO's replay is close to what the carriers would do).

**Branches.** `UNRESOLVED-DIVERGED` (a seed range > 5) → `SCALAR-NOT-COLLAPSED` (`k01` > **30**) → `POSITIVE-CONTROL-FAILED` (ISO − `k01` < 20).  Then per held arm, **AT-ISO** iff L ≥ ISO − 5, **AT-K01** iff L ≤ `k01` + 2, else **BETWEEN**:

| order | condition | branch | what it does to 240's PlainNet sentence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | HOLDISO AT-K01 | **`HOLD-CONTROL-FAILED`** | untested on ResNet: an exogenous schedule on the carrier group breaks the rescue by itself |
| 2 | HOLDISO BETWEEN | `HOLD-CONTROL-PARTIAL` | untested; stop |
| 3 | HOLDLOW AT-K01 | **`LOW-STALLS`** | does not transfer as worded: on ResNet "small" is not sufficient, the trajectory matters (HOLDHIGH's state stamped) |
| 4 | HOLDLOW BETWEEN | `LOW-PARTIAL` | the floor half does not transfer cleanly (HOLDHIGH's state stamped) |
| 5 | HOLDLOW AT-ISO, HOLDHIGH AT-K01 | **`TRANSFERS`** | **TRANSFERS** to ResNet18_c100 at this cell: the mechanism sentence may be stated for both networks.  Not licensed: direct vs via the complement (`cvt6`), window, dose, any single carrier, GN / VGG / other cells or horizons |
| 6 | HOLDLOW AT-ISO, HOLDHIGH BETWEEN | **`TRANSFERS-GRADED`** | partly transfers: the carriers' large step size carries part of the stall on ResNet |
| 7 | HOLDLOW AT-ISO, HOLDHIGH AT-ISO | **`DOES-NOT-TRANSFER`** | the step-size mechanism is PlainNet-specific; every PlainNet mechanism sentence stays scoped to PlainNet.  Reachable only because G-BITE passed |

* **Frozen bars (O2).** GAP_MIN 20.0 (35.27 SE), **K01_MAX 30.0** (between `k01` + 5 and ISO − 30 for both anchors; asserted), MATCH 5.0 (8.82 SE), NULL 2.0 (3.53 SE), RESCUE 10.0 (TRAIN-agreement threshold only), DIVERGED 5.0, FLOOR_MIN 15.0, CEIL_MAX 90.0; G-BITE: BH_TOL 1e-5, TIE_REL 1e-12, N_RECORDS 500.
* **Stamps.** Always: `HARNESS-CLEAN`, `PATCH-BITES`, `HOLD-FROM-INIT`, `REPLAY-MAX-RATE-TRIANGLE`, `HIGH-IS-K01-TRAJECTORY`, `CARRIER-GROUP-OF-3`, `ONE-NETWORK-RESNET`, `HORIZON-100-ONLY`, `SIGMA-PRIOR-FROZEN`/`-INBATCH`.  Conditional: `POSITIVE-CONTROL-REPRODUCES`; `<ARM>-AT-ISO`/`-BETWEEN`/`-AT-K01`; `<ARM>-ABOVE-ISO`; `<ARM>-BELOW-K01`; `NONFINITE-<ARM>`; `FLOOR-READINGS-ARE-BOUNDS`; `TRAIN-AGREES`/`-DISAGREES`.
* **After FINAL, descriptive and unable to move it:** per run the complement's and the carrier group's beta peak, pin epoch, r(15–30), last value and `gh_active`; arm-mean TEST (TRAIN) at epochs 9 / 19 / 29 / 39 / 49 / 99.

### 243.7 The noise floor — through `corpus_exclusions.filter_rows` (OPERATIONS 36)

Re-derived on the 3,049-row corpus (`c2d1164d…`), exclusion list `f8455571…` (51 rows dropped → 2,998), 227.6's definitions: **`SIGMA_R18ALL` = 0.694442846939599** (df 209, 46 cells), FILTERED == NAIVE on ResNet18_c100 because every listed row is `PlainNet18_c100` (asserted in selftest C, disclosed).  `SIGMA_PRIOR` = SIGMA_R18ALL; `SE_PRIOR` 0.567010.  The scorer reads the corpus ONLY through `filter_rows` and only as a row-count disclosure; selftest C shows the frozen literal IS the filtered value (to 1e-12, df 209), zero rows carry seed 99/100/101, and no ResNet ISO row carries `cvt6`'s seeds.

**Ingest caveats, registered now (owed to the landing track).** (i) The CSV has no GROUP_HOLD column: the 9 HOLDLOW / HOLDHIGH / HOLDISO rows will carry ISO's 15 cell keys and go into `results/CORPUS-EXCLUSIONS.tsv` in the SAME commit as the ingest, witness = the run's own `GROUP_HOLD:` line verbatim.  (ii) `corpus_exclusions.py --check` (239) knows the kinds `VOTE_W` and `BETA_HOLD` only; a `GROUP_HOLD` witness names no registered kind and would FAIL it as written — the landing track needs its one-line `KINDS` entry (`("GROUP_HOLD", "GROUP_HOLD: off")`), which 239 designed for.  Because `GROUP_HOLD` does not start with `BETA_HOLD`, the existing prefix matching will not misread the new lines; every `cvt7` run prints `VOTE_W: off` and `BETA_HOLD: off`, so the existing completeness check is unaffected.  Not done here.

### 244.3 (b) K13's DOWN fraction, re-derived from the raw probes

`analysis/c244_cvt5_k13_readouts.py <runsdir>` (NEW, `9677e4c3…`; stdlib `json` only, imports nothing from the repo), run as `python3 analysis/c244_cvt5_k13_readouts.py ../runs_cluster_b`: exit 0, output committed as `results/c244_cvt5_k13_readouts.txt` (`2b5d21d3…`). * **Definition.** A record is DOWN iff `c = pt_b2 × mom_pre[0][0] + (1 − pt_b2) × z_agg[0][0] > 0` (group 0 = the complement; `pt_b2` 0.9) — the Lion direction the harness applies moves the complement's beta down. Checked on the records rather than assumed: on all **4,369** records where the complement's beta moved by more than half a step and sat more than two steps from both clamps, `c > 0` ⇔ beta fell, **0 exceptions**. Windows are [lo, lo + 50) epochs by record epoch = step / 500, 250 records each.
* **Per seed, the four windows from epoch 100 (100–150 / 150–200 / 200–250 / 250–300):** s93 0.492 / 0.504 / 0.516 / 0.468; s94 0.532 / 0.532 / 0.488 / 0.508; s95 0.520 / 0.564 / 0.536 / 0.512. **Exact range 0.468 (s93, 250–300, 117/250) – 0.564 (s95, 150–200, 141/250).** Seeds pooled (750 records per window): 0.515 / 0.533 / 0.513 / 0.496, range 0.496–0.533. Before epoch 100: 0.412–0.444 (0–50) and 0.532–0.592 (50–100).
* **241.4(2) is not amended:** "(0.47–0.56)" is this per-seed range at two decimals. ### 245.1 The gap

### 245.2 The rule for two-kind runs, and why (`analysis/corpus_exclusions.py`, `9ede7453…` → `81c12d2a…`; the `--check` path, KINDS and its docstring only)

* **No second-witness column.** `load()` requires every row's arity to equal the header's, so a tenth column means editing all 51 rows and changing `load()`'s output — both frozen here.  A second row per run would break the duplicate-key check and make the row count differ from the run count.
* **Rule.** A run is listed ONCE, by ANY one of its ON lines; being listed satisfies completeness.  A listed run whose `(batch, arm)` — read from its run name — is in the new `MULTI_KIND` table must print EXACTLY the registered line of every kind registered there, so the line the row does not carry is verified, and a wrong, missing or `off` second line FAILs.  Any other listed run printing an ON line of a kind its witness does not name FAILs, as in 239.  A listed two-kind batch also holds its unlisted runs to that kind's `off` line.
* **`MULTI_KIND`** = `cvt6` HIGHHEADPATH / LOWMUTEPATH / LOWHEADPATH × {`BETA_HOLD`, `COMP_HOLD`}, re-typed from `cVT6_complementpath_score.py`'s `WITNESS_BH` / `WITNESS_CH` (not imported, as 227.6's sigmas); test C16 pins it to the scorer's tables byte for byte.  **The landing appends exactly the rows 242.7 and 243.7 planned** (15 `cvt6` rows by BETA_HOLD witness, 9 `cvt7` rows by GROUP_HOLD witness); a forced arm may equally be listed by its COMP_HOLD line.
* **Limits.** As in 239, a single-kind row's witness is compared with the run's own log, not with the registration (that is the scorer's `G-HOLDW` / `G-GHOLD` and RULE 20); only two-kind runs are compared with registered lines.  A future two-kind batch needs its own `MULTI_KIND` entry.

### 245.3 Prefix collisions — proof

Every registered reader selects witness lines with `ln.startswith(<prefix>)` (`witness_lines` here; the `cvt4` / `cvt6` / `cvt7` scorers' parsers).  A line selected for two prefixes A ≠ B starts with both, so one of A, B is a prefix of the other.  `VOTE_W`, `BETA_HOLD`, `GROUP_HOLD`, `COMP_HOLD` begin with V, B, G, C: none is a prefix of another, so no line is read as two kinds (and `kind_of`'s `<prefix>:` match is unambiguous for the same reason).  Each patch prints only `<PREFIX>: off` / `<PREFIX>: on type=…` literals (C16 parses the four patch sources); `check()` now FAILs if a future KINDS entry breaks the property, and prints it.  Real logs: every line starting with one of the prefixes begins `<PREFIX>: ` — 81 `VOTE_W` and 18 `BETA_HOLD` lines in the Mac's 3,117 `.out` files; 36 `VOTE_W`, 36 `BETA_HOLD`, 21 `COMP_HOLD` and 15 `GROUP_HOLD` in the 36 `cvt6` / `cvt7` `.out` files on cluster_b, where no other line contains any of the four.

### 246.4 What bounds the result, led with

**(1) No bar is near.** LOWMUTEPATH is BETWEEN by 18.34 and 27.49 pp; HIGHHEADPATH AT-K01 by 2.58 pp (worst seed 2.30); HOLDHIGH AT-K01 by 2.46; HOLDLOW AT-HEAD by 5.71; LOWHEADPATH AT-HEAD by 5.12. `D_HEAD` is 32.83 over GAP_MIN; `k01` 7.93 under K01_MAX; the worst seed range 4.07 under DIVERGED.

**(2) Floor readings are locations.** HIGHHEADPATH (−0.58 pp vs `k01`) and HOLDHIGH (−0.46) sit at the clamp-frozen floor (`FLOOR-READINGS-ARE-BOUNDS`): "at `k01`" is a location, not point agreement.

**(3) Open loop — what the design cannot separate.** In the three forced arms neither step size responds to the network. LOWHEADPATH shows the complement hold costs nothing when 50 is LOW (`P_CTLC` −0.12 pp, −0.21 SE; TRAIN −0.82). No arm tests whether losing the complement's responsiveness contributes when 50 is HIGH (242.9). HIGHHEADPATH's reading is a statement with the complement on this exogenous replay only.

**(4) One shape per factor: no dose curve, no time gate.**
* 50's HIGH replay starts at b0 (−13.82), not the floor, so HIGH and LOW differ from update 1 (50's schedule minus the floor +2.18 log units at update 1,000, rising).
* **(wording fix 5)** MUTEPATH and HEADPATH are identical to within 0.04 through epoch 18. HEADPATH then falls below (first gap > 0.1 at update 9,036 = epoch 18.07; −0.85 at epoch 20), crosses once at epoch 22.45, and stays above until both reach the floor.
* LOWMUTEPATH's complement gets MORE step size over epochs 15–30 (r 10,064 vs 8,632) and ~90× less over 30–60 (11.4 vs 1,021). Its partial loss (−23.47 pp) cannot be tied to one window: it departs from LOWHEADPATH for good only from line 28, and the design has no time gate.

**(5) HEADPATH is a median replay, not any run's path.** In this batch the free HEAD / HOLDLOW complements miss it by up to 0.237–1.106 (246.7 [D4]).

**(6) One network (`PlainNet18_c100`), one cell, one tensor (idx 50), 100 epochs.** RULE 11.

**(7) `P_INT` +23.59 pp is DESCRIPTIVE.** The HIGH × MUTEPATH forced arm was not run; HOLDHIGH's complement is free.

**(8) `R_LOW` +0.71 pp** (seeds +0.92 / +1.06 / +0.14) repeats `cvt4`'s `P_LOW` pattern but is not a registered effect.

### 246.8 What this licenses, and what it does not

**Licensed — the registered text for `GRADED` (242.6 order 8, as the scorer prints it):** "At least one forced decisive arm sits between k01 and HEAD (states stamped): each route carries part of the stall, or one route is partial. EFFECT ON 240's OWN-STEP-MAGNITUDE and its bound 240.4(1): PARTLY RESOLVED -- read the two stamped states and the co-primaries P_50 and P_C; no single-route sentence is licensed." At this cell, `PlainNet18_c100`, 100 epochs:

* **(wording fix 2) HIGHHEADPATH-AT-K01.** At this cell, this one large 50 trajectory (MUTE's, replayed) is sufficient to put the arm at the `k01` location. This holds with the complement on HEAD's measured path, which collapses late (r ≤ 2 from epoch 64.8) rather than on MUTE's early schedule, and is imposed open-loop. Whether the complement's lost responsiveness contributes when 50 is HIGH is untested (242.9).
* **(wording fix 3) LOWMUTEPATH-BETWEEN.** With 50 at the floor, this one complement path (MUTEPATH, open-loop) is sufficient for a partial loss (`P_C` +23.47 pp, +41.38 SE) and does not reach the `k01` location. No other complement path or dose was run.
* **LOWHEADPATH-AT-HEAD, HOLDLOW-AT-HEAD, HOLDHIGH-AT-K01.** Forcing the complement onto HEADPATH with 50 at the floor keeps HEAD's level; `cvt4`'s two replicates hold at new seeds.
* **(wording fix 4) Effect on 240.4(1).** Under that licence, 240.4(1)'s bound is PARTLY RESOLVED: the two stamped states are HIGHHEADPATH-AT-K01 and LOWMUTEPATH-BETWEEN, with `P_50` +53.53 pp and `P_C` +23.47 pp. No single-route sentence is licensed, and neither state is a statement about necessity.

**Not licensed.** That the complement's collapse plays no part in HOLDHIGH; necessity of either factor; why a large step size on this BatchNorm scale stalls the network; which window matters; any dose curve; any other complement path; that the forced (open-loop) arms stand for closed-loop ones; point agreement at `k01`; `P_INT` or `R_LOW` as effects; any other tensor, network (ResNet with BN or GN, VGG), cell or horizon; RULE 11.

### 246.9 Corrections IN PLACE to CORRECTIONS 242 (brackets; superseded wording kept)

1. **RULE H — "the 12 landed 100-epoch HEAD runs" (launch verifier; `cvt6` verifier fix 14).** 242's header, 242.3(2) (the source sentence and the RULE H bullet) and 242.9 said the replay is the median of the 12 landed 100-epoch HEAD runs, and the registered derivation's docstring (`analysis/cvt6_registration_derivations.py`, not edited, RULE 16) says "every landed 100-epoch HEAD run at this cell". That is 12 of the 15: `cpl2` HEAD s75–77 (same `--stepsize-groups`, `PlainNet18_c100`, 100 epochs, with probe records) were omitted. **Re-derived by this track** (`scratchpad/land_cvt67_record/ruleh15.py`, stdlib, `../runs_cluster_b`): at all 500 record steps the 12-run median (mean of the 6th and 7th values) equals `patches/cvt6_headpath.json`'s `v` exactly (max |diff| 0.0), and **the 15-run median (8th value) differs from it by at most 0.1601 log units (at step 32,300, epoch 64.6, in the steep descent), mean 0.0100**. The registration stays valid: the replay file is what was registered, witnessed (sha on every `COMP_HOLD` line) and bitten; "median of all eligible HEAD runs" was the description, not the gate. Brackets placed at each of the four places.
2. **242.14 "the first run (`cvt6-k01-s96`, 5022506) COMPLETED in 39 min 52 s" (fix 12).** By `sacct` End times, read independently by the score stage and the verifier, **8 runs (5022506–5022513) had ended by the pass-3 timestamp 00:46:56Z**, consistent with "13 RUNNING, 0 PENDING"; `cvt6-k01-s96` was the lowest job id, not the first to complete — LOWMUTEPATH-s96 ended first, at 00:44:34Z (k01-s96 at 00:45:02Z). The brief for this landing counted 7; the sacct record says 8. Bracketed in place.

### 247.4 What bounds the result, led with

**(1) Dose — and held set — are confounded with network.** The "large" trajectory is `k01`'s own, the only measured large trajectory at this cell (243.3(2), 243.9). Its peak is −5.21, ~0.8 log units below PlainNet's HOLDHIGH replay (MUTE's, −4.39). **And (verifier) PlainNet held idx 50 alone while ResNet held the three carriers together.** So `TRANSFERS-GRADED` cannot separate "the ResNet rescue is only partly sensitive to the carriers' step size" from "a smaller large step size does less damage" or "holding three tensors differs from holding one". No rung between, no dose curve, no time window: GRADED here means "between the bars", not "graded in dose".

**(2) The complement was free but not ISO-like.** HOLDHIGH's complement rose higher (peak ~−4.6 vs −5.0; r(15–30) 10,396 vs 8,164) and pinned by magnitude at 52.8–54.0 instead of ISO's 92.6–99.4. `P_HIGH` therefore changes both the carriers' step size and the complement's path; the batch cannot say whether the 19.8 pp loss is direct or goes through the complement (`cvt6`'s question, asked on PlainNet). **(wording fix 1)** The arm-mean TEST gap passes 2 pp at line 16 (after 17 epochs, record 17.0) while the two complements are identical to 0.000. This holds per seed on s100 and s101 only: s99's gap is 1.48 pp at line 16 and first passes 2 pp at line 17 (record 18.0), after its complements parted (first difference ≥ 0.0005 at 17.6, > 0.1 at 17.8). DESCRIPTIVE, UNSURE. **(wording fix 3)** The complement's exact clamp (continuous) is at 99.2 / 99.8 / 99.8.

**(3) No bar near the branch word.** HOLDHIGH is 14.81 pp (26 SE) from AT-ISO and 25.27 pp from AT-K01, seed range 0.396, every seed BETWEEN (50.03–50.42). The narrowest registered margins are the two other held arms' AT-ISO states: HOLDISO +5.02 pp (+8.85 SE), HOLDLOW +5.26 pp (+9.27 SE); if either flipped the branch would change (`HOLD-CONTROL-PARTIAL` / `LOW-PARTIAL`), but both sit ~9 SE inside.

**(4) `P_LOW` is not an effect.** +0.26 pp (+0.45 SE; seeds +0.20 / +0.89 / −0.32), and it speaks only to about the first 23 epochs: ISO's own carrier group sits at the exact clamp from 22.8–23.4.

**(5) Replay shapes (wording fix 5).** HOLDISO replays ISO's median carrier trajectory. The schedule peaks at −8.6625 (P=5153); its highest value on the 100-step record grid is −8.711, against in-batch ISO record-grid peaks of −8.774 / −8.620 / −8.704. `P_CTL` is −0.02 pp.

**(6) Scope.** One network, one cell (`ciso1`'s), 100 epochs, the three carriers held together (nothing about any single carrier); no time gate; GN, VGG and other cells out of scope (RULE 11).

### 247.8 What this licenses, and what it does not

**Licensed — the registered text for `TRANSFERS-GRADED` (243.6 order 6, as the scorer prints it):** "Handing the carrier group k01's step size lowers the rescued arm by more than 5 pp but keeps it more than 2 pp above k01, while HOLDLOW and HOLDISO keep ISO's level. EFFECT ON 240's PlainNet sentence: PARTLY TRANSFERS -- on ResNet the carriers' large step size carries part of the stall, not all of it (on PlainNet it carried all of it). No single-mechanism sentence for ResNet; no dose curve." **[Registered licence text. Whether it acts directly or through the complement's earlier collapse is not separated (247.4(2)). The PlainNet comparison differs in dose (peak −4.39 vs −5.21) AND in held set (idx 50 alone vs the three carriers together), so 'part vs all' is not attributable to the network (wording fix 6).]** At this cell only (`ResNet18_c100`, CIFAR-100, `ciso1`'s cell, 100 epochs, the three carriers held together as ISO's group, their vote out of the complement's sum):
* **HOLDHIGH-BETWEEN.** Giving the carrier group `k01`'s measured step-size trajectory (an exogenous replay) is sufficient to cost ~20 pp of ISO's 47 pp rescue (70.04 → 50.23). **(wording fix 6)** This replay (`k01`'s own trajectory, peak −5.21) is not sufficient at this cell to bring the run down to `k01` (22.95); larger trajectories were not tested.
* **HOLDLOW-AT-ISO.** Freezing the group at the floor is sufficient to keep ISO's level.
* **HOLDISO-AT-ISO.** Replaying ISO's own carrier trajectory keeps ISO's level, so the hold does not break the rescue by itself.

**Not licensed.** Necessity; any other network, cell or horizon; any single carrier; which epochs matter; whether the loss is direct or through the complement's earlier collapse; that ResNet is intrinsically less sensitive than PlainNet (dose and held set confounded); a dose curve; point agreement anywhere.

**DESCRIPTIVE, UNSURE (records only).** The free complement in HOLDHIGH did not stay ISO-like: it first took more step size, then shrank to the floor by epoch ~53 instead of ~96 — earlier than ISO's, later than `k01`'s (35.6) and than PlainNet's HOLDHIGH (39). **(fix 1)** As on PlainNet, the arm-mean TEST gap had passed 2 pp after 17 epochs while the two complements were still identical (true on 2 of 3 seeds; s99 passed 2 pp one epoch later, just after its complements parted); the carriers' step size had diverged from ISO's since epoch ~10.5. **(fix 7)** HOLDHIGH's TEST stayed within 0.06 pp of `k01`'s through line 16, fell 1.26–1.90 pp below it at lines 17–18, rose above it from line 19, and settled near 50 at line 41, shortly after its replayed carrier step size reached the floor (37.0).

### 247.9 What `cvt4`–`cvt7` together say about the mechanism now (registered where marked; descriptive where marked)

* **Registered, PlainNet (`cvt4`, `cvt6`), at `cvt1`'s cell, 100 epochs, idx 50's vote out of the complement's sum:** 50 on MUTE's large replayed trajectory is sufficient to put the arm at the `k01` location — with the complement free (`cvt4` HOLDHIGH, `cvt6` HOLDHIGH) and with the complement forced open-loop onto HEAD's measured path (`cvt6` HIGHHEADPATH); 50 at the floor is sufficient to keep HEAD's level, with the complement free or forced onto HEADPATH; with 50 at the floor, the complement forced onto MUTE's collapse schedule is sufficient for a partial loss (41.56, `BETWEEN`). `GRADED`: no single-route sentence; 240.4(1) PARTLY RESOLVED.
* **Registered, ResNet18_c100 (`cvt7`), at `ciso1`'s cell, 100 epochs, the three carriers held together:** `k01`'s own trajectory on the carrier group is sufficient to cost ~20 pp of the 47 pp rescue, not to reach `k01`; the floor and ISO's own trajectory keep the rescue. `TRANSFERS-GRADED`: partly transfers; dose, held set and the complement's path confounded.
* **Descriptive, UNSURE, across all three:** on both networks the arm-mean TEST gap between the large-step arm and its rescued twin passes 2 pp at `Epoch` line 16 while the two complements are still identical (PlainNet `cvt4` HOLDHIGH vs HEAD, complements 0.001 apart; `cvt6` HIGHHEADPATH vs LOWHEADPATH, complements bitwise identical by construction, per seed from lines 16 / 17 / 16; ResNet `cvt7` HOLDHIGH vs ISO, complements identical to 0.000, true per seed on 2 of 3); in `cvt6` the complement-path route shows up only from line 28. The records are consistent with the carriers' large step size doing damage early and directly, and a collapsing complement costing a separate, later amount — not tested: no batch has a time gate.
* **What stays open:** dose vs network vs held set on ResNet, and direct vs via-complement on ResNet (247.13 R1); when and how much on PlainNet (R2); the complement route's window (R3); responsiveness of the complement when 50 is HIGH (242.9); every other network, cell and horizon (RULE 11).

(iii) A closed-loop test of the complement's responsiveness when 50 is HIGH (242.9): no forced path both follows HEAD's trajectory and responds to the network, so no clean arm exists yet. (iv) Longer horizons on either network: `cvt5` (RHO 1.0012) and `ciso2` (RHO 0.9977) show the rescues are regimes; a horizon batch answers no open mechanism question.
* Ranks, questions and costs are a recommendation to the operator; **no registration was written, no scorer committed, nothing submitted.**
