### 248.1 Question

`cvt7` (247, `TRANSFERS-GRADED`): the carrier group {`layer4.0.bn2.weight` 50, `layer4.0.shortcut.1.weight` 53, `layer4.1.bn2.weight` 59}, held with its vote out of the complement's sum on `k01`'s own trajectory (HOLDHIGH, `tri:8609`), cost ~20 pp of ISO's 47 pp rescue (70.04 → 50.23), not all of it.  247.4 led with two bounds: **(1) dose** — PlainNet's full stall (240, 246) used MUTE's larger trajectory; **(2) route** — HOLDHIGH's free complement collapsed ~40 epochs early.  **`cvt8` crosses the dose (HIGH / BIG) with the complement's path (FREE / forced onto ISO's measured path), with LOWISOPATH as the control of the complement hold.**

### 248.2 Design

* **Cell.** `ciso1`'s / `cvt7`'s exactly (243.2): CIFAR-100, `ResNet18_c100` (62 tensors, 11,220,132 params), SGDm (0.99, wd 0.1) + Lion meta (0.99, b2 0.9, wd 0), ms 1e-3, alpha0 1e-6, 100 ep, batch 100, `AUGMENT=1`, `BETA_CLIP=-15:-2.3026`, `PROBE=100`, `PROBE_TENSOR=1`; the ENV line is `ciso1`'s byte for byte.
* **Seeds** {102, 103, 104} (pre-assigned; 0 corpus rows, 0 `.out` ARGS lines, 0 `sacct` jobs carry them — guards 1c4, 2c, 2d, 2e).

| arm | `--stepsize-groups` | `GROUP_HOLD` (carriers, group 1) | `REST_HOLD` (59-tensor complement, group 0) | cell |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `k01` | `scalar` | unset | unset | floor anchor |
| ISO | ISO's | unset | unset | positive control |
| HOLDHIGH | ISO's | `<C>:tri:8609` | unset (Lion) | HIGH × FREE (`cvt7` replicate) |
| HOLDBIG | ISO's | `<C>:tri:9428` | unset (Lion) | BIG × FREE |
| **HIGHISOPATH** | ISO's | `<C>:tri:8609` | `rec:cvt8_isopath` | HIGH × ISOPATH |
| **BIGISOPATH** | ISO's | `<C>:tri:9428` | `rec:cvt8_isopath` | BIG × ISOPATH |
| LOWISOPATH | ISO's | `<C>:floor` | `rec:cvt8_isopath` | REST_HOLD positive control |

`<C>` = `layer4.0.bn2.weight+layer4.0.shortcut.1.weight+layer4.1.bn2.weight`.  CO-PRIMARY `P_DOSE`, `P_ROUTE`, `P_ROUTE_BIG`; KEY `D_ISO`, `P_CTLC` = ISO − LOWISOPATH, `R_HIGH` = ISO − HOLDHIGH (`cvt7`'s `P_HIGH`), `P_DOSE_PATH` = HIGHISOPATH − BIGISOPATH; DESCRIPTIVE `P_INT` = `P_ROUTE_BIG` − `P_ROUTE`.

### 248.3 Decisions, taken from landed records (`analysis/cvt8_registration_derivations.py`, NEW, `c21fed15…`; output `b747d9aa…` on cluster_b)

**(1) RULE I — eligibility, stated and enumerated (S0).** Candidates: every CSV row, `ResNet18_c100`, whose granularity parses by name to ISO's partition (any spelling), in the corpus at registration (sha `355c0977…`, highest job id 5022526; later rows print `LANDED AFTER REGISTRATION` and never enter).  Eligible iff E1 one ARGS line with ISO's cell and `--num-epochs` ≥ 100; E2 one ENV line == `ciso1`'s (PROBE_DIR stripped); E3 one `PROBE_TENSOR: on every=100 type=blockwise tensors=62`; E4 no ON line of any `corpus_exclusions.KINDS` kind and not listed in the TSV; E5 complete, not superseded; E6 probe records at steps 0..49,900.  **21 candidates → 12 eligible** (ascending job id): `ciso1` s21–23 (4925520/25/30), `ciso2` s31–33 (4929329/33/37), `cdep1` s24–26 (4929650/57/63), `cvt7` ISO s99–101 (5022490/95/5022500); **9 not eligible**: `cvt7` HOLDLOW / HOLDHIGH / HOLDISO × 3 (E4: `GROUP_HOLD` ON and listed).  `ciso2`'s 250-epoch runs are eligible because `train.py` passes `num_epochs` only to its epoch loop (HF receives no horizon; `SCHED=none`; the cosine defaults in `build_optimizer.py` belong to the AdamW / SGD reference arms), so their first 50,000 updates are the process a 100-epoch run is — the reading `cvt7`'s RULE P already used (243.3).  The `cvt7` ISO runs ran from `harness_cvt7` with every switch off, bitwise the live tree (243.4 RR1).

**(2) ISOPATH is a replay file, not a closed form (S1).** Every eligible complement rises at the maximum rate to −4.89 … −5.02 at epoch 17.6–18.0, then drifts down (−7.0 at 30, −7.9 at 40, −8.6 at 50, −9.4 at 60, −11.5 … −12.1 at 80), r ≤ 2 for good only from 94.0–99.4; the best max-rate triangle misses every run by **≥ 5.278** log units.  **RULE I (docstring, before any `cvt8` run):** v_k = median over the 12 of record k's complement beta[0] (mean of the 6th and 7th), n_k = 100k + 2; the file stores `{id, rule, source, n, v}` (13,126 bytes, **sha `08ab25f3a329cb260bb39fb72f3299c021e7169bf612fa27d539166296e28e70`**); the schedule is 242.3(2)'s `rec:` arithmetic.  **Tolerance:** (a) at all 500 record steps the float32 schedule is within **4.77e-7** of the median; (b) every eligible trajectory moves ≤ 0.1000404 between two records, so the schedule is within 0.1 log units of the piecewise median path at every update.  Fidelity, reported: in-sample max |record − schedule| 0.166–0.642 (mean 0.034–0.118); out-of-sample (`cvt7` HOLDLOW / HOLDISO free complements) 0.341–0.752.  Window means r = e^(β+15): schedule 8,146 (15–30) / 1,116 (30–60) / 59.8 (60–100); runs 8,075–8,272 / 1,080–1,139 / 53.3–65.6; r ≤ 2 from 96.4 (runs 94.0–99.4).

**(3) HOLDBIG = `tri:9428`, justified (S3).** It is the SAME integer, so BITWISE the same schedule (b0, ms, clamp identical on both networks), as PlainNet's HOLDHIGH / HIGHHEADPATH (RULE P re-run on this host's PlainNet records: 9428, `k01` 8437) — the dose half of 247.4(1) is removed in absolute step size.  Against HOLDHIGH: peak step size ×2.268 (0.819 log units), r(15–30) ×2.50 (10,064 vs 4,026), clamp at epoch 40.08 vs 36.81.  **Why not larger:** no carrier-sized group measured at this cell rose above P ≈ 9,500 — `k01` P 8,599–8,627, ISO's complement 8,803–8,863, `cvt7` HOLDHIGH's free complement 9,213, and `ciso1`'s count-matched CTRL group (three non-carriers isolated, stalled at `k01`) **9,447**, 0.019 log units above 9428 (only singleton tensors of the `k62` / `lay` arms reach the upper clamp; the carriers there peak at −9.0 … −8.3).  The alternative matched RELATIVE to each network's own `k01` peak, 8609 + (9428 − 8437) = 9600, is 0.172 log units above; not chosen (the absolute match is exact and bitwise; the relative one would replay nothing measured).

**(4) BIGISOPATH is needed and included.** Without it the factorial cannot say, at the dose that stalled PlainNet, whether the stall runs through the complement: under DOSE-FULL a ROUTE-VIA reading at `k01`'s dose would leave the BIG-dose route unread, and BIGISOPATH is exactly `cvt6`'s decisive HIGHHEADPATH (which put PlainNet at `k01`) transplanted to ResNet — the one arm that can state "the PlainNet sentence transfers at PlainNet's dose with the complement on the rescued arm's path".  Price: +3 runs ≈ +2.1 (off [HOST_3c1b003035]) to +2.8 GPU-h; 21 runs ≈ 15.0–19.3 GPU-h + 0.22 registration, inside the brief's ~22.  HOLDLOW (the `cvt7` floor replicate) is NOT run: LOWISOPATH shares its carrier hold and adds the complement hold, and `cvt7`'s HOLDLOW sat 5.26 pp inside `AT-ISO`; saved 3 runs.

**(5) Lion momentum with both groups held (as 242.3(5)).** `Lion_meta_update` runs unchanged, then clamp, then `PATCH_GROUPHOLD` on group 1, then `PATCH_RESTHOLD` on group 0; in the three forced arms no applied beta depends on z or momentum (DEAD STATE).  `tests/test_resthold.py` R4 proves it bitwise over 3,000 synthetic updates: the whole momentum vector and the carrier group's beta equal the `cvt7`-tree object's; the complement equals the schedule after every update; `_rh_nat` / `_rh_active` exact (1,183–1,960 active); a second object on a DIFFERENT z stream holds bitwise-identical beta.

### 248.6 Gates, branches and licences — `decide()`, first match wins; frozen bars

**Harness gates (→ `HARNESS-UNSOUND`, rc 1).** `G-ARGS`; `G-ENV` (one ENV line == `ciso1`'s; `PROBE_TENSOR` type per arm, tensors=62); `G-VOTEW` (`VOTE_W: off`); `G-BHOLD` (`BETA_HOLD: off`); **`G-CHOLD`** (NO `COMP_HOLD` line); `G-GHOLD` and **`G-RHOLD`** (exactly one line == the arm's witness); `G-STRUCT` (manifest byte-identical, 7,525 bytes, with the `REPLAY … P_HIGH 8609 P_BIG 9428`, `RESTREPLAY ISOPATH … SHA256 08ab25f3… KNOTS 500`, GROUPHOLD / RESTHOLD / WITNESS / RWITNESS tables); `G-PROV` (MODE submit; build_network `c7998883…`; **HF `5197dc2e…`**; **RUNNER `1dbe4ff5…`**; **REPLAY `08ab25f3…`**; SCORER == the file); **`G-REPLAY`**; `G-FLOOR` / `G-CEIL`.

**`G-BITE` (→ `PATCH-NOT-VERIFIED`, rc 1; before any level)**: (a) 500 records; (b) Lion on every UNHELD group (all of `k01` / ISO; group 0 of HOLDHIGH / HOLDBIG; none on the forced arms); (c) carrier schedule in beta and beta_pre on the 5 held arms, ISOPATH in beta and beta_pre on the 3 forced arms; (d) `gh_*` / `rh_*` audits; (e) no `gh_*` / `rh_*` on controls, no `rh_*` on HOLDHIGH / HOLDBIG, no `bh_*` / `ch_*` anywhere.

**Branches.** `UNRESOLVED-DIVERGED` (seed range > 5) → `SCALAR-NOT-COLLAPSED` (`k01` > 30) → `POSITIVE-CONTROL-FAILED` (ISO − `k01` < 20) → `COMP-HOLD-CONTROL-FAILED` (LOWISOPATH ≤ `k01` + 2) → `COMP-HOLD-CONTROL-PARTIAL` (LOWISOPATH < ISO − 5) → `REPLICATE-FAILED` (HOLDHIGH outside [`k01` + 10, ISO − 10]) → **`<DOSE>+<ROUTE>+<BIGROUTE>`**:
* DOSE: HOLDBIG ≤ `k01` + 2 → **`DOSE-FULL`** (247.4(1) resolved toward dose: at PlainNet's dose the ResNet group stalls as PlainNet's tensor did); \|HOLDBIG − HOLDHIGH\| ≤ 5 → **`NO-DOSE`** (dose does not explain "part vs all" over this step; network or held set remains); HOLDBIG > HOLDHIGH + 5 → `DOSE-REVERSED` (no dose sentence); else **`DOSE-PARTIAL`** (graded over this step; PlainNet's dose does not reproduce the full stall).
* ROUTE (HIGHISOPATH vs HOLDHIGH): ≥ ISO − 5 → **`ROUTE-VIA`** (at `k01`'s dose the loss runs through the complement's collapse); ≤ HOLDHIGH + 5 → **`ROUTE-DIRECT`** (the loss does not need the collapse; also the null's prediction, reachable only past `G-BITE`); else **`ROUTE-PARTIAL`**.
* BIGROUTE (BIGISOPATH vs HOLDBIG), the same words, plus `BIGROUTE-UNREADABLE` when HOLDBIG > ISO − 10.  `DOSE-FULL` with `BIGROUTE-DIRECT` adds the registered sentence: the PlainNet sentence TRANSFERS to ResNet18_c100 at this cell AT PlainNet's DOSE (three carriers together; complement open-loop).
* The disjointness of every pair of word regions follows from the replicate gate (REP_MARGIN = 2 × MATCH, asserted in selftest A).  73 branch strings are registered, each with a licence; selftest F's 20,000-draw sweep plus section E reach every word.
* **Frozen bars (O2).** GAP_MIN 20.0 (35.60 SE), K01_MAX 30.0, MATCH 5.0 (8.90 SE), NULL 2.0 (3.56 SE), **REP_MARGIN 10.0**, RESCUE 10.0 (TRAIN agreement only), DIVERGED 5.0, FLOOR_MIN 15.0, CEIL_MAX 90.0; G-BITE: BH_TOL 1e-5, TIE_REL 1e-12, N_RECORDS 500.
* **Stamps.** Always `HARNESS-CLEAN`, `PATCH-BITES`, `HOLD-FROM-INIT`, `REPLAY-MAX-RATE-TRIANGLE`, `BIG-IS-PLAINNET-DOSE`, `ISOPATH-REPLAY-FILE`, `FORCED-ARMS-OPEN-LOOP`, `CARRIER-GROUP-OF-3`, `ONE-NETWORK-RESNET`, `HORIZON-100-ONLY`, `SIGMA-PRIOR-FROZEN`/`-INBATCH`.  Conditional: `POSITIVE-CONTROL-REPRODUCES`; `<ARM>-AT-ISO/-BETWEEN/-AT-K01` for the five held arms; `UNBRANCHED-<DOSE>` on the three control branches; `<ARM>-ABOVE-ISO`; `<ARM>-BELOW-K01`; `HIGHISOPATH-BELOW-HOLDHIGH`, `BIGISOPATH-BELOW-HOLDBIG`; `NONFINITE-<ARM>`; `FLOOR-READINGS-ARE-BOUNDS`; `TRAIN-AGREES`/`-DISAGREES`.

### 248.9 Deviations from the brief and limits, disclosed

* **A new patch and a new kind, not `PATCH_COMPHOLD`** (248.4): its guard requires `BETA_HOLD`, which `PATCH_GROUPHOLD` refuses, and its anchors do not exist in `cvt7`'s HF.py.  The `corpus_exclusions` `KINDS` / `MULTI_KIND` lines are **owed** (248.7), not added.
* **HOLDLOW not replicated** (248.3(4)); **BIGISOPATH added** (+3 runs).
* **`ciso2`'s 250-epoch runs enter RULE I** (their first 100 epochs), which PlainNet's RULE H did not do for `cvt5` — justified by the harness reading at 248.3(1), not by precedent.
* **Open loop.** The forced complement does not respond to the network; a `ROUTE-VIA` reading says an ISO-shaped complement schedule is sufficient to undo the loss, not that the free complement's responsiveness is the route (242.9's bound, on ResNet).  ISOPATH is a median, not any run's trajectory (in-sample misses up to 0.64).
* **Held set still differs from PlainNet** (three carriers vs one): a `DOSE-FULL` reading removes the dose confound, not the held-set one.  No time gate, one shape per factor, two doses.
* **Linear interpolation between records; float32 schedule exact, Lion accumulation not** (as 242.9).
* **The stage holds more than this registration.** `~/stage_cvt8` was rsync'd from the shared working copy, which also holds `cvt9`'s uncommitted files; the launcher and scorer read none of them; at launch the files guard 1b names are compared with `git show HEAD:<path>`.
* **Queue.** `cvt9` (249) may launch on the same account; `gpu-short`'s 12-GPU per-user QOS is shared.

### 249.1 Question

`cvt4` (240) and `cvt6` (246): with idx 50's vote out of the complement's sum, 50 on MUTE's replayed large trajectory (`tri:9428`) from init to the end puts PlainNet at the `k01` location — complement free (HOLDHIGH) or forced onto HEAD's path (HIGHHEADPATH, 11.49). Neither batch had a time gate or a dose rung (240.4(2), 246.4(4)); `cvt7` (247.4(1)) left "part on ResNet, all on PlainNet" confounded with dose. **`cvt9` asks, with the complement forced onto HEADPATH in every held arm: which half of 50's large trajectory does the damage, and how does the level depend on the trajectory's peak?**

### 249.2 Design

* **CO-PRIMARY** (in batch; plateau5 from each run's own `.out`; TRAIN beside TEST; bounded in neither direction): `P_MID` = CTL − MIDDOSE; `P_RES` = CTL − RESDOSE; `P_EARLY` = CTL − EARLY; `P_LATE` = CTL − LATE; `P_WIN` = LATE − EARLY. **KEY:** `D_CTL` = CTL − `k01`; `R_HIGH` = CTL − HIGHHEADPATH (`cvt6`'s `P_50`, replicated). **DESCRIPTIVE:** `ADD` = `P_EARLY` + `P_LATE` − `R_HIGH`; kept fractions.
* **Refinements of 247.13 R2, justified.** (i) No HEAD arm: every held arm shares the forced complement, so the control is LOWHEADPATH, and `cvt6` already showed LOWHEADPATH == HEAD (`P_CTLC` −0.12 pp); a HEAD arm would add 3 runs for a contrast no bar reads. (ii) ONE window pair, not two: a second pair (e.g. cut at the TEST split, update 8500) would take the batch to 27 runs, ≈ 18.1 GPU-h expected and 22.4 at 0.83, over the ~20 budget, and a cut at the split gives EARLY only ~20 % of the integrated step size (a LATE stall there would read "more dose", not "later"). (iii) `k01` kept: it is the in-batch floor anchor of every AT-K01 / STALLED bar and of `SCALAR-NOT-COLLAPSED`.

### 249.3 The rules, taken from landed records (`analysis/cvt9_registration_derivations.py`, NEW, `0ce09850…`; output `83f53e10…` on cluster_b)

* **RULE P (237.3, imported unedited) re-run on this host:** P_HIGH 9428, P_HEAD 5041, P_K01 8437. **P_RES 8609** is read from the registered `cVT7_grouphold_score.py` (ResNet's RULE P; `ciso2`'s records are not on every host); the selftest checks the literal.

The rungs' peak r: 505 (5041) | 4,535 (7235) | 17,917 (8609) | 40,639 (9428); MID/HEAD 8.97, HIGH/MID 8.96: a bisection rung. The registered file is the median of 12 of them (246.9); the 18-run median differs from it by at most 0.2521 log units (record 322, epoch 64.4), mean 0.0201. **The file is reused byte for byte, not regenerated**: LOWHEADPATH / HIGHHEADPATH are then exact replicates of `cvt6`'s arms, and every held arm shares the one complement schedule, so no contrast depends on which median is replayed. `cvt6`'s RULE H re-run on the host reproduces the file byte for byte (selftest B).

### 249.4 The patch, its inertness and its bite (proved BEFORE launch)

**`patches/patch_windowhold.py`** (NEW, `f2602888…`) applies on top of `cvt6`'s HF.py and makes FOUR insertions, editing no existing line: a guarded `_wh_apply()` right after `PATCH_COMPHOLD`'s `_ch_apply` region (before `_probe`); one `_wh_init` call right after `_ch_init`; a guarded `_wh_attach(rec)` after `_ch_attach` (before `_pt_attach`); five `_wh_` methods after `PATCH_COMPHOLD`'s block.
* **OFF** (unset or empty) prints `WINDOW_HOLD: off`; nothing touched; no probe key.
* **ON** requires `BETA_HOLD` on in mode `tri`; inside [n0, n1) group 1 keeps the value `PATCH_BETAHOLD` just wrote; outside it is set to the clamp floor; applied at init too. Records gain `wh_n`, `wh_active`, `wh_nat` (the tri value `PATCH_BETAHOLD` wrote), `wh_held`. `bh_nat` stays Lion's value; `bh_held` is the windowed value (so the scorer drops `bh_active`'s "≥ records where nat ≠ held" clause on the two windowed arms and applies it to `wh_active` instead).
* **Loud:** malformed values, n0 ≥ n1, BETA_HOLD off / floor / shared → ValueError (14 forms, W2).
* **Witness:** `WINDOW_HOLD: on type=blockwise group=1 name=layer4.1.bn2.weight base=tri P=9428 n0=0 n1=9429 outside=floor value=-15.0` (LATE: `n0=9429 n1=end`). Prefix starts with W: not a prefix of, nor prefixed by, VOTE_W / BETA_HOLD / GROUP_HOLD / COMP_HOLD (selftest A).
* **Meta-optimiser state:** Lion runs unchanged; both momentum entries remain dead state; the windowed arms are open loop (W4: two objects on different z streams hold bitwise-identical beta).

| proof | where | result |
|---|---|---|
| **Structure** (`tests/test_windowhold.py` W0): four regions as registered; **deleting them reproduces `cvt6`'s HF.py BYTE FOR BYTE**; five `_wh_` methods after the `_ch_`; every pre-existing method in order. Also `cvt6`'s `tests/test_comphold.py` C0, UNEDITED, on the base | stage V-f / V-g; guards 4b1 / 4b2 | 11 / 0 and 11 / 0 |
| **CPU** (W1–W5, login node, `~/l249_logs/test_windowhold_login.log`, and inside the GPU job): every arm prints exactly its three witnesses and `VOTE_W: off`, initial beta as registered; WINDOW_HOLD unset / empty leave every attribute and beta EQUAL to the `cvt6` object's on k01, LOWHEADPATH, HIGHHEADPATH, MIDDOSE, RESDOSE; 14 malformed forms raise; `_wh_value` == the scorer's schedule at every n in 0..50,001; W4 over 3,000 synthetic updates for EARLY, LATE, `0:150`, `150:end`: momentum and complement bitwise the unpatched object's, group 1 on the windowed schedule, `wh_nat` == the tri value, `wh_active` == the number of updates the window moves off the triangle (0 / 3000 / 2851 / 149), dead state | `$WS/runs/cvt9/inertness_windowhold.log` | **82 / 0**, `TEST_WINDOWHOLD_RC 0` |

* **Limit, disclosed (as 237.4 / 242.4).** In 300 steps EARLY's window never closes and LATE's never opens, so for the two registered window strings bite on the real path is shown as "the schedule held" (LATE at the floor where tri would have risen; `wh_active` 292) and the switch itself by the two test windows. The final weights of MIDDOSE, RESDOSE and HIGHHEADPATH are bitwise identical after 300 steps (their schedules coincide until update 7236; step sizes ~1e-6 on BatchNorm scales sit below float32 resolution).
* **One test failed on the login node before the GPU job and was fixed:** W4 required `wh_active` > 0 for EARLY, which is false before update 9429; the check now requires `wh_active` == the counted updates the window moves off the triangle. No patch, scorer or schedule line changed.

### 249.6 Gates, branches, licences — `decide()`; frozen bars

**Harness gates (→ `HARNESS-UNSOUND`, rc 1):** `G-ARGS`; `G-ENV` (one ENV line == `cvt6`'s; one `PROBE_TENSOR … tensors=53`); `G-VOTEW`; `G-HOLDW`; `G-CHOLDW`; **`G-WHOLDW`** (exactly one `WINDOW_HOLD` line == the arm's witness); `G-STRUCT` (manifest byte-identical, 7,720 bytes, with the `REPLAY … P_HIGH 9428 P_MID 7235 P_RES 8609 N_E 9429 HEADPATH … SHA256 74be71fa… KNOTS 500` line and the three hold tables); `G-PROV` (MODE submit; build_network `e65e6773…`; **HF `816e3357…`**; **RUNNER `0fe45b1d…`**; REPLAY `74be71fa…`; SCORER == the file); `G-REPLAY`; `G-FLOOR` / `G-CEIL`.

**`G-BITE` (→ `PATCH-NOT-VERIFIED`, rc 1; before any level):** (a) 500 records; (b) `k01` follows Lion in beta (tol 1e-5); (c) every held arm: group 1 == the arm's (windowed) schedule and group 0 == HEADPATH, in beta (step+2) AND beta_pre (step+1); (d) `bh_*` (n, nat == Lion, held == beta[1], active monotone ≤ n; the ≥ clause on non-windowed arms), `ch_*` (full), `wh_*` on EARLY / LATE (n, nat == `tri:9428` value, held == beta[1], active monotone, ≤ n, ≥ records where nat ≠ held); (e) no hold key on `k01`, no `wh_*` key on a non-windowed arm. **Branches (first match):** `UNRESOLVED-DIVERGED` (a seed range > 5) → `SCALAR-NOT-COLLAPSED` (`k01` > 20) → `CONTROL-FAILED` (LOWHEADPATH − `k01` < 20; the COMP-HOLD-BREAKS account) → `REPLICATE-FAILED` (HIGHHEADPATH not AT-K01) → TWO tokens:

### 249.7 The noise floor — through `corpus_exclusions.filter_rows` (OPERATIONS 36)

* **`cvt7`, the scorer log must match the runs directory.** The scorer prints two lines with the runs path in them (`manifest: <runsdir>/cvt7/PARTITION-MANIFEST.txt …` and `provenance: <runsdir>/cvt7/PROVENANCE.txt …`, log lines 102 and 106). The parser rebuilds them from the runsdir it is given and looks them up verbatim; it leaves them out of its own output, so the output does not depend on the host. ### 252.4 What bounds the result, led with

**(1) Below-`k01` floor readings (wording fixes 1, 7).** HOLDBIG is 3.68 pp under `k01` (−6.54 SE) and BIGISOPATH 3.63 pp under (−6.46 SE). Every seed is under its same-seed `k01` run: HOLDBIG by 3.36–3.90 pp (−3.764 / −3.364 / −3.904), BIGISOPATH by 3.36–3.78 pp (−3.360 / −3.752 / −3.784) (plateau5, `Epoch` lines 95–99; re-derived by this track from the raw `.out`). TRAIN is lower too (−4.02, −3.21). `DOSE-FULL` and `BIGISOPATH-AT-K01` name a location at or below `k01`, not agreement at a point.

**(2) `ROUTE-PARTIAL` has the nearest bar.** 3.56 pp (6.33 SE) above `ROUTE-DIRECT`, 7.07 pp below `ROUTE-VIA`. HOLDHIGH carries the batch's largest seed range (1.778, 3.22 under DIVERGED). All three seeds are PARTIAL, and each seed's own seven runs give the same three words.

**(3) `BIGROUTE-DIRECT` compares two arms that are both below `k01`.** Forcing ISOPATH recovered +0.05 pp at PlainNet's dose (per seed +0.40 / −0.39 / +0.12). A recovery smaller than 5 pp cannot be detected at this dose, and the reading does not show that the free complement's collapse plays no role in HOLDBIG.

**(4) Open loop.** The forced complement does not respond to the network; ISOPATH is the median of 12 runs, not a closed-loop trajectory.

**(5) Held set still differs from PlainNet.** `DOSE-FULL` removes the dose confound only (`tri:9428` is bitwise PlainNet's schedule): three carriers together here, tensor 50 alone there.

**(6) Two doses, one shape each, no time gate.** No dose curve and no window can be read on ResNet from this batch.

**(7) The `ROUTE-PARTIAL` recovery accrues late (wording fix 4; DESCRIPTIVE, UNSURE).** Arm mean, HIGHISOPATH − HOLDHIGH: +2.41 / +0.25 at `Epoch` lines 18 / 19, then **below HOLDHIGH on lines 20–40** (−0.96 at 20, −4.37 at 24, −5.58 at 28, −4.85 at 29, −0.81 at 39, −0.69 at 40), above again from line 41, and more than 2 pp above only from line 45 (per seed 45 / 44 / 47), ending +8.45 at line 99 (the line-18/19 values and the line-40 value re-derived by this track). The design cannot say whether the late gain comes from HOLDHIGH's free complement collapsing (pin ~51–56) or from its higher early step size (r over epochs 15–30: 10,414 vs 8,146).

**(8) Scope.** One network, one cell, 100 epochs, the three carriers held together (RULE 11).

**(9) Registered licence wording defect (wording fix 5; RULE 16, reported, not edited).** The printed `BIGROUTE-DIRECT` licence, built by string replacement from `ROUTE-DIRECT`'s, reads "the carriers on PlainNet's dose sit at or below HOLDBIG's level (within 5 pp or lower): the partial loss does NOT need the complement's earlier collapse". At PlainNet's dose HOLDBIG is not a partial loss; it sits 3.68 pp below `k01`. **This record reads it as:** "BIGROUTE-DIRECT (PlainNet's dose): with the complement forced open-loop onto ISO's measured path, the carriers on PlainNet's dose sit at HOLDBIG's level (19.42 vs 19.38, within 5 pp): at this cell and dose, the stall to (below) the `k01` location does not need the complement's earlier collapse (sufficiency; the forced complement is open-loop)." The same replacement garbles the unfired `BIGROUTE-VIA` text ("the ~20 pp loss of cvt7's HOLDBIG"); noted for any successor scorer. The verdict word itself is correct. Separately, BIGISOPATH's `rh_active` reads 41115 and LOWISOPATH s102's 41116; both are audit-consistent.

### 252.8 What this licenses, and what it does not

**Licensed — the registered text for the three words (248.6, as the scorer prints it), read as sufficiency at this cell only** (`ResNet18_c100`, `ciso1`'s cell, 100 epochs, the three carriers held together as ISO's group with their vote out of the complement's sum, forced complement open-loop):

1. **`DOSE-FULL` (fix 7).** Giving the carrier group PlainNet's dose (`tri:9428`, bitwise the schedule that stalled PlainNet), with the complement free, is sufficient to put the run at the `k01` location (in fact 3.68 pp below `k01` by arm mean, −6.54 SE, every seed below; a location, not point agreement). `k01`'s own dose (`tri:8609`) gives only a partial loss (49.63, `BETWEEN`; `cvt7` 50.23). So 247.4(1)'s dose confound is resolved toward dose: at matched absolute step size the ResNet carrier group stalls the run as PlainNet's tensor 50 did. The held-set difference (three tensors vs one) remains.
2. **`ROUTE-PARTIAL` (`k01`'s dose).** Forcing the complement onto ISO's measured path recovers +8.56 pp of HOLDHIGH's 20.63 pp loss but does not reach ISO's level (58.19 vs 70.26): part of the loss is direct and part runs through the complement. No single-route sentence at this dose.
3. **`BIGROUTE-DIRECT` (PlainNet's dose; fixes 5, 6).** With the complement forced open-loop onto ISOPATH, the carriers on PlainNet's dose sit at HOLDBIG's level (19.42 vs 19.38, within 5 pp): the carriers alone are sufficient to reproduce HOLDBIG's stall (`P_ROUTE_BIG` +0.05 pp; per seed +0.40 / −0.39 / +0.12). Because both arms sit about 3.6 pp below `k01`, a recovery smaller than 5 pp could not be detected, and this does not show that the free complement's collapse plays no role in HOLDBIG. The printed licence's "the partial loss" is a string-replacement defect (252.4(9)).
4. **Together (registered sentence).** 240's PlainNet sentence **transfers to `ResNet18_c100` at this cell at PlainNet's dose** — `cvt6`'s HIGHHEADPATH-AT-K01 transplanted to ResNet, with the three carriers held together and an open-loop complement.
5. **`LOWISOPATH-AT-ISO`.** The complement hold alone costs nothing (`P_CTLC` −0.21 pp, −0.37 SE).

**Not licensed.** Necessity; a dose curve; any single carrier; that the held set plays no role; when the step size acts; that an open-loop complement stands in for a responsive one; that the complement contributes nothing in the free arm at `k01`'s dose or at PlainNet's; point agreement at `k01`; `P_INT` as an effect; any other network, cell or horizon (RULE 11).

**DESCRIPTIVE, UNSURE (252.7).** All large-dose arms leave their ISOPATH-matched control by more than 2 pp from `Epoch` line 17 with bitwise-identical complements; HOLDHIGH's free complement repeats `cvt7`'s early pin (magnitude gate 50.8–56.4 vs 52.8–54.0); HOLDBIG's follows the carriers' own `tri:9428` path within 0.19–0.31 and pins at 39.2–39.4, as PlainNet's did; the `ROUTE-PARTIAL` recovery shows only after line 41 (> 2 pp from line 45).

### 253.4 What bounds the result, led with

**(1) No bar is near an arm, but the FINAL has a short single-arm flip (wording fix 2).** HIGHHEADPATH is 2.92 pp inside AT-K01 (worst seed 2.45); EARLY 4.24 pp above its stall bar (worst seed 3.21); MIDDOSE 4.35 pp under AT-CTL (worst seed 4.05); RESDOSE 7.70 pp above AT-K01 and 38.37 under AT-CTL; LATE 10.81 above its stall bar and 32.49 under AT-CTL. **No single window arm can change `WINDOW-GRADED`**: with the other arm PARTIAL, a STALLED or RESCUED arm still reads `WINDOW-GRADED`. **`DOSE-GRADED` changes on one arm only if RESDOSE rises about 39 pp** (`DOSE-NONMONOTONE`); MIDDOSE up 4.35 alone gives nothing new (MID AT-CTL with RES BETWEEN is still GRADED); `DOSE-THRESHOLD` needs MIDDOSE up 4.35 AND RESDOSE down 7.70. **The nearest single-arm change to the whole FINAL is 2.92 pp: HIGHHEADPATH up, or `k01` down, by 2.92 pp gives `REPLICATE-FAILED` and replaces both tokens.**

**(2) The registered accounts did not predict this pattern** (253.3): MIDDOSE sits just under the rescued band and above DOSE-GRADED's 20–50 band; RESDOSE is in the PART band; EARLY sits 1.63 under PART. So "graded" here means "between the bars at two rungs", not a smooth curve.

**(3) Dose is the triangle family.** Peak, fall onset, duration and integrated step size move together (integrated (r − 1) 9.05e6 / 3.58e7 / 8.13e7; clamp at 31.3 / 36.8 / 40.1 epochs). "Peak" cannot be separated from "how long above X".

**(4) One window pair, cut at the peak.** Both halves are PARTIAL, so no single-window sentence is licensed; which sub-window acts is not tested; the halves' losses are not additive (`ADD` +30.33), and the whole is floor-bound, so the sum is uninterpretable as an interaction. LATE starts with a one-update jump from the floor to near-peak step size on a network at ~11.9 % TEST; EARLY ends with a one-update drop. No free trajectory does either.

**(5) The cut is located only to the record grid.** Cuts 9403–9501 all pass `G-BITE`; 9429 rests on the witness (RULE 20) and the CPU schedule test (249.4). Same-seed runs are not bitwise identical before the cut (253.7 [D6]), so same-seed timing splits carry run-to-run noise.

**(6) Open loop.** The complement is forced onto HEADPATH (a median replay) in every held arm; nothing here speaks to a free or responsive complement.

**(7) Floor readings are locations.** HIGHHEADPATH at −0.92 pp vs `k01` is not point agreement.

**(8) `SIGMA-INBATCH`.** σ 0.747 > the prior 0.688, driven by the EARLY / LATE / RESDOSE seed spreads; every seed of every arm is in its arm's state.

**(9) The RESDOSE cross-check is not a network comparison.** On PlainNet `cvt7`'s ResNet trajectory (`tri:8609`) gives 21.84, `BETWEEN`, with 50 alone held and the complement on HEADPATH; on ResNet it gave 50.23 (`cvt7`) and 49.63 (`cvt8`) with three carriers held and a free complement. Network, held set and complement route all differ; between batch only.

**(10) Scope.** One network (`PlainNet18_c100`), one cell (`cvt1`'s), one tensor (idx 50), 100 epochs (RULE 11).

### 253.8 What this licenses, and what it does not

**Licensed — the registered text (249.6, as the scorer prints it), as sufficiency at this cell only** (`PlainNet18_c100`, `cvt1`'s cell, 100 epochs, idx 50's vote out of the complement's sum, complement forced open-loop onto HEADPATH):

* **`DOSE-GRADED`:** "At least one rung sits between k01 and the control (states stamped), monotone within 5 pp: the damage grows with the peak step size across the triangle family rather than switching at one rung. EFFECT ON 240's OWN-STEP-MAGNITUDE and 246's GRADED (HIGHHEADPATH-AT-K01): the stall is GRADED in dose at this cell; read P_MID and P_RES. CROSS-CHECK: RESDOSE's state is the PlainNet level of cvt7's ResNet trajectory. Not licensed: a functional form; any other network." **[Read as (wording fix 7): over the three rungs tried (`tri:7235`, `tri:8609`, `tri:9428`) the level falls through two `BETWEEN` states rather than switching at one of them (sufficiency at this cell; no threshold location or functional form is licensed).]**
* **`WINDOW-GRADED`:** "At least one window arm is PARTIAL (states stamped): each half carries part, or one half partly. EFFECT ON 240's OWN-STEP-MAGNITUDE and 246's GRADED (HIGHHEADPATH-AT-K01): PARTLY LOCATED -- read P_EARLY, P_LATE and P_WIN; no single-window sentence."

**In plain terms, at this cell:**
* **Replicate.** The full large trajectory (`tri:9428`) again puts the run at the `k01` location (11.21).
* **The smallest rung (`tri:7235`, peak −6.58)** is sufficient to cost ~9.4 pp of the control's 65.2 (to 55.86); it does not reach the `k01` location and is not within 5 pp of the control.
* **The ResNet trajectory (`tri:8609`, peak −5.21)** is sufficient to cost ~43.4 pp (to 21.84); it is not sufficient to reach the `k01` location (9.7 pp above it).
* **Either half of the large trajectory alone** is sufficient for a large partial loss; neither is sufficient to reach the `k01` location, and neither keeps the rescue. The rise alone (EARLY) costs 46.8 pp (to 18.37); the peak and fall alone (LATE) 37.5 pp (to 27.71). LATE keeps 9.3 pp more than EARLY (+15.3 SE, same sign on all seeds); the registered branch reads this only as "partly located", not as "the rise does the damage".
* **Relation to earlier batches.** 246's HIGHHEADPATH-AT-K01 and 240's `OWN-STEP-MAGNITUDE` stand. **(fix 7)** What changes: over the three rungs tried the level falls through two `BETWEEN` states rather than switching at one of them, and neither half of the window is on its own the whole story.

**Not licensed.** Necessity of any window or dose; a threshold's location or a functional dose form; which sub-window acts; any statement about ResNet or other networks, including that `cvt7`'s partial loss is or is not a dose effect (that is `cvt8`'s, 252); closed-loop complements, other tensors, cells or horizons; point agreement at `k01`; `ADD` as an interaction.

**(fix 6) DESCRIPTIVE, UNSURE.** EARLY's arm-mean TEST stays within 0.23 pp of HIGHHEADPATH's over lines 0–20 and ends only 7.16 pp above it after 50 returns to the floor. LATE leaves LOWHEADPATH only at line 20, after its window opens inside line 18. RESDOSE and EARLY leave the control at the same line as HIGHHEADPATH (16), MIDDOSE at 18. This describes when the curves separate; it does not say which half is necessary or which sub-window acts, and no registered word rests on it.

### 253.12 What `cvt4`–`cvt9` together say about the mechanism now (registered where marked; descriptive where marked)

* **Registered, PlainNet18_c100 at `cvt1`'s cell, 100 epochs, idx 50's vote out of the complement's sum (`cvt4` 240, `cvt6` 246, `cvt9` 253):** 50 on MUTE's large replayed trajectory (`tri:9428`) is sufficient to put the arm at the `k01` location, with the complement free or forced open-loop onto HEAD's measured path — now replicated three times (11.13, 11.61 / 11.49, 11.21); 50 at the floor keeps HEAD's level. With 50 at the floor, the complement forced onto MUTE's collapse schedule is sufficient for a partial loss (41.56). **Dose:** over the three rungs tried (`tri:7235` / `tri:8609` / `tri:9428`, complement on HEADPATH) the level falls through two `BETWEEN` states (55.86, 21.84) to the `k01` location, rather than switching at one rung; the triangle family moves peak, onset and duration together. **Window:** either half of the large trajectory, cut at its peak, is sufficient for a large partial loss (EARLY 18.37, LATE 27.71) and neither reaches the `k01` location. 240.4(1) PARTLY RESOLVED (246); 246.4(4)'s "no dose curve, no time gate" PARTLY ANSWERED (253), with no functional form and no single-window sentence.
* **Registered, ResNet18_c100 at `ciso1`'s cell, 100 epochs, the three carriers held together (`cvt7` 247, `cvt8` 252):** at `k01`'s own dose (`tri:8609`) the carriers cost ~20 pp of the ~47 pp rescue with the complement free (50.23, 49.63), part of it directly and part through the complement (`ROUTE-PARTIAL`: ISOPATH recovers +8.56 pp, not to ISO); at PlainNet's dose (`tri:9428`) the carriers stall the run to (below) the `k01` location with the complement free (`DOSE-FULL`) and with it forced onto ISO's path (`BIGROUTE-DIRECT`). 247.4(1)'s dose confound RESOLVED TOWARD DOSE; 247.4(2) PARTLY RESOLVED (partial at `k01`'s dose; not needed at PlainNet's dose, within a 5 pp detection limit, open-loop). **240's PlainNet sentence transfers to ResNet18_c100 at this cell at PlainNet's dose** (three carriers together).
* **Descriptive, between batch (orientation only, UNSURE).** The same absolute schedules give the same ordering on both networks: `tri:9428` at (or below) the `k01` location on both; `tri:8609` BETWEEN on both — keeping (arm − `k01`) / (control − `k01`) = 0.18 of the rescue on PlainNet (`cvt9` RESDOSE, complement on HEADPATH, 50 alone) and 0.56 on ResNet (`cvt8` HOLDHIGH, complement free, three carriers; 0.74 with the complement on ISOPATH). Network, held set, control and complement route all differ, so the 0.18 vs 0.56 is not a network effect. On every batch the large-step arm leaves its rescued twin at `Epoch` line 16–17 while the complements are still identical (PlainNet `cvt4` / `cvt6` / `cvt9`: 16; ResNet `cvt7`: 16, `cvt8`: 17), and a free complement next to a large carrier trajectory collapses early (PlainNet onto the carrier's own schedule; ResNet on `tri:9428` likewise, on `tri:8609` at ~53 instead).
* **What stays open:** the held set on ResNet (one carrier vs three, 247.4(1)'s other half); which sub-window of either half acts, and whether the peak neighbourhood alone suffices; a closed-loop (responsive) complement when the carrier is high (242.9); dose ladders on ResNet; every other network, cell and horizon (RULE 11).

### 253.13 RANKED RECOMMENDATION — the next experiments given `cvt4`–`cvt9`, and consolidate or continue (NOT registered, NOTHING launched)

Per-run cost by `sacct`: **ResNet18_c100, 100 epochs ≈ 0.82 GPU-h** (`cvt8` 62,269 s / 21, three on [HOST_3c1b003035]); **PlainNet18_c100, 100 epochs ≈ 0.82 GPU-h** (`cvt9` 61,778 s / 21, four on [HOST_3c1b003035]; ≈ 0.67 off [HOST_3c1b003035], `cvt6`).

**Consolidate or continue: CONSOLIDATE.** The mechanism line should now be written up (a mechanism section or appendix of the partition-audit write-up; `paper/` is not touched by this track) rather than extended by default. Why:
1. **Every bound the last three landings led with has been answered at the level the designs can reach.** 240.4(1) (direct vs via complement) and 247.4(2) are PARTLY RESOLVED on both networks; 247.4(1)'s dose confound is resolved toward dose; 246.4(4)'s "no dose curve, no time gate" now has three rungs and one window pair. The headline sentence — a large step size on the carrier BN scale(s) is sufficient to stall the run to the scalar arm's level, and the step sizes that keep the rescue are small — is registered on two networks, replicated, and survives every open-loop control.
2. **Each further split keeps returning "partial".** `GRADED` (246), `TRANSFERS-GRADED` (247), `ROUTE-PARTIAL` (252), `DOSE-GRADED` and `WINDOW-GRADED` (253): halving a window or adding a rung has, five times running, produced BETWEEN states rather than a sharp location. That pattern is itself the finding (a continuous, cumulative effect of step size on these scales), and another binary split is most likely to add a sixth "partial" without changing a sentence a reader would quote.
3. **Returns per GPU-hour are falling and code cost is rising.** Each remaining question needs a new patch or grouping (a window on `GROUP_HOLD`, a closed-loop complement, a singleton hold), ≈15–17 GPU-h and a full registration cycle, to refine a supporting section rather than the audit's headline (the count-matched partition effect, which none of these batches can move).
4. **What is missing is not more data but a single consistent account.** Six registered landings with their bounds, replicated levels (HIGHHEADPATH/HOLDHIGH at `k01` ×4 on PlainNet; HOLDHIGH ×2 on ResNet) and the cross-batch timing regularity (line 16–17) are enough for a write-up; writing it will show which one sentence, if any, still lacks a registered arm.

**If the operator nevertheless runs one more batch, the ranking is:**

### 253.15 Addendum (final audit, zero GPU): the single-arm flip sentence for `DOSE-GRADED` was incomplete

The sentence "`DOSE-GRADED` changes on one arm only if RESDOSE rises ~39 pp" (253 header bound (1), 253.4(1), 253.6 fix 2, MASTER-TABLE row 227's so-what cell) omits a second single-arm route. In the registered `decide()` of `analysis/cVT9_dosewindow_score.py` (`5c53a40d…`, read, not edited), `DOSE-NONMONOTONE` fires when RESDOSE − MIDDOSE > 5 before any state is read. At the landed means (MIDDOSE 55.8553, RESDOSE 21.8387; difference −34.0166), that happens if RESDOSE rises **or MIDDOSE falls** by more than **39.02 pp**. A MIDDOSE at 16.84 would still be `BETWEEN` (above 14.1347), so the branch reads `NONMONOTONE`, not `ALL-STALL`. The sentence should read: "`DOSE-GRADED` changes on one arm only if RESDOSE rises, or MIDDOSE falls, by ~39 pp (`DOSE-NONMONOTONE`)." Checked by calling the scorer's own `decide()` on the landed means while moving one arm at a time in 0.01 pp steps (LATE onset 11.90). The only other single-arm flips are the whole-FINAL ones: HIGHHEADPATH +2.93 / `k01` −2.93 → `REPLICATE-FAILED`; `k01` +7.87 → `SCALAR-NOT-COLLAPSED`; LOWHEADPATH −33.08 → `CONTROL-FAILED`. The same check on `cvt8`'s `decide()` reproduces 252.3 exactly (nearest 3.56 pp → `ROUTE-DIRECT`; whole FINAL at 5.21 pp). No number, gate, token or outcome moves. MASTER-TABLE row 227 is left as it stands; this entry is the correction.

*Note, added after this entry: MASTER-TABLE row 227 has since been amended in place. Its so-what cell now reads "DOSE-GRADED changes on one arm only if RESDOSE rises, or MIDDOSE falls, by ~39 pp (DOSE-NONMONOTONE)", followed by a `CORRECTED IN PLACE at cycle 153, CORRECTIONS 253.15` bracket that keeps the superseded wording verbatim; no line moved, and `analysis/c73_mastertable_check.py`, run unedited, exits 0. The sentence above saying the row is left as it stands no longer holds; no number, gate, token or outcome moves.*

### 255.1 PRIOR ART (the user's rule: checked BEFORE designing; queries run 2026-09-17)

* **Queries.** arXiv API: `abs:hypergradient AND abs:"learning rate" AND abs:momentum`; `abs:"learning rate" AND abs:"weight decay" AND abs:"batch normalization" AND abs:instability` (0 hits); `abs:"meta-learned learning rate" OR abs:"learned step size" OR abs:"step-size adaptation" AND abs:momentum AND abs:collapse` (15 hits, none on topic); `ti:/abs:"short-horizon bias"`; `abs:"spherical motion dynamics" OR ti:"weight decay" AND abs:momentum AND abs:"angular update"`; `abs:hypergradient AND abs:"weight decay" AND abs:"step size"` (0 hits); `abs:"effective learning rate" AND abs:momentum AND abs:"weight decay" AND abs:normalization`; `abs:"learning rate" AND abs:hypergradient AND abs:"batch normalization"` (0 hits); `abs:"no bias decay" OR (weight decay AND batch normalization AND gamma)`; `abs:"step-size" AND abs:"meta-gradient" AND abs:momentum AND (IDBD OR "stochastic meta-descent" OR "learning rate adaptation")` (0 hits); `abs:learning rate AND meta AND momentum AND "weight decay" AND online AND hyperparameter` (0 hits, 2019+).  Web: "hypergradient descent learning rate collapse momentum 0.99 weight decay batch normalization"; "MetaOptimize step size adaptation scalar blockwise momentum sensitivity follow-up"; "hypergradient learning rate adaptation momentum sensitivity step size vanishes"; "arXiv 2402.02342 MetaOptimize cited by … scalar collapse CIFAR-100 SGD momentum".
* **Closest papers (each read on its arXiv abstract page or ar5iv HTML, in place):**

| paper | id | what it establishes | relation to `cmo1` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wu, Ren, Liao, Grosse, *Understanding Short-Horizon Bias in Stochastic Meta-Optimization* | arXiv:1803.02021 (2018) | short-horizon meta-objectives bias meta-optimisation toward too-small step sizes, by orders of magnitude, even at 100-step horizons | a generic, momentum-independent reason for a shrinking meta-learned step size: a prior FOR `COLLAPSE-PERSISTS`; says nothing about carriers, momentum or WD |
| Baydin, Cornish, Martinez Rubio, Schmidt, Wood, *Online Learning Rate Adaptation with Hypergradient Descent* | arXiv:1703.04782 (2017) | hypergradient LR adaptation on SGD, SGD-Nesterov and Adam | tunes one LR with momentum present; no momentum or WD ablation of a failure reported in the abstract |
| Chu, Gao, Ye, Udell, *Provable and Practical Online Learning Rate Adaptation with Hypergradient Descent* | arXiv:2502.11229 (ICML 2025, PMLR v267 per search result) | first convergence analysis of HDM; explains its reported instability; heavy-ball / Nesterov HDM variants robust on DETERMINISTIC CONVEX problems | the nearest "momentum × hypergradient" result: convex, deterministic, no normalisation — does not answer ours |
| Wan, Zhu, Zhang, Sun, *Spherical Motion Dynamics* | arXiv:2006.08419 (2020) | with normalisation + WD + SGD(M), the angular update equilibrates at √(2λη/(1+α)) (ar5iv, Theorem 3; heavy-ball momentum α) | predicts WD and momentum change the effective rate of scale-INVARIANT weights; the carriers are BN gammas (scale-variant), and our SGDm is the EMA form (no 1/(1−μ) gain) — mechanism-adjacent, not an answer |
| Kosson, Messmer, Jaggi, *Rotational Equilibrium* | arXiv:2305.17212 (ICML 2024, as 254) | with WD, per-layer angular updates equilibrate; a shared LR gives unequal effective rates until then | predicts W0 removes the equilibrating force — W0 could plausibly DEEPEN or REMOVE the collapse; untested for a meta-learned LR |
| Summers, Dinneen, *Four Things Everyone Should Know to Improve Batch Normalization* | arXiv:1906.03548 (2019) | WD on BN gamma/beta: +0.3% on CIFAR-100 ResNet-18 (ar5iv), helps only with norm-free paths to the output | WD on gamma is a live, architecture-dependent effect at exactly our dataset/network — W0 is not a null change |
| He, Zhang, Zhang, Zhang, Xie, Li, *Bag of Tricks for Image Classification* | arXiv:1812.01187 (2018) | "no bias decay": WD only on conv/FC weights, BN γ/β unregularised (ar5iv) | common practice avoids what our cell does (coupled WD on gammas) — the reviewer line LIMITS-PREP §6 anticipates |
| Chandra, Xie, Ragan-Kelley, Meijer, *Gradient Descent: The Ultimate Optimizer* | arXiv:1909.13371 | hyper-optimises step size (and other hyper-parameters) by autodiff | adjacent; no momentum/WD failure analysis in the abstract |
| Sharifnassab, Salehkaleybar, Sutton, *MetaOptimize* | arXiv:2402.02342 (ICML 2025) | the parent; scalar (SGDm, Lion) reported working on ImageNet at momentum parsed as 0.9 (254 / LIMITS-PREP 2.3, alignment UNSURE) | the reason the question is sharp |

* **Verdict: `WORTH-TESTING`.**  Nothing read reports whether a meta-learned SHARED step size's collapse, or a per-group rescue of it, depends on the base optimiser's momentum or weight decay; the searches pairing hypergradient / meta-step-size with weight decay or batch normalisation return 0 arXiv hits.  The literature gives priors in BOTH directions (short-horizon bias → persists; WD/momentum-driven effective-rate equilibria and gamma-WD effects → could be configuration-bound), so the answer is not already published.  **Not reshaped**, with one refinement taken from the reading: the base SGDm in this harness is the EMA form (`m ← μm + (1−μ)g`, live `SGDm_base_update`), so "momentum 0.9" changes the averaging window (100 → 10 steps), NOT the effective step scale; the licence text says so and no heavy-ball effective-LR argument is licensed.

### 255.2 Design (LIMITS-PREP 5.1 S1a, refined)

* **Cell.** `ciso1`'s / `cdep1`'s / `cvt8`'s exactly: CIFAR-100, `ResNet18_c100` (62 tensors, 11,220,132 params), Lion meta (0.99, b2 0.9, wd 0), ms 1e-3, alpha0 1e-6, gamma 1, 100 ep, batch 100, `AUGMENT=1`, `BETA_CLIP=-15:-2.3026`, `PROBE=100`, `PROBE_TENSOR=1` on every arm; the ENV line is `ciso1`'s byte for byte (scorer `G-ENV`).
* **Arms (9 × 3 = 27).** `k01` scalar / `kL` layerwise / ISO (`sets:1-49,51-52,54-58,60-62/layer4.0.bn2.weight,layer4.0.shortcut.1.weight,layer4.1.bn2.weight`, byte-identical to `cIS1`'s, `cDP1`'s and `cVT8`'s — selftest B) at (momentum 0.99, WD 0.1); the same three at (0.9, 0.1) = `M9k01 / M9kL / M9ISO`; the same three at (0.99, 0) = `W0k01 / W0kL / W0ISO`.  Exactly ONE factor differs from the anchor twin (selftest A, launcher's per-line `expected_args` check).
* **The anchor triple is included, and it is why the batch is 27 not 24.**  5.1 priced S1a at 24 runs (base {k01, kL} + 2 × {k01, kL, ISO}); the ISO anchor (+3 runs) is added so that the rescue interactions `IR_X = R_X − R_A` and the anchor gate `ISO − k01 ≥ 20` are WITHIN batch at fresh seeds — no corpus anchor enters any contrast.
* **Seeds {108, 109, 110}; 111 not used.**  Fresh: 0 corpus rows carry 108–111, 0 `.out` ARGS lines under `$WS/runs`, 0 `sacct` jobs named `cmo1-` (guards 1c4, 2d, 2e; `cmo1-` also absent from repo, CSV and runs dir).  A fourth seed (36 runs, ≈33 GPU-h) would exceed the 1.3 × 19.7 = 25.6 GPU-h ceiling; 3 seeds match every earlier batch at this cell.
* **Cost.** 0.92 GPU-h/run (`cvt7` sacct incl. [HOST_3c1b003035]) → **≈24.8 GPU-h expected** (≈19.2 off [HOST_3c1b003035]; within 1.3 × 5.1's 19.7); **hard bound 81** (WALL 03:00:00 × 27).  Registration spend: 0 GPU-h (the flag proof is CPU).
* **Names re-derived on the LIVE model** (launcher guard 4, dry run): idx 50 / 53 / 59 = `layer4.0.bn2.weight`, `layer4.0.shortcut.1.weight`, `layer4.1.bn2.weight`, BatchNorm2d, 512 each; ISO → `[59,3]`, params `[11218596, 1536]`; layerwise → beta shape (62,); scalar → (); no `_rednorm`.  The live manifest is byte-identical to the scorer's `synthetic_manifest_text()` (4,554 bytes).

* **COLLAPSE-IS-CONFIG vs COLLAPSE-PERSISTS is the question the brief asks** (`k01` recovers at 0.9 or WD 0, or not), and **"ISO still rescues where k01 still collapses"** is the ISO word inside a `COLLAPSE-PERSISTS` or `COLLAPSE-ATTENUATED` half.
* Selftest C: every account's midpoint AND both range corners land in its registered branch; the null's levels give ROBUST's branch.

### 255.4 Gates, branches, licences — `decide()`, first match wins; frozen bars

* **Harness gates** (→ `HARNESS-UNSOUND`, rc 1): `G-ARGS` (each run's own ARGS line == `expected_args(arm, seed)` flag by flag, the two factor flags included; no repeat, no unregistered flag); `G-ENV` (one ENV line == `ciso1`'s; one `PROBE_TENSOR: on … type=<scalar|layerwise|blockwise> tensors=62`); **`G-NOSWITCH`** (no `VOTE_W` / `BETA_HOLD` / `GROUP_HOLD` / `COMP_HOLD` / `REST_HOLD` / `WINDOW_HOLD` / `DECAY_MASK` / `SHADOW_VOTE` line — the live harness prints none); `G-STRUCT` (manifest byte-identical); `G-PROV` (MODE submit; LIVE build_network / HF / train.py / runner shas; this scorer's sha); `G-FLOOR` ≥ 15, `G-CEIL` ≤ 90.
* **`G-TBARGS`** (→ `FLAGS-NOT-VERIFIED`, rc 1, BEFORE any contrast): `train.py` writes `vars(args)` — after argparse and the −1 → None mapping — as a `|key|value|` table into each run's own `runs/cmo1/Tensorboard_outputs/<run>/events.out.tfevents.*` (verified on `ciso1-k01-s21` / `ciso1-ISO-s21`: `|momentum_param_base|0.99|`, `|weight_decay_base|0.1|`, `|weight_decay_meta|0.0|`).  The gate requires, for every run, each of 17 registered keys once-valued and equal (`momentum_param_base` 0.99 / 0.9; `weight_decay_base` 0.1 / **0.0**; alg, meta flags, `stepsize_groups`, seed, run name, …).  Selftest E: a witness of 0.99 on `M9k01`, 0.1 on `W0ISO`, a missing events file, a two-valued table → `FLAGS-NOT-VERIFIED`.
* **Branch.** `UNRESOLVED-DIVERGED` (an ANCHOR arm's seed range > 5) → `ANCHOR-FAILED` (`k01` > 30, or `kL − k01` < 20, or `ISO − k01` < 20) → `M9:<C>/<I>+W0:<C>/<I>`, a half with a diverged arm reading `X:DIVERGED`.  C: `XkL` < 45 → `REF-UNHEALTHY`; `XkL − Xk01` ≤ 5 → `COLLAPSE-IS-CONFIG`; `Xk01` ≤ 0.5 `XkL` and `XkL − Xk01` ≥ 20 → `COLLAPSE-PERSISTS` (the 254 census's R50 plus the gap bar); else `COLLAPSE-ATTENUATED`.  I: unreadable when C is `REF-UNHEALTHY` / `COLLAPSE-IS-CONFIG` or the gap ≤ 10; `XISO` ≥ `XkL − 5` → `ISO-RESCUES`; `XISO` ≤ `Xk01 + 5` → `ISO-FAILS`; else `ISO-PARTIAL` (disjoint once the gap > 10; selftest A).  126 registered branches, each with a licence; a 20,000-draw sweep reaches every word.
* **Co-primaries (in batch, unbounded):** `G_X = XkL − Xk01`, `R_X = XISO − Xk01`, `L_X = Xk01 − k01`.  KEY: `G_A`, `R_A`, `DL_X = XkL − kL`, `DI_X = XISO − ISO`, `IG_X = G_X − G_A`, `IR_X = R_X − R_A`, and the ratio `Xk01 / XkL` beside the anchor's.
* **Frozen bars (O2).** GAP_MIN 20.0 (35.96 SE at the prior), K01_MAX 30.0, REF_MIN 45.0, R50 0.5, MATCH 5.0 (8.99 SE), RESCUE 10.0, NULL 2.0 (3.60 SE), DIVERGED 5.0, FLOOR_MIN 15.0, CEIL_MAX 90.0.  SIGMA_USED = max(frozen floor, in-batch, df 18).
* **Stamps.** Always `HARNESS-CLEAN`, `FLAGS-WITNESSED`, `LIVE-HARNESS`, `ONE-VALUE-PER-FACTOR`, `ONE-FACTOR-AT-A-TIME`, `ISO-IS-CISO1-CARRIERS`, `NO-CTL-AT-NEW-CONFIGS`, `ONE-NETWORK-RESNET`, `HORIZON-100-ONLY`, `ALPHA0-1E-6`, `SIGMA-PRIOR-FROZEN`/`-INBATCH`.  Conditional: `ANCHOR-REPRODUCES`; `X-K01-LIFTED` (≥ 10 above `k01`), `X-K01-AT-ANCHOR` (within 2), `X-K01-BELOW-ANCHOR`; `X-KL-DROPPED` (≥ 10); `X-GAP-TOO-SMALL-FOR-ISO`; `X-ISO-AT-REF` / `-BELOW-REF` in unreadable halves; `X-ISO-ABOVE-REF`; `UNBRANCHED-HALVES-…` on the two stop branches; `DIVERGED-<arms>`; `FLOOR-READINGS-ARE-BOUNDS`; `TRAIN-AGREES` / `-DISAGREES`.  After FINAL, DESCRIPTIVE and non-gating: per scalar arm, each carrier's share of Σ|z_tensor| over the 500 records and the top-5 tensors (does `ciso1`'s trio still dominate the vote at M9 / W0?).
* **Licences, in words.** `COLLAPSE-PERSISTS`: "at this cell the scalar collapse does not require SGDm momentum 0.99 / coupled base WD"; `COLLAPSE-IS-CONFIG`: "… requires it", and the carrier account becomes a mechanism OF THAT CONFIGURATION (LIMITS-PREP §6); `COLLAPSE-ATTENUATED`: "deepens it, not required for a gap"; `ISO-RESCUES`: "and isolating the carriers still rescues" (not specificity: no CTL at M9 / W0, that is S4); `ISO-FAILS`: "the collapse at X does not run through THESE carriers" (not re-nominated).  Never licensed: the parent's exact configuration (alpha0 1e-6 not 1e-5), an interaction or a dose curve, other networks / datasets / horizons, and for W0 which route (WD on gammas vs WD in the meta trace `h ← γ(1 − wd·a)h − δ`, removed together).

* **No layerwise arm.**  LIMITS-PREP prices S2 at k01 / ISO / CTL; the claim registered is within batch (ISO vs `k01`, CTL vs `k01`, ISO vs CTL). ### 256.3 The nomination check and the statistics (defined in `analysis/cCV0_carrier_vote_core.py`, shared with `cct1`, sha-pinned in both scorers)

* Per record (500 per run, steps 0…49,900): `L_i = b2·m_i + (1−b2)·z_i` from the record's own `m_tensor` / `z_tensor` (the term that enters the sign `Lion_meta_update` applies, cTD2 184.1(1)); `s` = the harness's own `sign(b2·mom_pre + (1−b2)·z_agg)` on scalar runs, `sign(Σ L_i)` (the counterfactual shared vote) elsewhere.  **DOM_C** ⇔ `sign(Σ_C L_i) = s` and `|Σ_C L_i| > Σ_{i∉C} |L_i|`; **TOP3_C** ⇔ the three largest `|L_i|` are C.  Pooled over `k01`'s 1,500 records.
* **`NOMINATED`** ⇔ DOM_C ≥ 0.50 and TOP3_C ≥ 0.50; **`NOT-NOMINATED`** ⇔ DOM_C ≤ 0.10; else **`NOMINATION-PARTIAL`**.
* **Calibration** (`analysis/cst1_cct1_registration_derivations.py`, output `a0f1cbb9…` on the Mac mirror, reproduced on cluster_b by launcher guard 1e): scalar `ctd1` sc s18–20, `ciso1` k01 s21–23, `cdep1` k01 s24–26: DOM_C 0.820 / 0.784 / 0.810 / 0.806 / 0.786 / 0.806 / 0.814 / 0.816 / 0.820, pooled **0.8069**; TOP3_C 0.822–0.824 (pooled 0.8238); by decile 0.00 0.19 1.00 0.99 0.98 0.97 0.98 0.98 0.99 0.99; on pinned records 0.9827.  Layerwise `ctd1` lay, `ciso1` k62, `cdep1` k62: **0.0000 / 0.0000 on all 9** (the carriers' SHARE_C median 0.041; `linear.weight` is the argmax on 4,208 / 4,500).  Every calibration run passes the core's decomposition check.  **Not discriminative, printed only:** DOM_TOP3 (whichever three are largest fix the sign) — 0.92 scalar, 0.91 layerwise.
* **Disclosure.** At 1e-3 the dominance begins at the ascent peak (~step 9,000) and is near-total in the pinned phase; 3e-4 has no pinned phase in the corpus (181.5), so its DOM_C could sit anywhere.  UNSURE.

### 256.5 Gates, branches, licences — `score()` / `decide()`, first match wins; frozen bars

* **`INCOMPLETE` (rc 2)**: fewer than 9 complete `.out` (RUN_DONE, epochs 0–99, finite plateau5, no traceback) or fewer than 500 records on a run; a truncated resubmission never shadows a complete run (highest COMPLETE job id wins).
* **`HARNESS-UNSOUND` (rc 1)**: `G-CORE` (core sha `0754ca84…`); `G-PROV` (`runs/cst1/PROVENANCE.txt`: MODE submit; HF `4732b74a…`, build_network `c7998883…`, train.py `3fea309e…`, runner `a0d0a1b9…`, core, this scorer); `G-STRUCT` (manifest byte-identical); `G-ARGS` (the one ARGS line == `args_line(arm, seed)` verbatim); `G-ENV` (one ENV line == `ciso1`'s modulo PROBE_DIR, which must be the run's own); `G-PT` (one `PROBE_TENSOR` line, type scalar / blockwise per arm, `dir` == PROBE_DIR); **`G-FOREIGN`** (no `VOTE_W` / `BETA_HOLD` / `GROUP_HOLD` / `COMP_HOLD` / `REST_HOLD` / `WINDOW_HOLD` / `DECAY_MASK` / `SHADOW_VOTE` / `WD_SCALE` line — the live tree prints none); `G-HEADER` (`probe_tensor.json`, ResNet18_c100 numels); `G-RECORDS` (steps 0…49,900).
* **`SPEC-NOT-APPLIED` (rc 1)**: `G-SPEC` — every record of `k01` carries 1 beta and 1 `z_agg` coordinate, of ISO / CTL 2.
* **`UNRESOLVED-DECOMPOSITION` (rc 1)**: `G-DECOMP` — group sums of `z_tensor` / `m_tensor` equal the harness's `z_agg` / `mom_pre` (rel. 1e-5 / 1e-4) and `−(beta − beta_pre)/ms = sign(L)` on unclamped coordinates, each on ≥ 99 % of records.
* **`decide()`** (reads no record): `UNRESOLVED-DIVERGED` (an arm's seed range > 5.0, or a run outside [5, 90]) → `SCALAR-NOT-COLLAPSED` (`k01` > 34.0) → **`<NOM>+<ISO>+<CTL>`**: ISO-RESCUES `D_ISO = ISO − k01` ≥ 20.0, ISO-NO-RESCUE ≤ 5.0, else ISO-PARTIAL; CTL-RESCUES `D_CTL` ≥ 20.0, CTL-NULL ≤ 5.0, else CTL-PARTIAL.  29 branches, each with a licence (selftest A).
* **Frozen bars (O2).** DOM_HI 0.50, DOM_LO 0.10, TOP3 0.50, RESCUE 20.0 (35.96 SE), NULL 5.0 (8.99 SE), K01_MAX 34.0, DIVERGED 5.0, LEVEL [5, 90]; SIGMA_PRIOR 0.6811983409351905, SE_PRIOR 0.556196.
* **Licences.** `NOMINATED+ISO-RESCUES+CTL-NULL`: *"at ms 3e-4 (CIFAR-100, ResNet18_c100, otherwise the mechanism cell) k01's own records nominate the same three carriers, isolating them recovers ≥ 20 pp over k01 and the matched non-carrier set stays within 5 pp: the carrier rescue holds at a second meta step size"* (sufficiency of isolating C, at this cell).  `…+CTL-RESCUES`: not carrier-specific at 3e-4.  `NOMINATED+ISO-NO-RESCUE+…`: nomination not sufficient for the rescue here.  `NOT-NOMINATED+ISO-RESCUES+CTL-NULL`: the rescue does not need the carriers' vote dominance.  `NOT-NOMINATED+ISO-NO-RESCUE+CTL-NULL`: the carrier account does not transfer to 3e-4.  Others: composed per word.  **Never licensed:** other datasets / networks / alpha0 / horizons; necessity; why CTL sits where it sits; a scalar-vs-layerwise gap measured in batch.
* **Stamps.** Always `HARNESS-CLEAN`, `SPEC-APPLIED`, `DECOMPOSITION-OK`, `DOM_C=`, `TOP3_C=`, `PINNED-FRAC=`, `ONE-CELL-MS-3E-4`, `ALPHA0-1E-6-ONLY`, `HORIZON-100-ONLY`, `ONE-NETWORK-RESNET18_C100`, `CTL-HAS-A-BIAS-MEMBER`, `NO-LAYERWISE-IN-BATCH`, `NOMINATION-FROM-K01-RECORDS-ONLY`, `SIGMA-PRIOR-FROZEN`; conditional `FLOOR-READINGS-ARE-BOUNDS`, `CTL-ABOVE-ISO`, `TRAIN-AGREES` / `-DISAGREES(…)`, `UNBRANCHED-<NOM>`.  Descriptive after FINAL: per-seed vote statistics, the counterfactual vote inside ISO and CTL, beta peak / terminal / floor share per group.

### 257.1 PRIOR ART

* **The sweep is 256.1's** (one set of queries for the pair: which layers dominate global / shared adaptive learning rates or hypergradients; last-layer BN gamma dominance in gradient statistics).  The paper that bears most directly on S3 is **Gray, Tiwari, Bergsma, Hestness, arXiv:2411.00999 (2024)**: in HEALTHY transformer training the normalisation layers' per-example gradients alone predict the TOTAL gradient noise scale — so "normalisation parameters stand in for a global gradient statistic without anything failing" has precedent, for a different statistic (noise scale, unsigned) on a different architecture.  **Tomihari & Sato, arXiv:2502.00213 (2025)**: block-level gradient heterogeneity is architecture-shaped and harms SGD, sign methods less so.  **LARS (arXiv:1708.03888, 254)**: per-layer ‖w‖/‖g‖ spans orders of magnitude in healthy BN nets.  From the campaign itself (184.4, descriptive): per ELEMENT, BN scales are the largest class under both scalar and layerwise dynamics at the CIFAR-100 cell; the carriers' TOTAL dominance was scalar-trajectory-specific (rank 5 / 6 / 11 and ~30× smaller under layerwise).
* **Verdict: `WORTH-TESTING`.**  No paper attributes a shared hypergradient / meta-gradient SIGN to named tensors on a non-failing run, and the corpus holds no per-tensor record on CIFAR-10.  The priors point both ways (Gray et al. and LARS → dominance may be generic; 184.4 → dominance was trajectory-specific), so the answer is not published.  **Refinement:** LIMITS-PREP priced S3 as `k01` + probe ×3; the batch adds `kL` ×3 so that "does not collapse" is measured IN BATCH (batch is the campaign's unit of replication, F(62,85) = 5.47, 188) and the layerwise vote is read beside the scalar one (184.4's companion).  Cost +2.5–2.8 GPU-h; the S2 + S3 pair is 15 runs = 1.24 × 5.1's 9.9 GPU-h at its 0.82 / run (1.39 × at 0.92 / run incl. [HOST_3c1b003035]).

### 258.1 PRIOR ART (the user's rule; queries run 2026-09-18, every paper read on its arXiv abstract page in place — no PDF fetched, no file downloaded)

* **Queries.**  Web: "per-layer learning rate sensitivity batch normalization gamma residual branch last BN shortcut ResNet"; "hypergradient meta-learned per-layer learning rates which layers dominate shared learning rate collapse"; "\"shortcut\" batch norm gamma versus residual branch gamma different roles learning rate instability single layer ablation"; "which normalization layers require separate learning rate minimal subset layers training collapse hypergradient layerwise step size".  arXiv API: `abs:"learning rate" AND abs:"batch normalization" AND (abs:"single layer" OR abs:"which layers") AND abs:"residual"` and `abs:"learning rate" AND abs:"batch normalization" AND abs:"residual" AND (abs:"per-layer" OR abs:"layer-wise")` — **both returned HTTP 429 (rate limited) and were NOT re-run**; the web queries above cover the same ground and 254's 2026-09-17 sweep (≈70 papers, `docs/PRIOR-ART.md`) was read first and is not repeated.
* **Closest verified papers.**

| paper | id | verified where | what it establishes | relation to `cvt10` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kim, Choi, Jang, Lee, Jeong, Kim, *Guidelines for the Regularization of Gammas in Batch Normalization for Deep Residual Networks* | arXiv:2205.07260 (15 May 2022); ACM TIST 15(3) 2024, DOI 10.1145/3643860 | arXiv abstract page, 2026-09-18 | gamma's admissibility for L2 depends on its POSITION in the residual block (the abstract states the two analyses — variance control and "stable optimization through the improvement of effective learning rate" — but does not itself name last-in-branch vs shortcut; that distinction is in the body, filed at 254) | **the only lead for 3-vs-1**: it is the one paper that treats `layer4.x.bn2.weight` (last-in-branch, "gamma_last") and `layer4.0.shortcut.1.weight` (projection, "gamma_down") as different categories — for L2, NOT for step size, and never one tensor at a time |
| De, Smith, *Batch Normalization Biases Residual Blocks Towards the Identity Function in Deep Networks* | arXiv:2002.10444 (24 Feb 2020), NeurIPS 2020 | arXiv abstract page, 2026-09-18 | BN downscales the residual branch relative to the skip connection by ≈√depth; "batch normalized networks can be trained with larger learning rates" | ADJACENT: the residual branch's scale is the object, so a last-in-branch gamma is a plausible single lever — but nothing there varies ONE tensor's learning rate, and the shortcut BN is not contrasted with it |
| Arora/Li/Lyu (1812.03981), You et al. LARS (1708.03888), Davis & Frank (2110.13989), MimicNorm (2010.09278) | as 254 | as 254 | scale-invariance gives BN an auto-tuned effective LR; per-layer ‖w‖/‖g‖ spans three orders; gamma wants its own smaller LR; a last BN carries trainability at large LR | the "of course normalisation scales are LR-sensitive" background; none isolates a SINGLE tensor, none holds a step-size trajectory, none counts how many tensors are needed |

* **In-corpus prior art (the campaign's own; the literature cannot see it).**  `cdep1`'s ONE arm ({50} alone, FREE) 64.8267 and `ciso1`'s ONE 64.7500 — one tensor's own group largely rescues on ResNet; `cvt4` / `cvt6` (PlainNet): ONE tensor (idx 50) HELD on `tri:9428` stalls to the scalar level; `cvt8`: on ResNet the THREE carriers held together at that dose stall (HOLDBIG 19.3780 under `k01` 23.0553, `DOSE-FULL`), and no ResNet arm has ever held ONE tensor at that dose (252.8(1)'s remaining confound — held set 3 vs 1 — is exactly what this batch attacks).
* **Verdict: `WORTH-TESTING`.**  No paper asks how MANY individual normalisation-scale tensors must carry a large step size for training to stall, and none compares a last-in-branch gamma with the projection-shortcut gamma under a step-size intervention.  The question is also not answerable from the corpus: `cdep1`/`ciso1` vary a tensor's GROUPING (free), never its step-size TRAJECTORY.  Reshaped in one way only: **the shortcut carrier 53 is added as a third singleton pair** (ONE53 / ONE53BIG, +6 runs over LIMITS-PREP's 24) so that Kim et al.'s position category is a within-batch contrast rather than a story told after the fact (258.9).

### 258.2 What the words would and would not mean (registered before any run exists)

* **`ONE-SUFFICES` (any single `ONE<s>BIG` ≤ `k01` + 2 while its free twin rescues by ≥ 10 pp)** would mean: at this cell, ONE carrier isolated ALONE in its own step-size group and held on PlainNet's dose — with every other tensor, the other two carriers included, on one free shared Lion step size — puts the run at the `k01` location.  For that carrier the held SET is not needed at this dose, and 240 / 246's PlainNet sentence ("one tensor on this dose stalls") TRANSFERS to ResNet18_c100 for that tensor.  **Sufficiency, at that cell only.**
* **`NO-ONE-SUFFICES`** would mean: neither last-in-branch carrier (50, 59), alone and held, stalls the run, while the three held together (HOLDBIG3) do — i.e. the held set **differs by network at matched absolute dose**.  It would NOT say why, which pair would do, or that no LARGER single-tensor dose would stall.
* **NOT licensed by any branch:** necessity (every reading is what a hold is SUFFICIENT to do); any other network, cell, dose (one dose, `tri:9428`), horizon (100 epochs) or timing (every hold runs from init); any PAIR of carriers (not run); a category law from one tensor per category; `ISOSPLIT`'s cost against its OWN free partition (`[59,1,2]` free is NOT run — stamp `NO-FREE-SPLIT-CONTROL`); and point agreement at the `k01` level, which is read as a LOCATION (164.6).

### 258.3 The design — ten arms, one variable per contrast

| arm | `--stepsize-groups` | `GROUP_HOLD` | role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `k01` | `scalar` | unset | the floor anchor (PROBE_TENSOR on, as on every arm) |
| `ISO` | `sets:1-49,51-52,54-58,60-62/…bn2,…shortcut.1,…bn2` `[59,3]` | unset | positive control, byte-identical to `ciso1` / `cdep1` / `cvt8` |
| `HOLDBIG3` | ISO's | `…bn2+…shortcut.1+…bn2:tri:9428` | `cvt8`'s HOLDBIG replicated in batch at new seeds |
| `ONE50` / `ONE50BIG` | `sets:1-49,51-62/layer4.0.bn2.weight` `[61,1]` | unset / `layer4.0.bn2.weight:tri:9428` | `cdep1` / `ciso1`'s ONE, and its hold |
| `ONE59` / `ONE59BIG` | `sets:1-58,60-62/layer4.1.bn2.weight` | unset / `layer4.1.bn2.weight:tri:9428` | the final block's gamma_last (never run free before) |
| `ONE53` / `ONE53BIG` | `sets:1-52,54-62/layer4.0.shortcut.1.weight` | unset / `layer4.0.shortcut.1.weight:tri:9428` | the projection-shortcut gamma_down (never run free before) |
| `ISOSPLIT` | `…/layer4.0.bn2.weight/layer4.0.shortcut.1.weight,layer4.1.bn2.weight` `[59,1,2]` | `layer4.0.bn2.weight:tri:9428` | 50 held with 53 and 59 OUT of the complement's vote |

Every held arm's spec is BYTE-IDENTICAL to its free twin's; only `GROUP_HOLD` differs (the selftest checks this).  `tri:9428`: u(n) = min(n−1, P) − max(0, n−1−P), beta = clamp(b0 + 1e-3·u, −15, −2.3026), b0 = float32(log 1e-6) = −13.815510749816895; peak after update P+1, back at the −15 floor after update 20,041 (epoch 40.08) and there after.  `REST_HOLD`, `BETA_HOLD`, `COMP_HOLD`, `WINDOW_HOLD`, `VOTE_W` are never set; `cvt8`'s tree prints each of them `off` on every run, and the scorer requires exactly those lines.

### 259.1 PRIOR ART (the user's rule; queries run 2026-09-17, every paper read on its arXiv abstract page or arXiv HTML in place; no PDF opened)

* **Queries.** Web: "Adam-mini partition parameters blocks one learning rate per block wrong partition instability"; "separate learning rate batch norm gamma parameters grouped with convolution weights effect training layer-wise learning rate groups"; "\"per-layer\" learning rate \"normalization parameters\" separate group ablation merging layer groups coarser grouping hurts training"; "Adam-mini ablation LayerNorm normalization parameters separate block partition loss spike default PyTorch partition"; "learning rate groups BatchNorm parameters same group as convolution weights vs own group experiment CIFAR ResNet sensitivity".  arXiv API: `abs:"learning rate" AND abs:"batch normalization" AND abs:"parameter groups"` (0 hits); `abs:"blockwise" AND abs:"layerwise" AND abs:"learning rate" AND abs:granularity` (0); `"blockwise adaptivity" OR ti:"blockwise adaptive"`; `abs:hypergradient AND (abs:"per-layer" OR abs:"layer-wise") AND abs:"learning rate"` (0); `hypergradient learning rate per layer` (cs.LG, 15 read by title); `abs:"learning rate" AND abs:"normalization layers" AND (abs:"separate" OR abs:"decoupled") AND abs:"scale parameters"` (0).  254's 2026-09-17 sweep (≈70 papers) was read first and is not repeated.
* **Closest papers.**

| paper | id | what it establishes | relation to `cmg1` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Zhang, Chen, Li, Ding, Wu, Kingma, Ye, Luo, Sun, *Adam-mini: Use Fewer Learning Rates To Gain More* | arXiv:2406.16793 (2024) | one learning rate per parameter block is harmless IF blocks follow the Hessian's dense sub-blocks; the default PyTorch partition gives loss spikes that vanish under their partition (§2.3, Fig. 7, arXiv HTML) | the nearest precedent: "a bad merge of parameters onto one learning rate destabilises training" is KNOWN for Adam's v on Transformers.  It does not concern a meta-learned step size, normalisation scales or a matched-control merge |
| Kalra, Kirchenbauer, Barkeshli, Goldstein, *When Can You Get Away with Low Memory Adam?* | arXiv:2503.01843 (2025) | layer-wise SNR decides where second moments may be shared; LayerNorm second moments resist compression (per search-result summary; abstract read) | adjacent: normalisation parameters are where sharing hurts — for Adam's v, not a shared step size |
| Zheng, Kwok, *Blockwise Adaptivity* | arXiv:1905.09899 (2019) | blockwise adaptive step sizes converge and generalise as well as coordinate-wise | adjacent: coarser sharing can be fine; no merge-identity control |
| Atallah, *LionVote: Per-Layer Learning Rate Adaptation for Lion* | arXiv:2607.09266 (2026) | per-layer rates for Lion on ViT-Tiny/CIFAR-100; a global rate cannot reproduce a cross-layer-type disparity incl. normalisation layers | adjacent (Lion, per-tensor, CIFAR-100); no merge experiment, no BN carriers |
| Filatov, Wang, Ebert, Kesselheim, *Optimal Scaling Needs Optimal Norm* | arXiv:2510.03871 (2025) | per-layer-group LR tuning helps; the output layer is most sensitive | adjacent (layer-group LRs), no normalisation/merge result |
| Davis, Frank (arXiv:2110.13989); Arora, Li, Lyu (arXiv:1812.03981); You et al. LARS (arXiv:1708.03888) | as 254 | gamma wants its own smaller LR; scale-variant tensors carry LR sensitivity; one global LR limited by a few layers | the "of course gammas" background already filed at 254 |

* **In-corpus prior art (the campaign's own, which the literature cannot see).**  At this cell (filtered, 259.3): contiguous coarsening already hurts — `cbl1` `[2]×30+[1,1]` 67.52, `[4]×14+[3,3]` 59.998, `[8]×6+[7,7]` 42.37, `resnet18_blocks` 53.11 vs layerwise 69.42; and `cts1`/`cpk1` show moving ONE carrier (50) into a 49-tensor group drops `[49,13]` 55.42 → `[50,12]` 30.34 (147).  None of these has a matched control, and none keeps the rest of the grouping at layerwise.
* **Verdict: `WORTH-TESTING`, RESHAPED.**  That a bad merge onto one learning rate can hurt is published (Adam-mini) and visible in-corpus (`cbl1`); no paper and no campaign batch asks whether it is the CARRIERS' presence in a merged group that does the harm, against a count / numel / width / depth / norm-layer matched non-carrier merge, with the rest of the grouping held at the healthy singleton level.  Reshaped: (1) the reference is `sets:` singletons, not `layerwise`, so all three arms share one code path (`layerwise` uses `torch.stack` on-device, blockwise `torch.tensor` of group sums — equal arithmetic, different path; KLS's level is checked against the corpus layerwise band as a stamp only); (2) the control's inertness was MEASURED, not assumed, and it is not inert on the layerwise trajectory (259.4) — registered as a competing account; (3) 4 seeds per arm (the pre-assigned block), 12 runs ≈ 9.8 GPU-h = 1.33 × 5.1's 7.4.

### 259.2 What "necessary" would and would not mean (registered before any run)

* **Would mean (`CARRIER-MERGE-HARMS`):** at this cell, starting from layerwise's grouping, putting the three carriers into ONE step-size group with N costs ≥ 5 pp of plateau5, and ≥ 5 pp more than putting the matched non-carrier triple {47, 48, 56} into the same N, which itself costs < 5 pp.  Sentence: *"keeping the carriers out of a shared step-size group with N is necessary for the layerwise level at this cell."*  It is necessity of SEPARATION, relative to THIS ONE merge.
* **Would NOT mean:** necessity against any other merge (neighbour set, size, position, grouping family), cell, network or horizon; that the carriers' step size (large or small) is the lever (no step size is manipulated; the merged group's beta is whatever its Lion vote makes it — the G* pin stamps are descriptive); identity vs MAGNITUDE (188.3 — at a shared step size the carriers' |L| is ×300 T's, premise S); anything about the scalar collapse beyond 187 / 193 / 240–253; and an arm within 5 pp of KLS is a BOUND ("costs < 5 pp"), not "costs nothing" (164.6).
* **`NO-MERGE-HARMS` would mean** separation is NOT necessary for the layerwise level at this merge (±5 pp) — read with the G* pin stamps (pinned G* → N's own step size does not matter here; free G* → the carriers did not capture the merged vote).  It would not say separation is never necessary (`[50,12]` and scalar collapse).

### 259.9 Deviations from the brief, disclosed
