### 280.6 THE PROOF JOB — the k=1 and k=2 name-list forms, and the SAME-k discriminations, on the real GPU path

`sbatch --export=ALL,CWD4_EXPORT_PROBE=<the two-carrier string> ~/stage_cwd4/bin/cWD4_realrun_bite.sbatch` → **job 5051780, `gpu-short` [HOST_e8d809bd94] (NVIDIA L4, 23034 MiB), 00:08:32, COMPLETED, `ALL PASS` twice, 61 PASS / 0 FAIL**, copied to `$WS/runs/cwd4/bite_decaymask_cwd4.log` (`c1a943aa…`), which guard 4f reads and pins by sha.  It ran `tests/test_decaymask.py --structural-only` (13 PASS: deleting the three `PATCH_DECAYMASK` regions reproduces `cvt8`'s HF.py byte for byte) and `tests/test_decaymask_realrun_cwd4.py` on the two trees, 300 real CIFAR-100 steps per variant, 24 variants:

* **RR0 / RR1** — the parent tree twice is bitwise identical; on `cwd1`'s tree `DECAY_MASK` **unset** and **empty** are bitwise the parent (beta every step, per-step loss, `probe.jsonl` bytes, every final parameter and buffer, `1c020df285575d75`), print `DECAY_MASK: off`, and write no `dm_*` key.
* **RR2** — each of the SIX masked strings printed EXACTLY the design's witness, and at every one of the 30 probe records `dm_n` = step + 2, `dm_skipped` = `dm_n` × k, `dm_masked` = k and `dm_wdterm` > 0 with k finite norms, for **k = 3 / 2 / 2 / 1 / 1 / 1**.  **The k=1 form had never run on this network** (`cwd2` ran a one-name list on PlainNet's tree) and **`{50,53}` had never run at all.**
* **RR3** — with the verifier wrapped around `base_update`, at EVERY step and for EVERY tensor `w'`, `h'` and `m'` are **BITWISE** the registered formula with wd 0 on exactly the registered indices and 0.1 elsewhere: `expect` mismatches **[0, 0, 0]** on all six arms and on the OFF control.
* **RR4 (SET DISCRIMINATION) — THE POINT OF THE JOB.**  At a test-only α₀ 1e-2 each masked run matches ITS OWN set and **FAILS** the set it must be told apart from.  **FIVE of the six pairs are SAME-k**, which is exactly what `G-BITE`'s record audit cannot separate: `TWOWD0` {50,53} vs `CTL2WD0` {47,56} (**1,200 wrong**, 600 bites) and back (**1,200 wrong**), `ONE50` vs `ONE53`, `ONE53` vs `ONE59`, `ONE59` vs `ONE50` (**600 wrong each**, 300 bites each).  The sixth, `CARWD0` vs its own PROPER SUBSET `TWOWD0`, gives exactly **300 wrong = 300 steps × the ONE tensor (idx 59) that differs**.  Every masked run's final weights differ from the OFF run's.
* **RR5 (LOUDNESS)** — on this tree a **misspelt ONE-NAME list**, a misspelt pair, a duplicated name, an empty `+` token, a name outside the model and a bad character EACH raise `ValueError` at construction: a typo in a name list of ANY length **cannot run silently unmasked**.
* **THE EXPORT PROBE** — the two-carrier string (which contains `+` and `.`) was passed through `sbatch --export` exactly as the launcher passes `DECAY_MASK` and echoed back unchanged.

**EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION OF THE DECLARED LIMIT, recorded because it is the honest version of headline bound (3):** at record 292 `TWOWD0`'s and `CTL2WD0`'s `dm_wdterm` are **4.277068885240954e-06 — the SAME NUMBER to the last printed digit** (two 512-entry scales of equal norm under the same α), while their final weights differ (`430dc5da…` vs `87d1b4bb…`).  **The record readout genuinely cannot tell those two arms apart; RR4 and `G-WITNESS` can.**

**What the proof does NOT cover:** the 100-epoch dynamics (300 steps only), and the accuracy of any arm.

It was read.  `HF.SGDm_base_update` is `delta = a * (m + wd * w); w <- w - delta; h <- gamma * (1 - wd*a) * h - delta`: the decay is multiplied by the LEARNED step size in the weight update AND its Jacobian factor `(1 - wd*a)` is baked into the meta trace, so a decoupled arm needs a NEW harness patch touching BOTH — a full patch cycle. ### 281.1 PRIOR ART, CHECKED BEFORE ANY DESIGN WAS FIXED (the standing rule)

**Queries run** (WebSearch): (1) "weight decay value threshold training collapse batch normalization scale parameters optimizer instability ablation"; (2) "coupled versus decoupled weight decay normalization layer gamma optimizer stability comparison"; (3) "hypergradient meta-learned learning rate weight decay interaction failure \"weight decay\" sweep threshold learned step size"; (4) "rotational equilibrium weight decay normalization Kosson effective learning rate arXiv".  **Two abstract pages were read in full** (arXiv:1711.05101 and arXiv:2607.21005).  **No `.pdf` was fetched and no notebook or Vercel URL was opened.**

**Verified closest work:**

| paper | id | what was read | relation to `cwd5` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Li, Zhou, Xu, *Weight-norm Criticality: A Mechanism for Loss Spikes Induced by the Normalization and Weight Decay* | arXiv:2607.21005 (23 Jul 2026) | abstract page, in full (already ADJACENT at 275.1; now the DIRECT neighbour) | **THE CLOSEST HIT ON THE VALUE AXIS, AND IT RESHAPES THE READING RATHER THAN KILLING THE BATCH.**  It argues for a *weight-norm criticality*: "as the weight decay coefficient increases, the norms of scale-invariant weights are progressively driven toward zero", sharpness rises and training destabilises — i.e. **a weight-decay VALUE threshold for a normalisation-related instability already exists in the literature, at the CLASS grain**.  It reports no numerical threshold, no per-tensor exemption, and nothing about a meta-learned step size or a scalar-vs-layerwise granularity gap.  **Consequence, registered now: a `THRESHOLD-*` verdict may NOT be written as "we discover that weight decay has a critical value"; it must be written as "the campaign's cell sits above / below the value at which this configuration breaks", which is the DIAGNOSTIC framing the area chair asked for.** |
| Kosson, Messmer, Jaggi, *Rotational Equilibrium: How Weight Decay Balances Learning Across Neural Networks* | arXiv:2305.17212 (ICML 2024) | search result + abstract summary | **SUPPLIES THE CONFOUND THAT MAKES THE DECOUPLED ARM UNREADABLE EVEN IF IT WERE BUILT.**  On scale-invariant vectors the weight decay and the gradient updates reach an equilibrium in which the *expected rotation* — a proxy for the EFFECTIVE learning rate — is set by the decay.  Changing the decay VALUE therefore changes the effective LR of the normalisation scales, and swapping coupled for decoupled changes it again (the paper attributes part of AdamW-vs-Adam+L2 to exactly this).  So a decoupled arm would move the effective step size as well as the decay's coupling, and would not be a clean coupling contrast.  This is the second, independent reason (b) is descoped. |
| Loshchilov & Hutter, *Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization* | **arXiv:1711.05101**, ICLR 2019 (id verified in this session on the abstract page, as the brief required) | abstract page, in full | The definition of the descoped arm.  It decouples the decay from the optimiser step so the optimal decay factor stops depending on the learning rate.  **Nothing in it concerns a shared vs per-group META-LEARNED step size, and it does not bear on whether a collapse has a decay-value threshold.** |
| Lobacheva, Kodryan, Chirkova, Malinin, Vetrov | arXiv:2106.15739 (NeurIPS 2021) | verified at LIMITS-PREP 3.3 / 280.1 | ALREADY-SHOWN at the CLASS grain: BN + WD together destabilise training periodically.  Network-wide, no value threshold reported for an optimiser-configuration failure. |
| He et al., "no bias decay" | arXiv:1812.01187 | verified at 271.8 / 275.1 | The standard reference for NOT decaying BN parameters at all — the practice the campaign's configuration departs from.  It is a recipe, not a threshold study. |
| Kim et al. | arXiv:2205.07260 | verified at 275.1 | γ_last / γ_down / γ_others by POSITION; relevant to `CARW2`'s set, unchanged here. |

**Seen in result lists only, NOT read, NOT cited:** "Towards Understanding Neural Collapse: The Effects of Batch Normalization and Weight Decay" (arXiv:2309.04644 — *neural* collapse, a feature-geometry phenomenon, not an optimiser failure), "Correction of Decoupled Weight Decay" (arXiv:2512.08217), "Does Your Optimizer Care How You Normalize?" (arXiv:2604.01563), "Cautious Weight Decay" (arXiv:2510.12402), OUIDecay (arXiv:2605.10161, verified at 280.1).

**VERDICT: `WORTH-TESTING`, RESHAPED.**  Nothing found reports a weight-decay VALUE threshold for a **meta-learned shared-step-size collapse**, and nothing measures a **scalar-vs-layerwise granularity gap as a function of the decay**, which is the number this batch exists to produce.  **But the reshaping is real and is registered before any run:** Li–Zhou–Xu already own "there is a critical weight decay for normalised training", so a `THRESHOLD-*` result is NOT a new mechanism and must be written as a scope / diagnostic statement about the campaign's own configuration; and Kosson et al. mean that the decoupled arm, even if built, would confound the coupling with a change in the effective learning rate.  **A reasoned DROP was considered and rejected**: without the ladder the campaign cannot answer the first question any referee asks about a wd-0.1 result, the area chair's subsection is unsafe to publish in any form, and the audit's own scalar arm keeps an undisclosed configuration risk.

### 281.2 THE DECOUPLED ARM: READ THE CODE, THEN DESCOPE IT — WITH REASONS

The brief said: *"READ the harness's base optimiser code to find out whether decoupled decay is available at all … Do not guess: read the code."*  It was read, on `cluster_b`, in the tree the batch runs from.

* `$WS/harness_cwd1/cifar10/Optimizers/HF.py`, `SGDm_base_update` (and the `PATCH_DECAYMASK` twin `_dm_SGDm_base_update`):
  `delta = a * (momentum_base[i] + args_base['weight_decay'] * w.data)` ; `w.data = w.data - delta` ;
  `h_condenced[i] = gamma * (1 - args_base['weight_decay'] * a) * h_condenced[i] - delta`.
* `$WS/harness_cwd1/cifar10/train.py` declares **`--weight-decay-base` (float, default 0.1)** and `--weight-decay-meta`; `Optimizers/build_optimizer.py` puts the value into `args_base['weight_decay']`.  **There is no decoupled flag, no decoupled branch, and no decoupled alg.**  The only decoupled optimiser in the tree is `torch.optim.AdamW` inside the FIXED-STEP baseline class `AdamW_optimizer`, at a hard-coded `weight_decay=0.1` and a fixed lr — not a MetaOptimize arm and not a controlled contrast.

**So (b) needs a NEW harness patch**, and it needs it in TWO places: the weight update and the meta trace's Jacobian factor.  That is a full patch cycle of the same size as `PATCH_DECAYMASK`'s (260): structural delete-back, a real-GPU bite job with a bitwise formula verifier, loudness tests.  **THE DECIDING REASON IS NOT THE COST, IT IS THAT THE ARM WOULD NOT BE READABLE.**  "The same effective strength" has no value at this cell:

* the coupled per-step dose is `wd * a`, and `a = exp(beta)` is **learned**, clamped by `BETA_CLIP=-15:-2.3026` to `[3.06e-07, 0.1]`;
* `a` is what DIFFERS between the arms this batch compares — in the collapsing scalar arm the carriers carry a LARGE `a` (that is the mechanism, 240 / 246 / 253 / 273), while the layerwise arm's are small;
* so a decoupled arm at ANY fixed λ matches the dose of at most one arm, and the comparison confounds "coupled vs decoupled" with "λ too big / too small for this arm";
* and Kosson et al. (arXiv:2305.17212) add that swapping coupled for decoupled moves the *rotational equilibrium* of every scale-invariant tensor, i.e. their effective learning rate, which is the very quantity under study.

**DESCOPED, PLAINLY, AND STAMPED.**  `DECOUPLED-NOT-TESTED` is on every `cwd5` FINAL, the scorer's licence text says in terms that nothing about decoupled decay is licensed **in either direction**, and the write-up may not use `cwd5` to say the collapse is "a coupled-decay phenomenon".  **What a future decoupled batch would need, recorded so it is not re-derived:** an additive `PATCH_DECOUPLEDWD` implementing `w <- w - a*m - λ*w` with the trace factor `(1 - λ)`, its own structural and bitwise proofs, and a λ LADDER of its own (since no single λ is matched) — i.e. a second batch, not an arm.

### 281.3 THE DESIGN, AND WHY 9 ARMS

`cwd5` = **9 arms × 3 seeds {146, 147, 148} = 27 jobs, ONE submission**, `cwd3`'s / `cwd4`'s cell byte for byte (CIFAR-100 / `ResNet18_c100` / SGDm 0.99 + Lion 0.99 / 0.9 / ms 1e-3 / α₀ 1e-6 / 100 ep / bs 100 / `AUGMENT=1` / `BETA_CLIP=-15:-2.3026` / `PROBE=100` / `PROBE_TENSOR=1`) **except the base weight decay, which is the axis**, and no hold patch on any arm.

| rung | `--weight-decay-base` | scalar arm | layerwise arm | extra | what the rung buys |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **W1** | `0.1` | `k01W1` | `kLW1` | — | **the anchor**: the campaign's own value, replicated IN BATCH, so the ladder has a baseline and the batch ties to the landed cells |
| **W2** | `1e-2` | `k01W2` | `kLW2` | **`CARW2`** (scalar, `DECAY_MASK` = 50+53+59) | one decade down — the rung most likely to still collapse, and therefore the one where a carrier companion can be READ |
| **W3** | `1e-3` | `k01W3` | `kLW3` | — | two decades down |
| **W4** | `5e-4` | `k01W4` | `kLW4` | — | **the standard CIFAR SGD value**, 200× below the anchor: the number the referee will name |

**Why BOTH grains at EVERY rung, and not a scalar-only ladder against the landed layerwise mean (69.42, n=32).**  A collapse is defined *relative to its own reference arm* (LIMITS-PREP 2.2, R50).  Weight decay changes BOTH arms' levels; reading a scalar ladder against a layerwise level measured at a DIFFERENT weight decay would compare two different experiments and would be exactly the cross-batch contrast this campaign refuses elsewhere.  The 12 layerwise runs are the price of a within-rung reading and they are not optional.

**Why the carrier companion is at ONE rung, and at W2.**  The brief asked for "enough of a carrier-mask companion to say whether the carrier account still holds wherever the collapse still exists".  Where it still exists is not knowable before the runs, and a mask arm at a rung that does not collapse is UNREADABLE (cmo1's `ISO-UNREADABLE` at wd 0, 264).  W2 is the highest non-anchor rung and therefore the one most likely to still collapse; at the anchor the same mask is already landed twice (`cwd3`'s `CARWD0` 70.2640 and `cwd4`'s in-batch replicate), so three runs there would buy a third replicate instead of a new fact.  **The risk is registered, not hidden:** if W2 does not collapse, `CARW2` is stamped `CAR-UNREADABLE` and the batch says nothing about the carrier account.

**Not added, and why:** a fifth rung (the four points already span 200× and each extra rung costs 1.43 GPU-h × 2 grains); a wd-0 rung (`cmo1`'s `W0k01` already has it, between-batch); a carrier companion at W3 or W4 (over the ≤ 20 GPU-h target and unreadable if those rungs do not collapse); an ISO / hold arm (a different question); **the decoupled arm (281.2).**

**Spend:** `cwd3` measured **10.7111 GPU-h / 15 runs = 0.7141** per run at THIS EXACT cell (278.1, `sacct`) → **27 × 0.7141 = 19.28 ≈ 19.3 GPU-h expected**, **under the brief's ≤ 20 GPU-h target**, said at the top of the range rather than rounded down.  Hard bound WALL 3 h × 27 = **81 GPU-h**; the two proof jobs 0.1903 GPU-h together.

### 281.4 THE REGISTERED DECISION, ACCOUNTS WITH EVERY ARM's PREDICTED LEVEL, AND THE NULLS

**Per-rung STATE, computed WITHIN the rung and never across rungs:** `UNREADABLE` iff layerwise `< REF_MIN` (55); `COLLAPSE` iff scalar `<= R50` (0.50) × layerwise — LIMITS-PREP 2.2's PRIMARY definition; `NOGAP` iff layerwise − scalar `< GAP_BAR` (10 pp); `PARTIAL` otherwise.

**Gates first (first match wins):** `UNRESOLVED-DIVERGED` (a seed range > 5 pp) → `UNRESOLVED-REFERENCE` (any rung's layerwise arm below `REF_MIN`, naming the rung) → `ANCHOR-NOT-COLLAPSED` (`k01W1` > 30, or rung W1 is not `COLLAPSE`) → `NON-MONOTONE` (a COLLAPSE at a LOWER weight decay than a non-collapsed rung) → one account.  The state word `W1-<s>+W2-<s>+W3-<s>+W4-<s>+<carrier word>` is printed beside it.

Bands (UNSURE): K01 18–28, PART 40–55, FREE 62–78.  Every account has all four layerwise arms FREE unless stated.

| account (token) | `k01W1` | `k01W2` | `k01W3` | `k01W4` | sentence it licenses (at this cell only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`COLLAPSE-AT-ALL-VALUES`** | K01 | K01 | K01 | K01 | **"the shared-step-size collapse is not an artefact of the campaign's large coupled weight decay: at the standard CIFAR value the scalar grouping still falls to at most half the layerwise level"** — the CORNER-CASE CHARGE REFUTED at this cell |
| **`THRESHOLD-W1-W2`** | K01 | FREE | FREE | FREE | **ADVERSE, and registered as such**: the collapse needs a coupled decay within a decade of 0.1.  **THE REFEREE'S CHARGE LANDING** — the mechanism line becomes a diagnostic of ONE extreme configuration and the audit's scalar cells must be reported with that disclosure |
| **`THRESHOLD-W2-W3`** | K01 | K01 | FREE | FREE | a threshold between 1e-2 and 1e-3: the phenomenon is a decade wide, not a point, but the audit's cells still sit above it |
| **`THRESHOLD-W3-W4`** | K01 | K01 | K01 | FREE | the collapse spans two decades and is absent only at the standard value — the boundary sits exactly where a referee will look |
| **`GRADED-ABOVE-THRESHOLD-W1/W2/W3`** | K01 | (PART somewhere above the prefix) | | | the gap is GRADED in the decay, not a threshold; quote `G_W2..G_W4`, do NOT report a threshold |
| **`NON-MONOTONE`** | K01 | FREE | K01 | FREE | **NO threshold sentence and NO corner-case verdict either way**; report the non-monotonicity with all four rungs' levels |
| `ANCHOR-NOT-COLLAPSED` | FREE | — | — | — | the batch did not reproduce the mechanism cell; no rung is read |
| `UNRESOLVED-REFERENCE` | — | — | — | — | a rung's layerwise arm is unhealthy; a GATE, and itself a fact about the configuration worth reporting |

**CO-PRIMARY:** `G_W4` = `kLW4` − `k01W4`, the granularity gap at the STANDARD CIFAR weight decay — the one number that decides whether the audit's scalar arm is a granularity result or a configuration artefact.  **KEYS:** `G_W1`, `G_W2`, `G_W3`, and the four R50 ratios.  **CARRIER HALF (rung W2 only, read ONLY if that rung is COLLAPSE):** `P_CARW2` = `CARW2` − `k01W2`; `D_CARW2` = `kLW2` − `CARW2`; recovery against the IN-BATCH `kLW2` (`CARRIER-AGAINST-KLW2`).

**THE NULLS, and the gate that separates each.**  (i) **A mask that never bites** makes `CARW2` = `k01W2`, which reads as `CAR-NULL` — *"the carrier account fails at 1e-2"*, an adverse reading the batch can genuinely produce.  It is separated ONLY by `G-BITE`'s carrier gate, and the selftest proves the separation on REAL landed records: the 3 landed `cwd1` `k01` runs read as `CARW2` FAIL the `DECAY_MASK` audit on every record, while the 3 landed `cwd3` `CARWD0` runs PASS it.  (ii) **A weight-decay flag that did not reach the update** would make two rungs the same experiment; no in-run witness covers W3 and W4, so that null is separated by the **proof job's RW2** (bitwise formula at all four values, non-vacuity against another rung's wd, and pairwise-distinct final weights) plus each run's own ARGS line.  (iii) **A stray mask on a ladder arm** is a LADDER-gate failure (`PATCH-NOT-VERIFIED`), proved on real records by reading `cwd1`'s masked `kLNWD` runs as unmasked cwd5 ladder arms.

**Frozen literals (O2):** `SIGMA_R18ALL` = `SIGMA_PRIOR` **0.6451413439065666** (df 258, 51 cells, 309 rows; NAIVE **12.482176983761198** df 332), `SE_PRIOR` **0.526756**, so **2 SE = 1.053512 pp is the HALF-WIDTH of a ±2 SE interval and is NOT a bound on any effect** (278.6 C1); `R50` 0.50 | `GAP_BAR` 10.0 (**18.98 SE**) | `REF_MIN` 55.0 | `K01_MAX` 30.0 | `MATCH` 5.0 (**9.49 SE**) | `NULL` 2.0 (**3.80 SE**) | `DIVERGED` 5.0 | floor / ceiling 15 / 90.  `SIGMA_USED` = max(frozen floor, in-batch).  Registration corpus `results/all_runs.csv` `fe3874d3…` (**3,268** rows) + `CORPUS-EXCLUSIONS.tsv` `50f75cde…` (**183** rows) → **3,085** after `filter_rows`; the selftest re-derives the literal to 1e-12 on both hosts.  **`G-HW` is DISCLOSURE ONLY.**

### 281.6 THE PROOF JOB — the ladder's own premise, on the real GPU path

`sbatch --export=ALL,CWD5_EXPORT_PROBE=<the three-carrier string> ~/stage_cwd5/bin/cWD5_realrun_bite.sbatch` → **job 5052114, `gpu-short` [HOST_2f2f29d9e1] (NVIDIA L4), 00:05:41, COMPLETED, `ALL PASS` twice, 52 PASS / 0 FAIL**, copied to `$WS/runs/cwd5/bite_decaymask_cwd5.log` (`7f5a3eaf…`), which guard 4f reads and pins by sha.  It ran `tests/test_decaymask.py --structural-only` (13 PASS: deleting the three `PATCH_DECAYMASK` regions reproduces `cvt8`'s HF.py byte for byte) and `tests/test_decaymask_realrun_cwd5.py` on the two trees, 300 real CIFAR-100 steps per variant:

* **RW-EQ** — the NEW wd-parameterised child and the REGISTERED child of `tests/test_decaymask_realrun.py` are **BITWISE identical at wd 0.1**, OFF and with the carrier mask: same final-weight sha256, same beta trajectory, same stats, same bite count.  The additive code is proved against the file it transcribes.
* **RW0 / RW1** — the parent tree twice is bitwise identical; on `cwd1`'s tree `DECAY_MASK` unset at wd 0.1 is bitwise the parent (beta, per-step loss, `probe.jsonl` bytes, every final parameter and buffer), prints `DECAY_MASK: off`, and writes no `dm_*` key.
* **RW2 — THE LADDER'S PREMISE, AND THE POINT OF THE JOB.**  At EACH of the four rung tokens `0.1 / 1e-2 / 1e-3 / 5e-4`: at every step and for every tensor `w'`, `h'` and `m'` are **BITWISE** `w - a*(m + wd*w)`, `gamma*(1 - wd*a)*h - a*(m + wd*w)` and `mp*m + (1-mp)*g` **with THE PASSED wd** (`expect` mismatches `[0, 0, 0]`), the optimiser's own `args_base['weight_decay']` is the passed float; the SAME run checked against the formula at ANOTHER rung's wd **FAILS** (non-vacuity, 4/4); and **the four rungs' final weights are PAIRWISE DISTINCT** — no two rungs are secretly the same experiment.
* **RW3 — `PATCH_DECAYMASK` AT A WEIGHT DECAY IT HAS NEVER RUN AT, AND THE ROUTE IT BITES THROUGH, MEASURED.**  The three `ctd1` carriers masked at wd `1e-2` printed EXACTLY the registered witness `DECAY_MASK: on base=SGDm wd=0.01 spec=… masked=3 of=62 numel=1536 idx=50,53,59 names=…`; at all 30 probe records `dm_n` = step + 2, `dm_skipped` = `dm_n` × 3, `dm_masked` = 3 and `dm_wdterm` > 0 with three finite norms (`dm_wdterm` **5.238318104171683e-07** at record 292); and the update is bitwise the formula with wd 0 on {50,53,59} and 0.01 elsewhere.  **THEN A FACT THE FIRST JOB UNCOVERED AND THE SECOND MEASURES RATHER THAN ASSUMES:** at the run's OWN α₀ 1e-6 the skipped term is `a·wd·|w| ≈ 1e-6 × 1e-2 × 1 = 1e-8`, **below float32 resolution beside a BatchNorm scale's `|w| ≈ 1`** — so the **WEIGHT UPDATE is bitwise unchanged** while the **META TRACE differs at every one of 900 tensor-steps** (`wrong` = `[0, 900, 0]` against the fully unmasked formula).  At a test-only α₀ 1e-2 **both** routes bite (900 bites), the masked run matches its own set exactly, an UNMASKED run at the same wd FAILS the masked formula, and the two runs' final weights differ (`4d72b0ff…` vs `ddb0aa2f…`).  **The consequence is DECLARED, not glossed:** at α₀ 1e-6 the masked and unmasked 300-step weight trajectories COINCIDE, and the scorer asserts that they coincide EXACTLY WHEN the weight update never differed in float32.  **That is a limit of the PROOF — 300 steps at the CLAMPED INITIAL step size — not of the batch, whose runs are 50,000 steps at a LEARNED, rising `a`.**  It also sharpens one registered prediction: **at rung W2 a `CAR-NULL` would be a REAL reading, not a broken mask**, because `dm_wdterm` is positive on every record and `G-BITE`'s carrier gate passes.

* **A TEST-ONLY DEFECT, DISCLOSED.**  The FIRST proof job, **5052102 ([HOST_2f2f29d9e1], NVIDIA L4, 00:05:44, COMPLETED), returned 47 PASS / 3 FAIL** — all three in `RW3`, and **all three were defects in this batch's own new bite driver's ASSERTIONS, not in the harness, the design, the scorer or the launcher**: (a) it asserted `bites > 0` at α₀ 1e-6, where the term is below float32 resolution as above; (b) it asserted that the masked run matches the **fully unmasked** formula, which a masked run must FAIL — the assertion was inverted; (c) it bundled the α₀ 1e-2 weight comparison (which DOES differ) with the α₀ 1e-6 one (which does not).  The three assertions were rewritten to state what is true and to MEASURE the route, `bin/cWD5_wdladder.sh`'s guard 4f was extended to require the two new `RW3` lines, **no arm, rung, bar, sigma, contrast, account, state, stamp or literal changed, and the scorer's selftest was 138 / 0 / 0 before and after**.  The fix was committed as `fdb16ac0…` and pushed **before** the second proof job ran and long before the submission.  Precedent for recording rather than quietly re-running: 260.6.
* **RW4 (LOUDNESS)** — at wd 1e-2 a misspelt name, a misspelt triple, a duplicate, an empty `+` token, a name outside the model and a bad character EACH raise `ValueError` at construction; and at wd 0 the same mask raises the patch's own *"a mask would be vacuous"* error.  A typo cannot run silently unmasked at any rung.
* **THE EXPORT PROBE** — the three-carrier string (which contains `+` and `.`) was passed through `sbatch --export` exactly as the launcher passes `DECAY_MASK`, and echoed back unchanged.

**What the proof does NOT cover:** the 100-epoch dynamics (300 steps only), and the accuracy of any arm.

### 281.12 A CODE GAP FOUND AT REGISTRATION AND **REPORTED, NOT FIXED** (RULE 16)

**The defect.**  `CARW2` is the first run in this campaign that BOTH prints a `<KIND>: on` witness line (`DECAY_MASK`,
because the three carriers are masked) AND deviates on an ARGS value (`weight-decay-base` `1e-2`, because it sits on
rung W2).  `analysis/corpus_exclusions.py` lists **one witness per run** (`listed` is `{fn: entry}`, line 393), and
its two readers disagree about which witness that must be:

* the **KINDS** reader (line ~446) requires a run printing an ON `DECAY_MASK` line to be listed with a `DECAY_MASK`
  witness, unless the kind is registered for that `(batch, arm)` in `MULTI_KIND`;
* the **ARGS-VALUE** reader (CORRECTIONS 263, line ~513) requires a run whose ARGS deviates to be listed with THAT
  kind's witness, and has **no `MULTI_KIND` escape at all**: `if ent is not None: bad.append("%s deviates on %s but is
  listed with a %s witness")`.

**Verified empirically, not inferred.**  A COPY of the module was loaded from a scratch directory with its own
`results/` (the registered file was NOT edited and NOT run against the real corpus), a single synthetic
`cwd5-CARW2-s146` `.out` carrying both the `wd=0.01` `DECAY_MASK` line and `--weight-decay-base 1e-2` was built, and
the REAL `check()` was run against BOTH possible listings:

| listing | `check()` |
|---|---|
| the `DECAY_MASK` witness | **FAIL** — *"deviates on ARGS_WD_BASE but is listed with a DECAY_MASK witness"* |
| the `ARGS_WD_BASE` witness | **FAIL** — *"prints an ON DECAY_MASK line but is listed with a ARGS_WD_BASE witness"* |

**The fix, also verified on the copy, and OWED AT LANDING UNDER ITS OWN NUMBER.**  List `CARW2` with the
**`ARGS_WD_BASE`** witness and register `("cwd5", "CARW2"): {"DECAY_MASK": <the wd=0.01 witness>}` in `MULTI_KIND` —
the same append-only pattern CORRECTIONS 251 and 269 used for `cvt8` / `cvt9` / `cwd2`.  With that one runtime
addition applied to the copy, `check()` returned **rc 0, `VERDICT: PASS`**, with
*"completeness (DECAY_MASK): 1 .out files print an ON line; 1 are CSV rows, every one listed with its kind: True"*.

**RULE 16 HELD: `analysis/corpus_exclusions.py` IS NOT EDITED BY THIS ENTRY.**  The gap is reported here, at
registration, with the reproduction and the fix, so that the landing closes it deliberately under its own CORRECTIONS
number **before** the ingest rather than discovering it while ingesting.  **This is a NEW reported RULE 16 defect and
it is the only one this entry creates.**

* **Why that framing.** The audit reports, at `ResNet18` / CIFAR-100 / SGDm+Lion / α₀ 1e-6, scalar **22.78 ± 0.70 (n 5)** against plain layerwise **69.17 ± 0.60 (n 6)**, gap **+46.39 pp** (`docs/FINDINGS.md`'s per-setting table — **cited as the campaign's own audit figure and NOT re-derived by this entry**, in the same form E0 is cited; E2's census gives 22.96 / 69.42 and `cwd4`'s in-batch anchor 22.8213, and the three agree to a few tenths, which is the only claim made for them). **A referee meets that row and asks whether the gap is granularity or a broken scalar configuration — and the campaign can now answer.** Removing coupled decay from **1,536 of 11,220,132 parameters** lifts the scalar arm to **70.2640** (`cwd3`), **one** scale alone lifts it to **67.9567** (`cwd4` `ONE59`), and two matched carrier-free scales lift it **not at all** (22.8547).
* **THE ONE-SENTENCE FORM MAY NOT LEAD WITH THE MAGNITUDE LINE.** The chair's reason, checked against the campaign's own record and found already written there: **Lion aggregates per-tensor terms by a SIGN**, so *"the biggest terms decide the shared rate"* is close to a property of `sign(Σ L_i)` itself, and everything genuinely empirical lives in the **premises**. **This is T14, written before the chair said it**; T14 concluded the magnitude framing is the right one, the chair concludes it is therefore **not the headline**, and §10.4 records that both are true and not in tension. The licensed lead sentence leads with the failure and the cheap fix.
* **THE NOVELTY TABLE, EVERY ROW RE-FETCHED BY ME.** **Mueller et al. (arXiv:2306.04226) is the sharpest hit and it costs us two things, not one**: a tiny normalisation-affine subset (*"typically comprising 0.1% of the total parameters"*) carrying a whole optimiser-level effect **across SAM variants and across ResNet-BN and ViT-LN**, **AND** — the half the draft never conceded — *"alternative sparse perturbation approaches … do not achieve similar performance enhancement at such extreme sparsity levels"*, i.e. **the matched-sparse control that fails is THEIR design move too**, so our `CTL2WD0` / `DEPTH2` asymmetry is not a methodological novelty. **Kim et al. (arXiv:2205.07260) is stronger prior art than the draft conceded**, per P3. What is left: a decay **exemption** rather than an adversarial perturbation; an optimiser that **fails and is repaired** rather than a generalisation gain; a subset **nominated by attribution** rather than chosen as a class; and **named tensors one at a time**.
* **THE RANKED REVIEWER ASKS, R1–R10**, each with the campaign's current answer: **R1 the weight-decay ladder (not yet — and it decides the section); R2 decoupled vs coupled (no); R3 identity vs magnitude vs position class (PARTLY — count refuted by `cwd4`, the other two not); R4 a non-sign meta-update (no — Lion only, and cheap); R5 another network / dataset (partly); R6 beyond 100 epochs (no); R7 more than three seeds (no); R8 the collapsing arms' weight norms (no, and the instrument cannot — O-2); R9 reproduce from the repository (partly, and §9.0 now says exactly where not); R10 multiple comparisons (no correction anywhere — T16).**

`G-DIVERGE` PASS: every arm's seed range ≤ 5.0 pp, the largest being `k01`'s **1.498**.  `G-FLOOR` / `G-CEIL` PASS (max arm mean 70.0100, inside 15–90).

### 283.4 What bounds the result, led with

The ten bounds are the headline of this entry and are not repeated in full here.  The four a reader of the paper must carry are:

1. **THE NULL IS A FLOOR READING — A BOUND, NOT A MEASURED ZERO.**  `|P_CTL2|` sits below the registered 2.0 pp `NULL` bar and inside **[−1.0202, +1.0868] at ±2 SE**, an interval that **spans zero**, with per-seed values that **flip sign**.  Against a carrier effect of +44.2500 pp (`P_TWO`) that is a ratio of **40.7 : 1 at the 2-SE bound** (44.2500 / 1.0868) or **22.1 : 1 against the registered `NULL` bar** (44.2500 / 2.0).  **That ratio is what carries the specificity claim; it is not a measured zero.**
2. **THE MAGNITUDE RIVAL IS UNTOUCHED AND THE BATCH MAKES IT STRONGER.**  Headline bound (2).  The singles land in exactly the in-batch mean-`|L|` rank order with both gaps resolved and `SINGLES-SATURATED` absent, so the ordering is measured, not bounded.  **This is the most dangerous fact in the batch and it is stated in the headline rather than in a footnote**, which is why `MAGNITUDE-NOT-SEPARATED` and `CTL-NOT-MAGNITUDE-MATCHED` are unconditional stamps rather than conditional ones.
3. **POSITION CLASS IS NOT SEPARATED, AND NOW BITES AT COUNT ONE AS WELL AS COUNT TWO.**  Headline bound (4).  `{50, 59}` are both γ_last and recover; `{53}` is γ_down and only partly recovers; `{47, 56}` are γ_others and stay at the floor.  **The batch separates COUNT.  It does not separate CLASS, and it does not separate MAGNITUDE.**  These are **three distinct confounds**; one is refuted here and two are not.
4. **`ONE50`'s `REC` IS A 0.40 SE READING.**  Headline bound (3).  The `ONE50-REC` token and any *"two of the three singles suffice"* phrasing are DESCRIPTIVE / UNSURE; the `ONE-ORDER` stamp is not, because the scorer sorts by level rather than by state.

**Also carried forward, unchanged:** the batch says nothing about the 100-epoch dynamics beyond the 500 probe records per run, and **no weight-norm readout exists on the UNMASKED (collapsing) arms** — `k01` carries no `dm_*` key at all — so this remains a **SCOPE result and not a mechanism** (274.1, 276.1, 278.4).  And `cwd3`'s bound about the WD value stands: **every number here is at coupled weight decay 0.1**, and whether any of it survives at normal values is exactly what `cwd5` (281) was launched to decide.

### 283.5 The attack — four independent derivations of the design, and a bite gate that could have failed

* **`G-BITE` PASSES ON ALL 21 RUNS.**  Each run: **500 records, 1 step-size group, lion-mismatch 0** (ties 0, worst 4.0e-07), 0 bad records, 0 non-finite, 0 hold-key records.  The `DECAY_MASK` audit on **every record of every run**: `dm_masked == k` with k = 3 / 2 / 2 / 1 / 1 / 1 exactly as registered, `dm_n == step + 2` strictly increasing, `dm_skipped == dm_n × k`, and a **POSITIVE `dm_wdterm` on 9,000 of 9,000 masked records — 18 masked runs × 500, the right denominator (274's lesson)**.  **No `dm_*` key on any of the 1,500 `k01` records.**  So **280.4's null (i) — a mask that bit on `CARWD0` but on NO subset arm, which predicts EXACTLY `ALL-THREE-NEEDED` and would have forged the count account this batch exists to test — is excluded ON THE LIVE RECORDS, not assumed.**
* **THE CROSS-READ, AND ITS DECLARED LIMIT.**  Every run's records are read as its OWN arm's k and as every other k in the batch: **all 21 pass their own and all 21 refuse every other.**  **But `k` separates by COUNT only**, so `TWOWD0` / `CTL2WD0` (both k=2) and the three singles (all k=1) are mutually readable by the record audit alone — **280.4(iii)'s serious null, declared at registration and printed by the parser rather than hidden.**  **What refuses it is `G-WITNESS` and `G-SETSEP`**: all 21 runs printed exactly the witness rebuilt from the architecture, the **7 rebuilt witnesses are PAIRWISE DISTINCT**, and **no run carries another arm's registered witness (0 swaps)** — plus the proof job's RR4, where five of the six discriminations are SAME-k and all five passed on the real GPU path (280.6).
* **FOUR INDEPENDENT DERIVATIONS OF THE MASK SETS AGREE**: the registered `analysis/cwd4_design.py`; the launcher's guard 4/4h on the LIVE model; the RULE 20 ENV audit's **RE-TYPED** literals; and `analysis/cwd4_attack_indep.py`'s rebuild **from the architecture** importing no repo module — **62 tensors, 11,220,132 parameters**, the 20 `normscale` indices (2, 5, …, 59) and numel 4,800, **every 512-wide BN scale exactly {47, 50, 53, 56, 59} and the carrier-free ones exactly {47, 56} — TWO**, which is the whole reason the matched control exists at count 2 and cannot exist at count 3.  **The refute pass added a fifth, written by itself and agreeing.**  `TWOWD0` is confirmed a PROPER SUBSET of `CARWD0`; `CTL2WD0` is DISJOINT from it; the two count-2 arms are **numel-matched 1,024 = 1,024** and **both class-pure — every member a 1-dim BatchNorm SCALE, no shift**, which is precisely what `cdep1`'s `CTLWD0` could not be at count three (278 bound (5)).
* **The 6,002-byte `PARTITION-MANIFEST.txt` is rebuilt from the architecture and is byte-identical to the batch's own** (sha256 `db540cb4…`), and all 9 `PROVENANCE` keys equal the literals re-typed in the parser, the scorer's own sha included.
* **Other gates, all PASS:** `G-ARGS` 21/21; `G-ENV`; `G-WITNESS` (every kind, every run); `G-STRUCT`; `G-PROV` (MODE submit, `build_network.py` = `cvt8`'s `c7998883…`, `HF.py` = `cwd1`'s `PATCH_DECAYMASK` tree `94aedc33…`, `HF.py.pre_decaymask` = `cvt8`'s `5197dc2e…`, runner `34a8c90e…`, scorer, design, `cwd_design`, `cwd_common`); `G-HW` (disclosure only: **distinct devices `['NVIDIA L4']`**).

### 283.8 What this licenses, and what it does not — and the launch refuter's two obligations, answered

**OBLIGATION (a), DISCHARGED, AND VERIFIED HERE RATHER THAN TAKEN ON TRUST.**  The launch refuter's condition was that **if the stamp `CTL2-PARTIAL` fired, three registered licence paragraphs — `ANY-ONE-SUFFICES`, `TWO-SUFFICES` and `COUNT-GRADED`, each of which asserts in terms that the carrier-free pair *"stays at `k01`"* — could no longer be quoted verbatim, because a `PART` control is not at the floor.**  **IT DID NOT FIRE.**  Checked three ways by this entry: `CTL2WD0` **22.8547 ≤ 24.8213**, the `NULL` bar, so its state is `NULL`; the FINAL line carries **`CTL2-NULL`** inside the state word and **contains no `CTL2-PARTIAL` token** (grepped, count 0); and the independent parser's `[5]` re-derives the reachability over all **3⁵ = 243** state combinations, confirms *"the `CTL2-PARTIAL` stamp is present exactly when `CTL2WD0` is `PART`"*, lists the floor-clause accounts reachable with a non-floor control as exactly `{ANY-ONE-SUFFICES, TWO-SUFFICES}`, and prints **`QUOTE-OK`**.  **And the obligation is doubly moot**: the branch that actually fired, `ONE-SUFFICES-PARTIAL`, **asserts no floor clause at all**, so none of the three conditioned paragraphs is quoted anywhere in this landing.  **The matched pair's floor is therefore sourced NOT from a licence paragraph but from the state word, the `TWO-SPECIFIC` stamp and `P_CTL2` — as a bound.**

**OBLIGATION (b), CARRIED, NOT DISCHARGED.**  The launch refuter's second condition was that **the batch has NO power against the magnitude rival by construction, so no sentence may read its result as tensor identity.**  That is headline bound (2) and 283.4(2); `MAGNITUDE-NOT-SEPARATED` and `CTL-NOT-MAGNITUDE-MATCHED` are on the FINAL **unconditionally**; **no sentence in this entry, in MASTER-TABLE row 237 or in the write-up amendment says the effect is a property of these particular tensors' identity**; and the in-batch `|L|` re-derivation at 283.7 is recorded as **evidence FOR the rival, not against it**.  **`POSITION-CLASS-NOT-SEPARATED` travels with it.**

**LICENSED, at this cell only, in the scorer's registered words:** *"at this cell one named carrier scale's own decay suffices, and the effect is carrier-SPECIFIC WITHIN the three carriers — it is not a function of the number of masked scales alone."*  **Read "one named carrier scale" STRICTLY as the arms actually run** — `ONE59` (resolved `REC`), `ONE50` (`REC` by 0.40 SE, near-bar) and `ONE53` (`PART`, which does **not** suffice) — and read *"two matched non-carrier scales"* STRICTLY as **{47, 56}**, the one carrier-free class-pure pair that exists at that depth.  **It must not be paraphrased as "any single BN scale suffices" or "any matched non-carrier pair fails".**

**NOT LICENSED — every one of these must survive into any prose that uses the sentence:**

* **WHICH PROPERTY OF THE CARRIER DOES THE WORK.**  Not identity vs **TERM MAGNITUDE** (bound (2): no magnitude-matched carrier-free control can exist on this network — the carriers are mean-`|L|` ranks 1, 2, 3 of 62 in batch and the only admissible controls rank 33 and 38, a 140.1× gap at the closest pair).  Not identity vs **Kim et al.'s POSITION CLASS** (bound (4), now binding at count one as well as count two).  **What IS decided is COUNT**, and only that.
* **WHICH ROUTE.**  One switch removes the decay from the weight update and from the meta trace together.
* **AN ORDERING AMONG THE SINGLES AS AN EFFECT.**  `D_MAG` and `D_CLASS` are DESCRIPTIVE; three points on a 1.7× `|L|` range is not a dose–response curve.
* **A CLEAN MONOTONE LADDER.**  `ONE59` exceeds the carrier pair by +0.8853 pp = +1.68 SE, not resolved.
* **THAT `ONE53` IS CONVERGED.**  It is the one arm still visibly climbing at epoch 99 (283.7).
* **THE `CTL2WD0` READING AS A MEASUREMENT.**  It is a location at `k01`'s floor and a bound (283.6 **W1**, **W2**).
* **ANY OTHER CELL, network, WD value, decoupled decay, horizon beyond 100 epochs, momentum 0.9, WD on conv / linear weights, or anything about the LAYERWISE grouping** — every arm here is SCALAR and there is no layerwise arm, so **no scalar-vs-layerwise statement of any kind follows from this batch.**  `PlainNet` keeps its own separate one-tensor result (`cwd2`, 273).

*(The scorer's own NOT-LICENSED block records that the three carriers are the only tensors voting DOWN on **100 %** of the pinned records while `linear.weight` and `layer4.0.conv2.weight` vote UP on **100 %** of them — written here with ONE percent sign, because the registered file emits two and that is defect **F1**.)*

### 284.1 The gap, re-verified rather than inherited

281.12 reported it at registration and did not fix it (RULE 16).  It was re-run here before anything was written, on a
**nine-arm synthetic `cwd5` ladder** (the real run names, job ids and `ARGS` payload; `k01W1` / `kLW1` at `0.1`, six
rung arms at `1e-2` / `1e-3` / `5e-4`, and `CARW2`), against 269's module:

| listing of `CARW2` | 269's `check()` |
|---|---|
| its `ARGS_WD_BASE` witness | **FAIL** — `cwd5-CARW2-s146-5052150.out prints an ON DECAY_MASK line but is listed with a ARGS_WD_BASE witness` |
| its `DECAY_MASK` witness | **FAIL** — `cwd5-CARW2-s146-5052150.out deviates on ARGS_WD_BASE but is listed with a DECAY_MASK witness` |

Both messages are the ones 281.12 quoted, on a full batch rather than a single synthetic run, and both were reproduced
again on the REAL logs (284.7).  The asymmetry is the whole of it: the KINDS / completeness reader ends
`… and kd not in (multi_kind_of(fn) or {})`, an escape 245 built for two-kind runs; the ARGS-value reader (263) is
`if ent is not None: bad.append("%s deviates on %s but is listed with a %s witness")`, with no escape at all.

### 284.2 The rule, and why it is FORCED

**A run that deviates on an ARGS value AND prints an ON `<KIND>` line is listed with its ARGS witness, and every kind
it turns ON is registered in `MULTI_KIND`.**  It is not a preference between two workable listings:

* the ARGS listing is accepted **only because** the completeness reader has the `MULTI_KIND` escape — so the escape
  must be populated, and populating it is what makes the ON line VERIFIED rather than merely tolerated;
* the `<KIND>` listing cannot be made to pass without giving the ARGS-value reader an escape of its own, which would
  **weaken** it: that reader's whole job is to refuse a deviating row that is not listed by its value.  It is not
  given one, and C35a / the real-log control prove the reverse listing still FAILs.

**Why the escape cannot be abused.**  A kind registered in `MULTI_KIND` is then held to an exact line (`is registered
with %s ON but prints %r`), its batch's unlisted runs are held to that kind's `off` line, and an ON line of a kind NOT
registered there still FAILs (C35g, on a rung arm that has no entry).  So the entry buys expressiveness and pays for
it with three further checks.


**Independent agreement from the registered `cwd5` scorer, found after the rule was derived from the code.**
`analysis/cWD5_wdladder_score.py` — registered and sha-pinned before any run existed, and NOT edited here — already
prints, in its own "WHAT IT DOES NOT LICENSE" block: *"The 21 runs at a non-standard weight decay are ARGS-value
deviations and owe CORPUS-EXCLUSIONS rows of kind `ARGS_WD_BASE` at the landing"*.  **Twenty-one, not eighteen** —
`CARW2` included.  The scorer's parenthesis "(`corpus_exclusions.py` is NOT edited)" records the state at
registration, which 281.12 then qualified by owing this edit under its own number; it is not a prohibition, and the
kind it names is the one this entry makes expressible.  Two stages reached the same listing independently.

  (C36 pins the literal to that table; 284.7 pins it to the runs' own logs and to the RULE 20 ENV half's re-typed
  witnesses).  **An entry may now register ONE kind** — 245's register two or more — and that is the two-axis case.
* **`MULTI_KINDS_AT_251 = 2`**, the same device as 269's `KINDS_AT_251`: 245's `two-kind runs` COUNT and 251's
  `multi-kind runs` breakdown are computed over the entries registering two or more kinds, so **both stay
  byte-identical** as one-kind two-axis entries are added, and the two lines keep agreeing with each other (the count
  equals the sum of the breakdown — C36).  The one-kind entry is **verified** by the same loop; only the counters skip
  it, and it is counted on its own line.

  that each such run's ARGS witness IS its own `ARGS:` line's deviation and that each registered ON line IS the line
  the run prints — so the line's verdict is a statement, not a label.

  columns are EMPTY, by construction.

  ARGS-value reader has no escape by design; giving it one to express `ARGS_MOMENTUM_BASE` × `ARGS_WD_BASE` would
  weaken exactly the check that catches an unlisted deviating row.  `cwd5` has no such run (its only ARGS axis is the
  weight decay), test C26(d) already pins the current behaviour — such a row FAILs — and the fix is owed by the first
  batch that needs it, under its own number, as this one was.  **UNSURE** what the right shape is: a second witness
  column changes the TSV schema every reader loads, and that is a bigger decision than a code gap.
* **It fixes none of the RULE 16 defects reported by others** (269.8's two `cWD` selftest premises, 270.6 F1,
  271.6 F1 + F2, 272.6 F1 + F2, 273.6 F1 + F2, 278.6 D1, and the `cwd5` scorer defect Track B reported at 281), and

### 285.3 The numbers (in batch; every contrast WITHIN its rung)

`SIGMA_PRIOR_frozen` **0.645141** (in-batch 0.485817 was smaller, so the FROZEN PRIOR binds — `SIGMA-PRIOR-FROZEN`),
`SE_ARM_DIFF` **0.526756**, **2 SE = 1.053511 pp, the HALF-WIDTH of a ±2 SE interval and NOT a bound on any effect**
(278.6 C1).  Collapse bar at a rung = scalar ≤ 0.50 × **that rung's own** layerwise mean; `NOGAP` iff
layerwise − scalar < 10 pp; reference healthy iff layerwise ≥ 55.  **Both grains ran IN BATCH at every rung**
(`ALL-RUNGS-IN-BATCH`, `BOTH-GRAINS-AT-EVERY-RUNG`), so no gap is a cross-batch contrast.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**The layerwise ladder is nearly flat — 1.4127 pp of total spread across a 200× change in the weight decay — while

**GAP MONOTONICITY, re-derived here because the scorer did not print it** (see 285.6 F1).  The **SIGNED** gap

which reads as non-increasing as `wd` RISES — the opposite of the fact — and contradicts the direction reversal
stated three paragraphs above it)*.

**ANCHOR REPLICATION, non-gating.**  `k01W1` **23.2240** against `cwd3`'s landed `k01` 22.9853 → **+0.2387 pp**,

### 285.4 What bounds the result, led with

* **THE LADDER HAS FOUR POINTS** (`LADDER-IS-FOUR-POINTS`).  The threshold is a **BRACKETING PAIR**, 0.1 and 1e-2;
  nothing between two adjacent rungs was run.  **No finer localisation is licensed**, and the phrasings the refute
  pass struck are named so they are not written again: *"the collapse exists ONLY at 0.1"* (refute fix **W1**) and
  *"the collapse is a property of wd 0.1, not of scalar grouping"* (**W2**) are both **forbidden** — the first
  because it is a point localisation finer than the bracket and contradicts the scorer's own `NOT_FINER` clause, the
  second because it denies the grouping's role at the very rung where the **46.0700 pp within-rung gap IS the
  grouping contrast**.
* **EVERY `COLLAPSE` AND `NOGAP` READING IS A BOUND, NEVER A POINT EFFECT** (164.6; `FLOOR-READINGS-ARE-BOUNDS`).
  `G_W1` is a LOCATION: the scalar arm sits at its floor, so the gap's SIZE is where the arm landed, not a measured
  effect.  The three `NOGAP` readings are bounds in the other direction — *"below the 10 pp bar"*, **not** *"the two
  grains are equal"* and **not** *"the mechanism has no presence at 1e-2"* (refute fix **W3**: *"no presence"*
  asserts an absence of mechanism, which the registered `NOGAP` word does not license).
* **W2 IS NOT RESOLVED, AND MUST NOT BE POOLED WITH W3 AND W4** (refute fix **W5**).  At W3 and W4 the scalar arm is
  RESOLVED above its own layerwise arm (−7.90 SE, −8.59 SE, sign-consistent across all three seeds).  At W2 the same
  sign appears but is **NOT resolved** against the frozen prior: −1.0893 pp = −2.07 SE, ±2 SE **[−2.1428, −0.0358]**,
  an interval whose upper end is **0.04 pp from zero** — **DESCRIPTIVE / UNSURE**.  In all three cases the registered
  state word is `NOGAP`, a bound in the other direction, **not a claim that scalar wins**.
* **DECOUPLED WEIGHT DECAY IS NOT TESTED, IN EITHER DIRECTION** (`DECOUPLED-NOT-TESTED`; descoped with reasons at
  281.2).  The base optimiser has no decoupled path — `SGDm_base_update` multiplies the decay by the LEARNED step
  size in the weight update AND bakes `(1 − wd·a)` into the meta trace — and no single λ can match the coupled dose
  `wd·a` with `a` learned and clamped to `exp([−15, −2.3026])`.  **Nothing here may be written as "the collapse is a
  coupled-decay phenomenon".**
* **WHICH ROUTE the decay acts through is not separated.**  One flag changes both the weight shrink and the meta
  trace.
* **ONE network, ONE cell otherwise, ONE horizon, THREE seeds.**  `ResNet18_c100` / CIFAR-100, SGDm 0.99 + Lion
  0.99/0.9, ms 1e-3, α₀ 1e-6, 100 epochs, `AUGMENT=1`, `BETA_CLIP` −15:−2.3026.  Nothing about PlainNet, VGG,
  GroupNorm, other ResNet depths, other datasets, other meta step sizes, α₀, momenta, horizons, or groupings other
  than scalar and layerwise.
* **Three seeds resolve STATES against the 0.50 and 10 pp bars, not fine BETWEEN readings**; ±2 SE is a half-width,
  not a bound on any effect (278.6 C1).
* **Every reading is WITHIN this batch.**  The corpus disclosure line (3,088 rows) is DISCLOSURE ONLY — no bar,
  sigma, state, contrast, branch or stamp reads the corpus.  The between-batch block (`cwd3`, `cmo1`, the census
  layerwise mean) is frozen literals feeding one non-gating replication stamp.
* **UNSURE, and not guessed: WHY the scalar arm recovers so completely at 1e-2** rather than degrading gradually.
  The batch measures **that** it does; it does not measure why.  Nothing in the probe readout was examined for a
  mechanism and none should be quoted as one without its own registration.
* **`I am NOT reporting a critical weight-decay value.`**  Li–Zhou–Xu (arXiv:2607.21005) already own *"there is a
  critical weight decay for normalised training"* at the class grain (281.1).  The registered framing is that the
  campaign's cell sits **above the value at which this configuration breaks**, not that the campaign discovered a
  criticality.

**CARRIED OBLIGATIONS FROM `cwd4`'s LAUNCH REFUTER — both discharged here, VERIFIED BY ME rather than inherited.**
**(a)** `cwd4`'s FINAL reads `ONE-SUFFICES-PARTIAL | TWO-REC+CTL2-NULL+ONE50-REC+ONE53-PART+ONE59-REC | …`; `CTL2` is
**`NULL`**, and I confirmed by grep that the `CTL2-PARTIAL` stamp is **ABSENT from both committed scorer outputs**
(`results/cwd4_countwd_score_cluster_b.txt` and `_mac.txt`, 0 occurrences each; the 2 occurrences in
`results/cwd4_attack_indep_cluster_b.txt` are its own reachability-audit PASS lines, not a stamp).  **The floor clause
holds, so `cwd4`'s three licence paragraphs may be quoted verbatim.**  **(b)** `cwd4` carries
`MAGNITUDE-NOT-SEPARATED` and has **no power against the magnitude rival by construction**.  No sentence in this
entry reads any `cwd4` result as tensor identity, and `cwd5` says nothing about carriers at all.


### 285.5 The attack — a new independent parser that rebuilds all 401 lines

`analysis/cwd5_attack_indep.py` (77 KB, written for this landing).  **INDEPENDENCE, as designed**: it imports NOTHING

any other repo module — stdlib only (`hashlib`, `json`, `math`, `os`, `struct`, `sys`).  **No regular expression
anywhere**: `.out` lines are split on commas / colons / whitespace, the TSV on tabs, file names on hyphens.  Every
bar, sigma literal, rung token, witness string, tree sha and licence sentence is **RE-TYPED** from CORRECTIONS 281.
The `ResNet18_c100` tensor table is rebuilt **FROM THE ARCHITECTURE** (stem, four stages of two BasicBlocks, three
downsample shortcuts, linear head) and `CARW2`'s mask resolved against that rebuild **by NAME**.  float32 rounding is
re-derived through `struct`; the Lion natural step is recomputed from the records' own `beta_pre` / `mom_pre` /
`z_agg` on each arm's own group count.

**RESULT: 401 rebuilt vs 401 in the log, 398 matched VERBATIM, 3 matched host-independently** (the 2 path echoes by
suffix, the corpus count re-filtered by hand), **0 MISMATCHES**; the FINAL rebuilt **token by token**; **VIOLATIONS 0**
over 18 independent PASS checks.  Its own stdout is **BYTE-IDENTICAL on both hosts** — 121 lines, `b78c4254…`.

**RULE 16 DEFECT F1 (`cwd5`), NEW, REPORTED AND NOT FIXED.**  `analysis/cWD5_wdladder_score.py` guards its
DESCRIPTIVE gap-monotonicity stamp with

```
    if word and "UNREADABLE" not in (word or "") and branch in ACCOUNT_TOKENS:
```

The substring test was plainly meant to catch a **RUNG** state of `UNREADABLE`.  But a rung is `UNREADABLE` exactly
when its layerwise arm is below `REF_MIN`, and `decide()` returns `UNRESOLVED-REFERENCE` in that case, which is
**NOT** in `ACCOUNT_TOKENS` — so **the rung reading of the test is DEAD CODE**, and the only string that can ever trip
it is the CARRIER word `CAR-UNREADABLE`.  Measured on this batch rather than inferred: `G` =
[+46.0700, −1.0893, −4.1607, −4.5267] is monotone non-increasing within 2 SE at every step, so
**`GAP-MONOTONE-IN-WD` would have fired — and it is SUPPRESSED, because rung W2 did not collapse and the carrier
companion is void.**  Gap monotonicity and carrier readability are unrelated facts, and one is silencing the other.
Verified by me: `GAP-MONOTONE-IN-WD` and `GAP-NOT-MONOTONE-IN-WD` each appear **0 times** in the committed output.
**COSMETIC IN SCOPE**: the clause appends a descriptive stamp only; no bar, sigma, level, contrast, rung state,
carrier word, branch or licence paragraph reads it, and the FINAL's account token (`THRESHOLD-W1-W2`) is unchanged
either way.  **The registered scorer was NOT edited** (RULE 16); the independent parser RE-TYPES the clause as
written and reproduces the bytes the scorer actually emits — which is why the 0-mismatch claim is honest rather than
flattering — following `cwd4`'s precedent (283.6 F1) of reproducing a defect rather than quietly correcting it.
**The eight older open defects stand; this entry creates no other and fixes none.**


### 285.7 THE AREA CHAIR'S QUESTION, ANSWERED IN ONE PARAGRAPH — **IS THE COLLAPSE A HAZARD OR A CORNER CASE?**

**On this evidence: a CORNER CASE, and the answer is not close.**  At the campaign's own coupled weight decay 0.1 the
scalar arm sits at 23.2240 against its in-batch layerwise 69.2940 — a 46.0700 pp within-rung gap, 87.46 SE, with the
scalar run reaching only 23.17 % TRAIN, i.e. it never learns; drop the decay one decade to 1e-2 and the scalar arm is
at 69.3513, **35.2203 pp above that rung's collapse bar**, and at 1e-3 and 5e-4 it is 38.33 and 38.47 pp above theirs
and is in fact slightly *higher* than its own layerwise arm (`G_W3` −4.1607 pp = −7.90 SE, `G_W4` −4.5267 pp =
−8.59 SE, sign-consistent across all three seeds).  **A practitioner running the standard CIFAR recipe's 5e-4 will
never meet this failure**, so it cannot be written as a hazard of shared step sizes, of BatchNorm, or of MetaOptimize;
the referee's *"corner-case configuration"* charge **LANDS**, and the campaign must say so in the first sentence of
any subsection it writes.  **What the answer is NOT.**  It is not a licence to call the collapse an artefact of a
mistaken setting: wd 0.1 is the **parent's own value**, the whole mechanism line and `cwd1`/`cwd3`/`cwd4` were run
there deliberately, and the audit's own most dramatic scalar row sits at that same decay — so the finding's real force
is that it **protects the audit's scalar arm by naming the configuration it is measured in**, which is exactly the
diagnostic framing §10 of `WRITEUP-mechanism` had already adopted for other reasons.  And it is **not a located
threshold**: with FOUR rungs the campaign can **BRACKET** the transition between 1e-2 and 0.1 and can do nothing
else — *"the collapse is present at 0.1 and absent at 1e-2"* is the whole of what may be said, and **no value inside
that unrun decade may be named, in the paper or anywhere** (`LADDER-IS-FOUR-POINTS`).  **And it is not a statement
about grouping alone or decay alone**: at 0.1 the grain matters enormously — layerwise is healthy at 69.2940 while
scalar sits at 23.2240 — and at 1e-2 and below neither grain reaches the collapse bar, so what the ladder identifies
is the **CONJUNCTION** of scalar grouping with a coupled weight decay at or near 0.1, and neither factor alone.

**Why the outcome is publishable rather than fatal, stated as a judgement and labelled as one.**  Every outcome of
this ladder was registered as publishable before any run existed (O-14's own row says so), and this one converts an
*assertion* the campaign could not defend — *"the scalar arm is a granularity measurement"* — into a *measured
qualification* it can: the scalar arm is a granularity measurement **at weight decays below ~1e-2, and at 0.1 it is
measuring a broken configuration**.  The subsection loses its claim to generality and gains a bound; the audit's
headline (the denominator result plus the count-matched partition audit) does not move at all.  **UNSURE, and it is
the professor's call, not mine**: whether a referee will read a bounded corner-case diagnostic as worth three-quarters
of a page, or as a reason to cut the subsection entirely.  §8 Q1 is where that question lives.


### 285.8 What this licenses, and what it does not

**The sentence the registration licenses, verbatim, at this cell:**

> *"the shared-step-size collapse at this cell requires a coupled weight decay within a decade of 0.1; at 1e-2 and
> below the two grains do not differ by the collapse bar."*

Its registered consequence, also written before any run existed: **this is the referee's corner-case charge landing.
The mechanism line must be written as a diagnostic of ONE extreme configuration, and the audit's scalar cells must be
reported with the disclosure that they sit at a weight decay roughly 200× the standard value, at which the scalar
configuration is broken.  The honest framing is that the subsection PROTECTS the audit's scalar arm by naming the
configuration, not that it explains a general granularity effect.**

**`CARW2` IS UNREADABLE, AND THIS ENTRY SAYS SO PLAINLY RATHER THAN READING IT.**  The carrier companion at rung W2
was pre-registered to be read **ONLY** if that rung is in the `COLLAPSE` state.  W2 is `NOGAP`.  There is therefore no
collapse for the carrier mask to remove, and **NOTHING about the carrier account is licensed at 1e-2 — not that it
holds, not that it fails.**  `CARW2` **71.8327** is printed as a level and nothing is read from it; `P_CARW2` and
`D_CARW2` were never computed.  This is `cmo1`'s `ISO-UNREADABLE` at wd 0 (CORRECTIONS 264) repeating one rung higher,
and `CAR-UNREADABLE` was named as a reachable outcome **before any run** — it is not a disappointment discovered
afterwards.  **The mask DID bite** (`dm_wdterm` positive on all 1,500 masked records, `MASK-UPDATE-AND-TRACE`
stamped), so this is a **design-scope limit and not a patch failure**; the carrier gate passing is exactly what tells
the two apart.  **A fact about the design worth recording for whoever designs the follow-up**: a carrier companion is
only readable at a rung that still collapses, and the only such rung is the anchor, where `cwd3` and `cwd4` have
already landed it twice.  Siting the companion at W2 and the threshold at W1–W2 were bound to collide.

**On `cmo1`'s two endpoints.**  The wd-0 endpoint (`W0k01` 71.56) and the four `cwd5` rungs are now consistent with a
single picture — **the scalar arm is healthy everywhere except at 0.1**.  `cmo1` fixed the endpoints between batch;
`cwd5` fills the interval **in batch, both grains at every rung**.

**NOT licensed**: decoupled weight decay in either direction; any threshold finer than the bracketing pair; any other
network, dataset, meta step size, α₀, momentum, horizon or grouping; the carrier account at any rung other than W2;
which ROUTE the decay acts through; anything about the corpus's landed cells.

### 289.2 (A) The realised per-step shrink α·κ (1.5a)

The harness's base update is `delta = a*(m + wd*w)`, so one step multiplies w by (1 − a·wd), a = exp(β) the learned
step size; no momentum amplification.  Peaks are per seed; κ = `--weight-decay-base`.

| arm | κ | state | peak a·κ per seed (epoch) | ep 10-15 median | ep 15-20 median |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cwd5` `k01W1` | 0.1 | COLLAPSED | **5.53e-4 / 5.56e-4 / 5.45e-4** (17.4 / 17.4 / 17.2) | 4.94e-5 | 3.03e-4 |
| `cwd5` `k01W2` | 1e-2 | healthy | median 1.64e-4 | | |
| `cwd5` `k01W3` | 1e-3 | healthy | median 3.37e-5 | | |
| `cwd5` `k01W4` | 5e-4 | healthy | 2.43e-5 / 2.40e-5 / 2.50e-5 (89.6 / 62.4 / 73.6) | | |
| `cmo1` `k01` / `M9k01` | 0.1 | COLLAPSED | medians 5.50e-4 / 5.45e-4 | | |
| `ctd1` `sc` | 0.1 | COLLAPSED | median 5.45e-4 | | |
| **`cct1` `k01` (CIFAR-10)** | 0.1 | **healthy** | **4.67e-4 / 4.72e-4 / 4.86e-4** (17.2 / 17.0 / 17.2) | | |
| `cau1` `m6` / `m6t` (AdamW base, CIFAR-10) | 0.1 | healthy | medians 4.99e-5 / 3.00e-5 | | |

* **Against standard recipes** (lr·wd at peak lr; the sources are the local arXiv texts the script cites, re-checked by
  grep at the cited lines this cycle; the ResNet-20 column parse and its μ 0.9 stay **UNSURE**, as the script says):
  the largest small-batch raw shrink is 1.00e-4 (AdamW lr 1e-3, wd 0.1); the largest small-batch momentum-amplified
  one is 5.00e-4 (e.g. CIFAR SGD lr 0.1, wd 5e-4, μ 0.9: lr·wd/(1−μ)); large-batch amplified reaches 4.8e-3.  The collapse's
  peak dose is **+1.74 log10 above PyTorch's AdamW default, +0.74 above the largest small-batch raw recipe, +0.04 above
  the largest small-batch amplified one, −0.94 below the large-batch amplified maximum.**  Whether the harness's
  un-amplified a·κ should be compared with a recipe's raw or amplified shrink is **UNSURE**; both are printed.
* **Time-matched** at `k01W1`'s own peak record (same seed, same step): s148 at step 8,600, β = −5.212 in every rung,
  W1 5.45e-4 vs W4 2.72e-6 — ×200, exactly κ's ratio at equal β (on s146/s147 W1 has already turned by its peak
  record, 5.53e-4 vs 3.01e-6).
* **The dose is not sufficient on its own:** `cct1` `k01` carries the same peak dose (4.7e-4) on CIFAR-10 and does not
  collapse.  The AdamW CIFAR-10 cells (`cau1`) run an order of magnitude lower (3-5e-5) than the collapsing SGDm cells,
  so "κ 0.1 on SGDm" and "κ 0.1 on AdamW" are **not the same dose** — the question 1.5a asked.

### 289.3 (B0) THE REGISTERED LEAD-LAG TEST IS BIASED TOWARD "LAG" BY CONSTRUCTION — a finding about the test

`DOM_C` (256.3) is true on a record only if `sign(Σ_C L) == s`, the APPLIED shared sign, **and** |Σ_C L| > Σ_rest |L|.
Through the saturated early climb the applied sign is s = −1 (the vote pushes β up) on every record, while from
~5,000 steps on the carriers' summed term is positive (they push β down).  On those records `DOM_C` is false by
definition, whatever the carriers' magnitude, so it can only become true after s flips — i.e. after the very turn it is
being timed against.  The counts (39 unmasked COLLAPSED scalar runs, every quotable batch; TURN = first record with
s = +1):

* **3,392 pre-TURN records; s = −1 on all 3,392; the carriers oppose s on 1,361; `DOM_C` is even ADMISSIBLE (the
  carriers' sign equals s) on 2,031, and the last admissible record is at step 4,800-5,300** — from step 4,900-5,400 to
  the TURN (8,600-8,700) the carriers oppose s on **every** record.  `DOM_C` true pre-TURN: **0**.
* Healthy runs (42): 3,875 pre-TURN records, `DOM_C` true on 0 — the statistic is silent before the turn in both classes.

So section B's "pre-EXIT(0.1) `DOM_C` share 0.000" and its LAG column (`Dc` − EXIT(0.1) = +100..+500 steps; first
`DOM_C` record 8,900-9,200) are **near-guaranteed by the definition and carry no information about cause.**  The registered
definition is kept unchanged (RULE 16); the output now says so at the point of use.

**What is NOT an artefact.** The sign-FREE analogue MAG_C = |Σ_C L| > Σ_rest |L| (descriptive, not registered) is
also true on **0** pre-TURN records and first holds **+200..+500 steps after** the TURN on all 39 runs.  So even with
the sign clause removed, the carriers' magnitude does not exceed the rest's before the turn.  At the turn itself the
carriers ARE pivotal in the weaker net-sum sense: B2's PIV (the carriers set s against the rest's NET sum) equals the
down-vote rate on every turn-window record of the collapsing runs (0.605 / 0.605 at 8,500-9,000 steps), while in the
masked healthy arms the turn comes from the rest (Rdn ≈ sdn, carriers' share ≤ 0.002).  That is the strongest pro-C1
fact here, and it is about who tips the TURN, not about what starts the collapse.

### 289.4 (B1) THE FAIR EVENT: same-seed divergence from a healthy partner

The earlier B1 event "FALL" (first epoch after the TEST maximum with TEST < 0.9·max) is **undefined on 39 / 39** collapsed
runs — they never fall; they climb slowly and plateau near 23 % — and is **dropped**.  The collapse is a failure to
learn, so its accuracy onset is when the collapsing arm starts to trail a same-seed arm that differs only in κ or in
the decay mask.  GAP(e) = TEST_partner − TEST_collapsing at epoch e (ends at step 500·(e+1)); G_t = first epoch with
GAP ≥ t that stays ≥ t through epoch 49.  Pooled over ONE partner per collapsing run (`cwd5` W1 vs W4; `cmo1` k01 vs
W0k01; `cwd3` k01 vs CARWD0; `cwd4` k01 vs CARWD0; `cwd1` k01 vs k01NWD; 15 pairs):

| t (pp) | G_t end-step | G_t − TURN | before TURN | before first `DOM_C` record | a·κ of the collapsing arm at G_t |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **0.5** | 7,000-8,000 | **−1,700..−700** | **15 / 15** | **15 / 15** (by 1,100-2,100) | 1.10e-4 .. 2.99e-4 |
| **1** | 8,000-9,000 | −700..+300 | 14 / 15 | 14 / 15 (one tie) | |
| 2 | 8,500-9,000 | −200..+300 | 11 / 15 | 12 / 15 | |
| 5 | 9,500-10,000 | +800..+1,300 | 0 / 15 | 0 / 15 | |

* **β is identical across the pair until the divergence**: BDIV (|Δβ| > 1e-3 nat beyond the step-0 offset) is at
  8,600-8,700, at or one record before the TURN; G_0.5 precedes it on 15 / 15.  So the early accuracy deficit cannot come
  from the vote or from β; it comes from the decay term acting on the weights at the same learned α.
* **`cwd5` W1 vs W4 (the verifier's pair) reproduces exactly:** GAP 0.7 / 0.8 / 0.7 pp at epoch 14; G_0.5 at epoch 14 on
  all three seeds (step 7,500, a·κ 1.81e-4); G_2 at epoch 16 (step 8,500, a·κ 4.93e-4) on all three; TURN 8,700 ×3;
  first `DOM_C` 9,200 / 9,000 / 9,000.
* **Null** (12 same-seed pairs of two HEALTHY arms: `cwd5` W2/W3 vs W4, `cwd3` CARWD0 vs NWD, `cwd4` CARWD0 vs TWOWD0):
  max |GAP| over epochs 0-16 is **0.19-1.30 pp**, and **no null pair sustains 0.5 pp before epoch 41**.  So a single-epoch
  touch of 0.5-1 pp is within the null; the SUSTAINED crossing is what separates, which is why G_t, not the touch g_t,
  is the pooled event.  (The null pairs are not matched in κ-difference to the test pairs; this is orientation, not a
  registered floor.)
* **SHARE_C before the turn (B1b).** The collapsing arm's carrier share rises steadily through the climb — run medians
  0.002-0.003 (5.0-5.5k steps) → 0.057-0.060 (6.5-7.0k) → 0.174-0.184 (7.5-8.0k) → 0.283-0.306 (8.0-8.5k); first record
  ≥ 0.05 at 6,600-6,700, ≥ 0.10 at 7,100-7,200, ≥ 0.25 at 8,100, ≥ 0.50 only at 9,000-9,200 (after the TURN) — against
  ≤ 0.001-0.003 for W4 (verifier's 7,000-8,500 figure: W1 0.174-0.184 vs W4 0.0006; a one-off spot-check gives W4
  0.00059 / 0.00064 / 0.00061).  In these pairs the carriers' term is largely their own decay term, so the rise is the
  dose seen through the vote, not an independent lead indicator: it grows alongside the accuracy gap and cannot order
  them.

### 289.5 (C) N_eff — the plan's 1.8 soft gate is met

Early N_eff (epochs [1,5), run medians): `cwd5` W1 **3.21 / 3.09 / 3.50** vs W4 **3.17 / 3.05 / 3.47** (same seeds) —
**overlaps**; every paired cell (wd rungs, `cmo1` wd 0 vs 0.1, the three mask pairs, CIFAR-100 vs CIFAR-10) overlaps in
the early window, and separates only from epochs 10-15, when the dose is already large.  Over all 171 scalar runs with
per-tensor records the best single cut misclassifies **47 / 171** against a base rate of 53 / 171 (ResNet18_c100: 36 / 87).
`docs/ICML-PLAN.md` Phase 0 stated: "If early N_eff does not separate collapsing from healthy runs, the diagnostic
contribution (1.8) is dead."  **It does not separate; 1.8's early-diagnostic form is dead** (a late N_eff is not a
prediction, and is not claimed).

### 289.6 What this does to C1 — how strongly

* **Unsupported, not refuted.** No run here intervenes on the vote while holding the dose, so capture is not shown to be
  irrelevant.  But every observational ordering available puts the decay's effect on accuracy **first**: 0.5 pp
  sustained, 700-1,700 steps before the TURN and 1,100-2,100 before the first `DOM_C` record, on 15 / 15 pairs, with β
  identical in both arms.  On ICML-PLAN 1.19's own stated rule ("if capture LAGS the collapse, it is a symptom and C1's
  causal framing dies") the causal framing **dies as a cause-first claim**.  Verdict: **UNSURE, leaning against** C1's
  thesis sentence "a few normalisation gains capture that vote and collapse training".
* **What survives, descriptively:** decay dose → early accuracy deficit → a carrier-PIVOTAL turn (net-sum sense) → vote
  capture (`DOM_C`, then MAG_C) → β driven to the −15 floor (FLOOR 18,500-18,600) → the plateau.  Capture may be the
  LOCK-IN stage (the floor freezes learning), which is a mechanism claim about the terminal state, not about onset.
  The same dose on CIFAR-10 (`cct1`) does not collapse, so "dose alone" is not a sufficient story either.
* **What would decide it** (not registered; UNSURE which is cheapest): an intervention that holds the vote while the dose
  runs — e.g. the existing `BETA_HOLD` patch (237) replaying the healthy partner's β on the κ 0.1 scalar arm — asks
  whether the collapse still happens when the turn cannot occur.
* **Gate consequence** (recorded in `docs/ICML-PLAN.md` §4): the gate's Step 0 clause ("Step 0's lead-lag does not show
  capture lagging the collapse") is **NOT MET** on the fair event, and the registered `DOM_C` lead-lag is declared
  uninformative.  Autopilot decision: C1 cannot continue as a causal "vote capture" paper on the Phase 1 gate; Step 1
  (the standard-recipe cell, Track 1's registration) still decides "hazard vs corner case" for C2/C4 and for a
  re-scoped, descriptive C1, and nothing in this entry edits Track 1's design.

### 290.1 PRIOR ART, CHECKED BEFORE THE REDESIGN WAS FIXED (the standing rule)

*External (web search, 2026-09-22; titles and abstracts only, nothing downloaded, no `.pdf` fetched).*
- **Loshchilov & Hutter, arXiv:1711.05101** — AdamW's decay term is multiplied by the schedule multiplier η_t, **not** by the step size α; that is what "decoupled" means there.  The harness's decay, `a·(step + wd·w)` with `a` the LEARNED step size, has torch.optim.AdamW's `lr·wd` form, not theirs.  Used for V3 (290.2).
- **Wang & Aitchison, arXiv:2405.13698**, and **Kosson et al., arXiv:2305.17212** — the per-step shrink `lr·wd` (timescale `1/(lr·wd)`) and the resulting weight-norm / rotational equilibrium are what weight decay actually sets in AdamW-type updates.  This is why `caw2` reports the realised `a·wd` per arm instead of comparing nominal wd values across bases (290.7).
- A search for a tested "shared learned step size collapses under weight decay, scalar vs per-layer, by base / meta optimiser" found **nothing that runs this contrast**; the nearest hit is the parent itself (arXiv:2402.02342).  Not a novelty claim: a statement that no external result pre-decides any cell.

*Internal (the campaign's own landed cells, `results/all_runs.csv`, CIFAR-10 ResNet18, wd 0.1, α0 1e-6, meta step 1e-3; ARGS lines read on cluster_b).*  AdamW+Adam scalar **never** collapsed (`a0-scal-1e6` 91.66 / 91.47 / 91.76; `g2_mAdam_scal` 91.77 / 91.49 / 91.46); AdamW+Lion scalar **never** collapsed (`g1_adamw_scal` 91.75 / 91.65 / 91.45); **SGDm+Adam scalar collapsed on HALF its seeds** (`g3_sgdmAdam_scal` 88.16 / **18.33** / **20.48**; `g4-sgdmAdam-scal` 87.83 / **20.69** / 86.61).  This is the basis of the registered prediction (290.7) and the reason SPLIT is expected, not feared, in cell M.  `caw2`'s selftest proves AS / MS / LS carry those landed runs' optimiser flags flag for flag (only dataset / network / seed differ), and K01 carries the landed `cwd5` k01W1's.

### 290.2 THE HARNESS's DECAY AND AdamW, READ — and the V3 correction

`$WS/harness_cwd1/cifar10/Optimizers/HF.py` (94aedc33…, cwd1's tree, unchanged):
```
SGDm_base_update:  delta = a * (m + wd * w)                        (m the (1 - mp)-normalised momentum)
AdamW_base_update: lambda_t *= b2 ; mu = (1 - b2) / (1 - lambda_t)
                   m <- b1 * m + g   (UNNORMALISED sum) ;  v <- b2 * v + g**2
                   delta = a * ( m / sqrt(mu * v + eps) + wd * w )
both:              w <- w - delta ;  h <- gamma * (1 - wd * a) * h - delta
```
In both bases the decay is multiplied by the learned step size `a`: the per-step shrink is `a·wd` ("α-scaled", 292's name).  **V3, corrected here:** `caw1_design.py`'s docstring called this "decoupled in Loshchilov & Hutter's sense"; that is wrong — L&H's decay is scaled by η_t, not α (293 fixed the same error in the naming paragraph).  `caw1_design.py` is registered and is **not** edited; `caw2_design.py` states the correct reading and `caw2`'s selftest checks that it does.  The unnormalised `m` makes the harness's AdamW gradient step up to `1/(1-b1)` = 10× torch.optim.AdamW's at the same `a` (steady state, correlated gradients; ≈ 2.3× for pure noise) — the reason for the X cell (290.5).  The proof job re-verifies every one of these formulas bitwise (290.6).

### 290.3 `caw1` — WITHDRAWN BEFORE LAUNCH

### 290.4 THE DOM_C GATE WORD, AND WHAT IT IS NOT

`DOM_C` (256 / ICML-PLAN §4): per scalar record, `L_i` = tensor i's term of the applied meta momentum (Adam: `b1/(1-b1)·m_tensor_i + z_i`; Lion: `b2·m_tensor_i + (1-b2)·z_i`), `s` = the harness's applied sign; `DOM_C ⇔ sign(Σ_C L_i) = s ∧ |Σ_C L_i| > Σ_{i∉C}|L_i|`.  C is the top-3 by signed contribution on seed 160's records, and DOM_C is scored on 161 + 162 only.  Calibrated on landed `cwd5` (selftest B, on cluster_b): k01W1 C = {50,53,59}, DOM_C 0.8090; the non-collapsed k01W2/W3/W4 0.091 / 0.167 / 0.174.  The meta alg of the vote is the ARM's (an AdamW+Lion arm is decomposed as Lion); selftest B shows Lion-shaped records fail the Adam algebra and vice versa.  **Read only on cell A** (the standard recipe): GATE-FIRES-A iff A COLLAPSE ∧ DOM_C(AS) ≥ 0.50 ∧ DOM_C(K01) ≥ 0.50.  **This is the Step-1 half only.**  CORRECTIONS 289 (Step 0) found the registered lead-lag half biased toward "lag" by construction and C1's causal vote-capture framing unsupported (UNSURE, leaning against): the gate word may therefore **not** be combined with a lead-lag reading as 292 planned, and `LEADLAG-NOT-READ` is stamped on every FINAL.

### 290.5 THE DESIGN, AND WHY 9 ARMS

The cell is `cwd5`'s byte for byte (ResNet18_c100 / CIFAR-100, 100 epochs, batch 100, AUGMENT=1, BETA_CLIP −15:−2.3026, meta step 1e-3, α0 1e-6, γ 1, PROBE=100, PROBE_TENSOR=1, cwd1's tree + runner unchanged, every patch off).

| cell | arms | base | meta | wd | role |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| K | K01 (scalar) | SGDm(0.99) | Lion(0.99, 0.9) | 0.1 | positive control (landed 4× at 22.79–23.22) |
| M | MS \| ML | SGDm(0.99) | Adam(0.9, 0.999) | 0.1 | the META swap alone (base flags == K01's) |
| L | LS \| LL | AdamW(0.9, 0.999) | Lion(0.99, 0.9) | 0.1 | the BASE swap alone (meta flags == K01's) |
| A | AS \| AL | AdamW(0.9, 0.999) | Adam(0.9, 0.999) | 0.1 | the STANDARD RECIPE (both swaps) |
| X | XS \| XL | AdamW(0.9, 0.999) | Adam(0.9, 0.999) | **1.0** | the DOSE arm: A at 10× the decay |

**Why X at 1.0.**  harness AdamW(a, wd) ≈ torch.optim.AdamW(lr ≈ a/(1-b1), wd·(1-b1)) in steady state, so harness wd 1.0 restores torch's decay-to-gradient ratio at wd 0.1 at the upper (correlated-gradient) end of the mapping; at the pure-noise end the factor is ≈ 2.3×.  1.0 is therefore the value that makes a NO-COLLAPSE at A unambiguous if X also does not collapse *and* X's realised shrink reaches the control's.  **Dropped, with reasons:** caw1's wd-1e-2 AdamW cell (a smaller dose than A's; predicted no-collapse under every account this batch separates; its ~4.1 GPU-h bought the X cell); a K layerwise arm (the control only has to reproduce the collapse, and its wd-0.1 layerwise reference has landed at 69.05 (`cmo1` kL) and 69.29 (`cwd5` kLW1), 3-seed means in `results/all_runs.csv`).  **A prose slip in the registered design, recorded here and not edited (RULE 16):** `caw2_design.py`'s docstring says that reference "has landed four times (67.9-69.3)"; those four numbers are `cwd5`'s layerwise arms at FOUR decays, not four landings at 0.1.  No gate, bar or branch reads the sentence; more seeds (3, as every cwd batch; SPLIT is a registered state).  **Budget:** 27 × 0.6855 GPU-h (cwd5's sacct mean on L4) ≈ **18.5 GPU-h expected** (the AdamW base is untimed at this cell: UNSURE ± 20 %), inside the ~20 GPU-h ceiling; hard bound 27 × 3 h = 81 GPU-h.  **Seeds:** {160,161,162} from the block 160..165 (cgw1 holds 152..159; caw1 held 149..151): 0 corpus rows, 0 `.out` ARGS lines on cluster_b and 0 sacct jobs carried any of 160..165 (launcher guards 2d / 2e, selftest C).
